## Cloud Tasks — `google.cloud.tasks.v2`

**Backing component:** none — implemented by CloudBurrow. No official emulator exists and no
viable community implementation was found (#24).

**It runs in the CLI process, not the cluster**, since there is no upstream workload to
deploy. Its dispatch targets are therefore addresses reachable from the host. There is **no
emulator environment variable** in any official client, so the endpoint and insecure
credentials must be passed explicitly in client options — see `test/compat/tasks_test.go`
for the exact form.
Contract: `google/cloud/tasks/v2/cloudtasks.proto`.
**No emulator environment variable exists.** Callers must set an explicit endpoint and
disable authentication in client options. This is a documented ergonomic limit.

### Control plane

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateQueue` | **Verified** | `TestTasksQueueLifecycle`, via the official `cloudtasks/apiv2` client. Contract defaults are returned, each `retry_config` and `rate_limits` field defaulting on its own: before #692 a queue given only `max_dispatches_per_second` had it replaced by the default. |
| `GetQueue` | **Verified** | `TestTasksQueueLifecycle`, including `NotFound` for an absent queue. |
| `ListQueues` | **Verified** | `TestTasksListQueues`; pagination covered by unit tests. A **`filter` on `state`** (`:`, `=` or `!=` `RUNNING`, `PAUSED` or `DISABLED`; Google's sample is `state: PAUSED`) is honoured (`TestTasksListQueuesFiltersByState`, #1222). Since #1255 a filter on **any Queue field** is honoured, as the reference documents (`TestTasksListQueuesFiltersOnQueueFields`): a dotted path in snake_case or lowerCamelCase (`rate_limits.max_dispatches_per_second`, `retryConfig.maxAttempts`) ending on a string, number, enum, `Duration` (`90s`) or `Timestamp` (RFC 3339, quoted), with `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` and `:` (a case-insensitive substring on a string, `FIELD:*` for set), combined with `AND` (or a space), `OR` and `NOT` (or `-`), with parentheses; an enum takes `=`, `!=` and `:` only. A path that is no Queue field, or a value its field cannot hold, is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`** (Google's wording not measured); a regular expression (`=~`) is **`UNIMPLEMENTED`** rather than ignored, which would return every queue (`TestTasksRefusesWhatItWouldDrop`, #578). The console's queue list has a filter box evaluated by the same code (`TestConsoleQueueListFilter`). |
| `retry_config.max_retry_duration` | **Verified** | Stored, returned, and **honoured**: a task is retried until both it and `max_attempts` are exhausted, measured from its first attempt, as `RetryConfig` documents (`TestTasksRefusesWhatItWouldDrop`, unit `TestMaxRetryDurationExtendsRetryingUntilBothLimitsAreReached`, #578). |
| `stackdriver_logging_config` | **Verified** | `TestTasksStackdriverLoggingConfig` (#1256), through `cloud.google.com/go/cloudtasks/apiv2` and `cloud.google.com/go/logging/logadmin`: `sampling_ratio` is kept and returned by `CreateQueue`, `GetQueue` and an `UpdateQueue` whose mask names `stackdriver_logging_config` (or `.sampling_ratio`); a mask naming it with no config clears it, and a ratio outside 0.0 to 1.0 is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**. When the instance serves Cloud Logging, that fraction of dispatch attempts (every one at 1.0, none at 0, the default) is written through the instance's own `WriteLogEntries`, as Cloud Tasks writes it (docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/logging): log `cloudtasks.googleapis.com/task_operations_log`, monitored resource `cloud_tasks_queue` with `project_id`, `location`, `queue_id` and `target_type` (`HTTP`), severity `INFO` for an `OK` attempt and `ERROR` otherwise, and a jsonPayload of `@type` `type.googleapis.com/google.cloud.tasks.logging.v1.TaskActivityLog`, `task` and `attemptResponseLog` (`attemptDuration`, `dispatchCount`, `responseCount`, `maxAttempts`, `scheduleTime`, `status` as a `google.rpc.Code` name converted from the HTTP status, `UNAVAILABLE` or `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` with no response, `targetAddress` as `METHOD URL`, `targetType`, and `retryTime` when the task will be retried); read back with `ListLogEntries`. The console sets it on Edit queue and shows it on the queue's page (`TestConsoleTasksLoggingSampling`). **What differs:** Google documents the log, the resource and the sampling, not the payload field by field: its fields are those of entries Google wrote, and their exact value formats are UNVERIFIED. Only attempts are logged, not `CreateTask` or `DeleteTask`. Without Cloud Logging on the instance the config is kept and nothing is written. Attempts are also in the console's operations ledger and `/admin/events`. |
| `http_target` (queue-level routing) | **Verified** | `TestTasksQueueHTTPTarget` (#1282), through the official client: `CreateQueue`, `GetQueue` and `UpdateQueue` (mask `http_target`) keep and return it, and it is applied to each dispatch attempt of the queue's HTTP tasks, from the queue as it is at that attempt. `uri_override` replaces the scheme, host, port (0 clears it), path and query it names, for every task in `ALWAYS` mode (the default) and only for a task with no URL in `IF_NOT_EXISTS` mode; a task may be created with no URL on a queue whose override names a host. `http_method` replaces the task's (a `GET`, `HEAD`, `DELETE` or `OPTIONS` override drops the body), `header_overrides` replace the task's headers of the same name, and `oidc_token` / `oauth_token` replace its token, minted locally as for a task's own. The stored task keeps its own `httpRequest` (UNVERIFIED that Google does not rewrite it). An empty host, a port outside 0 to 65535, a header with no key or a token with no service account is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. |
| `app_engine_routing_override` | **Not supported, refused** | **`UNIMPLEMENTED`** naming the field when it is set, on `CreateQueue` and `UpdateQueue` (#692): App Engine targets are not supported. Before, `CreateQueue` accepted and dropped it. |
| `DeleteQueue` | **Verified** | Removes the queue's tasks too, so a recreated queue cannot inherit them. |
| `UpdateQueue` | **Verified** | `TestTasksUpdateQueue` (#692), via the official client: a mask of `retry_config.max_attempts` and `rate_limits` changes those and keeps the rest (`min_backoff` stays), and `GetQueue` reads them back; `gcloud tasks queues update --max-attempts --max-concurrent-dispatches` and Terraform's in-place change of `google_cloud_tasks_queue` do the same over JSON (`TestGcloudTasks`, `TestTerraformAppliesAndDestroysThroughTheWrapper`). **Mask semantics:** a path replaces the field it names, a whole message (`retry_config`) or one field of it (`retry_config.max_attempts`); an **empty mask replaces every settable field**, as the API documents, so a field the request leaves out is cleared and then defaulted as on create. Each field defaults on its own. A path naming `name`, an output-only field (`state`, `purge_time`, `rate_limits.max_burst_size`) or no field is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the path**; `state` is changed by `PauseQueue`/`ResumeQueue` only, and a `state` in the body is ignored. The fields `CreateQueue` refuses are refused when the mask names them: `app_engine_routing_override` is **`UNIMPLEMENTED`**; `http_target` is applied (#1282, below). **A queue that does not exist is created**, as the method documents ("creates the queue if it does not exist"), with `CreateQueue`'s name rules. The dispatcher reads the stored queue on every pass and retry, so an update applies to tasks already queued: a failing task in a queue updated from 5 attempts to 2 stops at 2 (same test; unit `TestAnUpdatedRetryConfigChangesRetrying`). Queues have no etag. **Documented limits are refused** (#784), on `CreateQueue` and on an `UpdateQueue` whose mask names the field: `max_attempts` below -1 ("Must be >= -1"), `max_dispatches_per_second` above 500 and `max_concurrent_dispatches` above 5000 (the contract's "maximum allowed value"), and a negative `min_backoff`, `max_backoff`, `max_doublings` or `max_retry_duration`, each `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the field; before, a value out of range was stored or silently replaced by the default (unit `TestQueueLimitsTheContractDocumentsAreRefused`; through the console, `TestConsoleTasksEditQueueAndCreateTask`). |
| `PauseQueue` / `ResumeQueue` | **Verified** | `TestTasksPauseAndResume`. A paused queue genuinely stops dispatching. |
| `PurgeQueue` | **Verified** | `TestTasksPurgeQueue`: every task in the queue goes and no other queue's, the queue and its state stay, it takes tasks again, and `purge_time` is reported (#691). A missing queue is `NotFound`. |
| `CreateTask` | **Verified** | `TestTasksTaskLifecycle`. Name generation, method, body and headers all round-trip. |
| `GetTask` / `DeleteTask` | **Verified** | `TestTasksTaskLifecycle`. |
| `ListTasks` | **Verified** | `TestGcloudTasks`: `gcloud tasks list` over JSON (#591); also gRPC unit tests. |
| Durability | **Verified, measured** | Queues and tasks follow `--mode`: a store under the state directory in persistent mode, memory in ephemeral mode. CI's restart probe (#596): `TestTasksRestartSetup` runs alone just before `stop` and leaves a paused queue holding a task scheduled a day ahead. After `stop` and `up` in persistent mode, `TestTasksAcrossRestart` finds the queue still `PAUSED` and the task's body and `scheduleTime` unchanged; brought up again with `--mode ephemeral`, `GetQueue` is **NOT_FOUND**. |
| `GetIamPolicy`, `SetIamPolicy` on a queue | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | `TestQueueIamPolicyIsStoredNotEnforced` (#366, [ADR-0006](adr/0006-iam-policy-surface.md)): bindings set through the official client read back with a new etag, and a stale etag is **ABORTED**. **No RPC consults a stored policy**: a binding grants and denies nothing, and dispatch is unaffected. Conditions and audit configs are **UNIMPLEMENTED** with the field named. A version 3 policy without conditions is accepted. The policy is kept on the queue, so it goes with `DeleteQueue`, is cleared by `/admin/reset` and is captured by `state save`. From the console's Permissions tab: `TestConsolePermissionsOnAQueue` (#793). |
| `TestIamPermissions` on a queue | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | Same test: returns **every** requested permission, the literal truth when nothing is enforced. |
| JSON API (`/v2/…/queues`) | **Partial** | On the same port as gRPC, for REST clients such as Terraform (#366). Queues are hand-written routes: create, get, list, delete, pause, resume and purge, and their IAM methods (`:getIamPolicy` by GET or POST), each calling the gRPC server; on them an unknown query parameter is ignored. **`PATCH` (UpdateQueue) is transcoded** (#692), by Google's binding `PATCH /v2/{queue.name=projects/*/locations/*/queues/*}`: `updateMask` is a lowerCamelCase FieldMask converted to proto paths, the path's name wins over the body's, and an unknown query parameter is INVALID_ARGUMENT. Unknown JSON fields are refused. Unit-tested (`TestRESTQueueAndIamPolicy`, `TestRESTUpdateQueue`) and driven by Terraform and gcloud (below). |
| JSON API, tasks (`/v2/…/queues/*/tasks`) | **Verified** | Since #591, through the shared `Transcoder` by Google's own `google.api.http` bindings, with the same `GRPCServer` gRPC registers: CreateTask, ListTasks, GetTask and DeleteTask. RunTask, BatchCreateTasks, BatchDeleteTasks and the CMEK config are transcoded too (#1215). The transcoder's query policy applies to task paths and the queue `PATCH` only: `pageSize`, `pageToken` and `responseView` are fields, and an unknown parameter is INVALID_ARGUMENT, where the queue routes ignore it. The official client's REST transport drives a task's lifecycle (unit `TestRESTTasksWithTheOfficialRESTClient`, `TestRESTTaskPathsRefuseUnknownParameters`), and `TestGcloudTasks` does it with the real gcloud. JSON requests, queues and tasks, appear in `/admin/events`. |

### Data plane

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP target dispatch | **Verified** | `TestTasksHTTPDispatchCarriesCloudTasksHeaders`: a task created with the official client reaches a host HTTP server with its method, body and headers, and with `X-CloudTasks-QueueName`, `-TaskName`, `-TaskRetryCount` and `-TaskExecutionCount`. The names are **short IDs**, as the service sends them; full resource names were sent until #276. Non-2xx is retried, matching the real service including 4xx. **`X-CloudTasks-TaskETA`, `-TaskPreviousResponse` and `-TaskRetryReason` are not set.** |
| `oidcToken` / `oauthToken` on an HTTP task | **Verified**, *locally minted* | `TestTasksOIDCAndOAuthTokens` (#1243), with the official client: the token config is kept and returned by `CreateTask` and `GetTask`, and a local HTTP target receives `Authorization: Bearer` with the token: an ID token for the service account whose audience is the URL when none is given, signature checked against the instance's `/certs`, or an opaque access token, the scope defaulting to `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`. A token without `serviceAccountEmail` is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**. Before #1243 both were refused `UNIMPLEMENTED` (#578). **What differs from Google:** the token is minted by this instance, not by Google. An OIDC token is an RS256 JWT signed with the instance's own key (the key behind the ADC fixture and the metadata server), so it verifies against the instance's `/certs` and **never against Google's certificates**: a target that verifies it with Google's keys, as Cloud Run's front end does, rejects it, and one that skips verification or checks the claims only accepts it. Its claims are Google's: `iss` `https://accounts.google.com`, `aud` the audience or else the URL, `email` the service account, `email_verified`, a numeric `sub` and `azp` derived from the account, `iat` and a one-hour `exp`, plus a `cloudburrow` claim naming its origin. An OAuth token is opaque (`cbl_…`), as Google's are, so it carries no account or scope; no Google API would accept it, and CloudBurrow's own services accept every request anyway. **No permission is checked** (ADR-0004): the service account need not exist or be in the queue's project, and the caller need not be allowed to act as it, where Google requires `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs`. A token is minted afresh for each attempt and replaces an `Authorization` header the target's own headers set. |
| A body on a `GET`, `HEAD`, `DELETE` or `OPTIONS` task | **Verified** | **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**, as Google; same test. |
| `dispatch_deadline` | **Verified** | Validated (15 s to 30 min, else **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**), stored and returned by `GetTask` (same test), and **applied to each attempt**: an attempt runs under the task's deadline, or Google's default of 10 minutes, and one that runs past it is a failed attempt recorded at the deadline (unit `TestAttemptsRunUnderTheTaskDeadline`, #579). Before, every attempt was cut off at a fixed 30 s. |
| App Engine target dispatch | **Verified unsupported** | `TestTasksUnsupportedOperationsAreHonest`: returns `Unimplemented` rather than accepting a task that would never be dispatched. |
| Scheduled execution at `scheduleTime` | **Verified** | `TestTasksScheduleTimeIsHonoured`: a task scheduled 3s ahead is not delivered early, and is delivered within 3s of its time. The dispatcher polls every 200ms, so delivery can trail the time by that much. |
| Retry with backoff | **Verified** | `TestTasksAFailingTargetIsRetriedPerRetryConfig`: a target answering 500 is retried after `minBackoff`, then after the doubled delay capped at `maxBackoff`, and dispatch stops at `maxAttempts`. **`maxDoublings` is modelled** as the service documents it: double that many times, then grow linearly (`TestBackoffGrowsLinearlyAfterMaxDoublings`, `TestTheWorkerReschedulesOnTheLinearPhase`). Each `RetryConfig` field defaults on its own, as in the API, and `maxAttempts: -1` is unlimited. Driven by the queue's own `RetryConfig`, distinct from Pub/Sub redelivery. Exhausted tasks are dropped, as the real service does. |
| `RunTask` (forced immediate run) | **Verified** | Since #1215. Returns the task and dispatches it on the dispatcher's next pass, even on a paused queue or one at its rate limits; on failure the retry policy reschedules it, and a task that has succeeded is `NOT_FOUND`, as documented. A task already in flight finishes that attempt first, where Google may start a second. Console: Run now on a task's page (`TestTasksRunTaskDispatchesNow`, `TestConsoleTasksRunNow`). |
| `BatchCreateTasks`, `BatchDeleteTasks` | **Verified** | Since #1215. At most 100 creates, all for the parent queue, and at most 1000 deletes, else `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Non-atomic: each request succeeds or fails alone, failures are in the operation metadata's `failed_requests` by index with state `PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED`, and when every request fails the operation's error is `ABORTED`. The operation is done when returned; a repeated `request_id` for the queue returns the first operation (`TestTasksBatchCreateAndDelete`). |
| `GetCmekConfig`, `UpdateCmekConfig` | **Verified**, stored only | Since #1215. The location's key is validated (a `cryptoKeys` name in the config's location), stored and returned; empty clears it. Nothing is encrypted with it and the key is not looked up in Cloud KMS (`TestTasksCmekConfig`). |
| Concurrent dispatch, `max_concurrent_dispatches` | **Verified** | Attempts run concurrently, across queues and within one, bounded per queue by `max_concurrent_dispatches` (default 1000); a task is never dispatched again while an attempt is out (unit `TestQueuesDispatchConcurrently`, `TestMaxConcurrentDispatchesBoundsAQueue`, #579). Before, dispatch was serial, so one slow handler held up every queue. |
| `max_dispatches_per_second` | **Verified** | **Enforced** with a token bucket per queue, refilled at the queue's rate (default 500/s) and holding up to `max_burst_size` tokens; each dispatch, first attempt or retry, takes one, and the queue's other due tasks wait for the next (#716). `TestTasksMaxDispatchesPerSecondSpacesDeliveries`: a queue created with the official client at 1/s delivers 3 tasks enqueued together at least a second apart, over at least 2 seconds (measured at the target, with 50ms allowed for loopback jitter); without enforcement they arrived microseconds apart. Unit tests on a fake clock cover the spacing, a rate below 1/s, a burst followed by the rate, an idle queue banking no more than its burst, and queues not sharing a bucket (`TestMaxDispatchesPerSecondSpacesDispatches`, `TestAFractionalRateSpacesDispatchesBeyondASecond`, `TestMaxBurstSizeBoundsABurstThenTheRateApplies`, `TestAnIdleQueueBanksNoMoreThanItsBurst`, `TestEachQueueHasItsOwnBucket`). The worker polls every 200ms, so a dispatch can trail its token by that much. Before, the rate was stored and returned but not enforced. |
| `max_burst_size` | **Verified**, CloudBurrow's own value | Output only, and enforced as the bucket's size (#716). Google picks it "based on the value of `max_dispatches_per_second`" and does not document the rule, so the value is **CloudBurrow's choice, not Google's**: one second of the rate, rounded up, at least 1 (500 at the default rate, 1 at 1/s or less). A queue on Google may report and allow a different burst. `GetQueue` returns it (`TestTasksMaxDispatchesPerSecondSpacesDeliveries`, unit `TestBurstSizeIsOneSecondOfTheRate`); before, it was returned as 0. |
| Task name reuse | **Verified** | A task name that was executed, deleted or dropped after its last attempt is **`ALREADY_EXISTS`** for an hour, Cloud Tasks' "approximately one hour", which applications use to de-duplicate enqueues (`TestTasksExecutedNamesAreTombstoned`, unit `TestTaskNamesAreTombstoned`, #579). Deleting the queue, which `/admin/reset` does, clears them. |
| Queue and task IDs | **Verified** | Cloud Tasks' own rules: a queue ID is letters, digits and hyphens, at most 100; a task ID adds underscores, at most 500; anything else is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`** (unit `TestCloudTasksIDRulesAndMissingQueue`). `ListTasks` on a queue that does not exist is **`NOT_FOUND`**, not an empty page (`TestTasksExecutedNamesAreTombstoned`). |

---

## Cloud Run — `google.cloud.run.v2`

**Backing component:** Knative Serving v1.23.0, behind a CloudBurrow-owned Cloud Run v2
adapter. Contract: `google/cloud/run/v2/*.proto`. Admin API is REST. No emulator environment
variable. Requires a local Kubernetes cluster; its absence is a clear capability error, not a
silent degradation.

> **Knative is not Cloud Run.** It is the closest available model. No blanket claim is made
> that it reproduces Cloud Run semantics. Revision traffic and scaling behavior are mapped and
> tested explicitly in #30; whatever is not tested there is not claimed here.
>
> The adapter **refuses configuration it cannot map** — Cloud Storage FUSE and NFS
> volumes return `Unimplemented` with the field named. Secret Manager and in-memory
> volumes, a mount's `subPath`, and the service account are mapped (#1297, #1346; see
> "Volumes and the service account" below); Cloud SQL volumes are served by the Cloud SQL
> Auth Proxy (#1346; see "Cloud SQL volumes" below). VPC access, encryption keys, binary
> authorization, `template.executionEnvironment` and `template.sessionAffinity` are **stored
> and returned, with no effect** (#1346; see "Stored settings" below). A caller who set one
> of the refused fields and had it silently dropped would believe it took effect.
>
> Secret-backed environment is **not** in that list and was listed there in error:
> `secretKeyRef` is mapped and tested — see the Secret Manager section's
> `TestCloudRunRevisionReadsASecretManagerSecret`, which also asserts the payload does not
> appear in the deployed Knative Service.

### Control plane

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateService` | **Verified** | `TestRunServiceLifecycle`: deploys a real container through the official SDK and returns a long-running operation. |
| `GetService` | **Verified** | `TestRunServiceLifecycle`, including `NotFound` for an absent service. |
| Stored settings (#1346) | **Verified** | `TestRunServiceStoredSettingsAndSubPath` and `TestRunJobSubPathAndStoredSettings`, the official `run/apiv2` clients: `template.vpcAccess` (connector, `networkInterfaces`, `egress`), `template.encryptionKey`, `template.executionEnvironment`, `template.sessionAffinity` (services only) and `binaryAuthorization` are accepted, the service becomes ready and the job runs, and each reads back as set on the service, its revision and the job. **Stored and returned, not acted on:** no VPC exists locally, so no traffic goes through the connector; nothing is encrypted with the key and the KMS key is not checked; there is one runtime, so gen1 and gen2 are the same; requests are not pinned to an instance; no image is checked against a policy. Each is a setting Google documents, so it is stored rather than refused; nothing here claims its effect. A worker pool and an instance still refuse VPC access and the encryption key, and an instance its execution environment. The console's deploy, job and edit forms set them (`TestConsoleRunStoredSettings`). `encryptionKeyRevocationAction` and `encryptionKeyShutdownDuration` stay refused. Unit: `TestStoredTemplateSettingsReadBack`, `TestVolumeMountSubPath`, `TestJobRefusesWhatItDoesNotMap`, `TestRunSettingsFieldsRoundTrip`. |
| Cloud SQL volumes (#1346) | **Verified** | `TestRunServiceCloudSQLVolume`, `TestRunJobCloudSQLVolume` and `TestRunServiceCloudSQLMySQLVolume`, the official `run/apiv2` clients on one instance with `--services run,storage,cloudsql,cloudsql-mysql`: a `cloudSqlInstance` volume naming `<project>:us-central1:postgres`, mounted at `/cloudsql`, gives the container a Unix socket at `/cloudsql/<connection name>/.s.PGSQL.5432`, as Cloud Run does; the revision answers `SELECT 1` over HTTP from `psql -h /cloudsql/<conn>`, and the task exits 0 only when that query returns 1. The volume reads back as set. **How:** as on Cloud Run, Google's Cloud SQL Auth Proxy runs beside the container: `gcr.io/cloud-sql-connectors/cloud-sql-proxy:2.19.0`, pinned by digest, unmodified, with `--unix-socket /cloudsql`, `--sqladmin-api-endpoint` at the Cloud SQL Admin API as pods reach it (`cloudburrow-host`), and the connection names; it takes its token from the metadata server. In a service it is a second container (and the serving container gets an explicit port 8080, which Knative requires beside a sidecar); in a job's task a Kubernetes native sidecar, so the task completes when its container exits. The proxy calls `connect.get` and `connect.generateEphemeralCert` and dials port 3307 with TLS 1.3, as against Google; `cloudburrow-host` maps 3307 to a connector listener for pods, and `connectSettings` asked from a pod names that Service's cluster IP, so a pod's volume works even while another CloudBurrow instance holds the host's 3307. A connection name that is not `project:region:instance`, or names an instance or region this instance does not serve, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (`Cloud SQL instance "…" does not exist or you do not have permission to access it`, UNVERIFIED wording); with Cloud SQL off, `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. For Cloud SQL for MySQL the socket is `/cloudsql/<conn>` itself: in `TestRunServiceCloudSQLMySQLVolume` a second container runs the MySQL 8.4 image's own `mysql -S /cloudsql/<conn>` as the `cloudburrow` user, and the service returns its `SELECT 1`. Worker pools and instances refuse the volume. **v1 and gcloud:** `TestGcloudRunDeployCloudSQL`, gcloud through the harness: `gcloud run deploy --add-cloudsql-instances` sends `run.googleapis.com/cloudsql-instances` on the revision template to the v1 (`serving.knative.dev/v1`) API, as `--log-http` shows; it is the same volume, named `cloudsql` and mounted at `/cloudsql` in every container, as Google documents the socket. The service answers `SELECT 1` through it, `services describe` shows the annotation, the official v2 client reads the `cloudsql` volume and mount (UNVERIFIED that Google's v2 shows exactly this shape), the console's edit form prefills Cloud SQL connections from it, and `--remove-cloudsql-instances` removes it. v1 reads any template's Cloud SQL volumes back as the annotation and lists no v1 volume or mount for them; a v1 replace that names the same instances keeps a v2 template's volume names and mount paths. A v1 job's execution-template annotation maps the same way, by unit test only (`TestV1JobCloudSQLAnnotation`). A `cloudsql` volume, or a mount at `/cloudsql`, beside the annotation is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. IAM database authentication is not served (docs/cloudsql.md). The console's deploy, edit and job forms take Cloud SQL connections (`TestConsoleRunCloudSQLConnections`). Unit: `TestCloudSQLVolumeRendersTheAuthProxy`, `TestCloudSQLVolumeInAJobIsANativeSidecar`, `TestCloudSQLVolumeRefusals`, `TestConnectSettingsForPods`, `TestV1CloudSQLAnnotationIsTheVolume`. |
| Volumes and the service account (#1297) | **Verified** | `TestRunServiceVolumesAndServiceAccount` and `TestRunJobMountsSecretAndMemoryVolumes`, the official `run/apiv2` clients with Secret Manager on the same instance; `TestRunV1VolumesProbesAndServiceAccount` for v1. A `secret` volume mounts a Secret Manager secret (see the Secret Manager section); an `emptyDir` volume is a Kubernetes `emptyDir`, `MEMORY` as `medium: Memory` (a tmpfs, which the job's task checks in `/proc/mounts` and writes to) with its `sizeLimit`; each container's `volumeMounts` are rendered, read-only for a secret, and one naming no declared volume, or with a relative path or `/`, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Volumes, mounts and `serviceAccount` read back as set on the service, revision, job and execution. **The service account is the one the workload is told it runs as** (#1388): `TestCloudRunWorkloadIsToldItsServiceAccount` deploys a service with `serviceAccount` set and one without, and runs a job with it set; each container reads `instance/service-accounts/default/email` through `cloud.google.com/go/compute/metadata`, takes an identity token from `google.golang.org/api/idtoken` and an access token from ADC, and reports them. The email and the identity token's `email` claim are the template's `serviceAccount`, or, when none is set, the project's Compute Engine default account `{number}-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com`, with the number every service reports; the access token is a local one (opaque, as Google's are). How: every workload reaches the one metadata server through `cloudburrow-host`, from an address that says nothing about it (the pod's traffic is translated on its way to the host), so the account rides on the name it dials. Each account has an ExternalName Service, `cloudburrow-sa-<hash>`, in the workload namespace, an alias of `cloudburrow-host`, recording the account in an annotation; the injected `GCE_METADATA_HOST` (and a Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sidecar's) names it, every client library sends that name as `Host`, and the metadata server answers as that account. `cloudburrow-host` itself, and the host's own port, still name the instance's `cloudburrow-local@…`, which `cloudburrow env` and the ADC file use. A worker pool's and an instance's pods are given their template's account the same way (unit `TestWorkerPoolPodsNameTheirAccount`). **Not acted on:** the workload still runs as the namespace's default Kubernetes ServiceAccount, the account need not exist in IAM, and no permission is checked: tokens are never verified (ADR-0004). **`UNIMPLEMENTED`**, naming the field: `gcs` (Cloud Storage FUSE needs `/dev/fuse` and a privileged container or a CSI driver, and Knative refuses both on a revision), and `nfs` (no NFS server; Knative refuses `nfs` volumes without its feature flag). **A mount's `subPath`** (#1346) is Kubernetes' `subPath`: `TestRunJobSubPathAndStoredSettings` mounts one in-memory volume at `/data` and at `/sub` with `subPath: a/b`, and the task finds at `/data/a/b/x` the file it wrote through `/sub`; `TestRunServiceStoredSettingsAndSubPath` reads it back on a ready service and its Knative revision; an absolute `subPath`, or one with `..` or not in clean form, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. A job's `startupProbe` and `livenessProbe` stay refused, as a task serves no port. Unit: `TestVolumesAndServiceAccountRender`, `TestV1RoundTripAndRefusals`. |
| `ListServices` | **Verified** | `TestRunServiceLifecycle`. Only CloudBurrow-owned Services are listed. |
| `DeleteService` | **Verified** | Refuses to delete a Knative Service CloudBurrow did not create. |
| `UpdateService` | **Verified** | `TestRunUpdateService` (#300): changing the image and an env var applies the Knative template, which cuts a new revision. The operation completes only when Knative has observed the new generation and **that** revision is ready, not while the old revision still reports Ready. The URL then serves the new version, and `ListRevisions` returns both revisions, newest first. A failed new revision fails the operation with the revision's own reason. With no `update_mask` the whole service is replaced, as `gcloud run deploy` and Terraform send it. A mask is merged onto the service as read back (`TestRunUpdateServiceWithAMask`, #1260): a mask of `labels` sent with no template keeps the container, a mask of `template.containers` keeps the labels the request also carried, a nested path (`template.scaling`) replaces only that message, and the field a path ends on is replaced whole or cleared when unset; `*` replaces everything. A path that is no field, goes inside a repeated field, or names an output-only field is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`** (unit `TestUpdateServiceRefusals`; Google's wording not measured). The console's **Manage traffic** sends a mask of `traffic` alone. `allow_missing` creates and `validate_only` applies nothing. |
| Traffic | **Verified** | `TestRunTrafficSplitAndTags` (#1224), with the official `run.ServicesClient`: a service's `traffic` is Knative's traffic block on `CreateService` and `UpdateService`. `LATEST` is `latestRevision: true`, `REVISION` pins `revisionName` (a full revision resource name is shortened to Knative's), and `percent` and `tag` carry over. Two revisions split 50/50 with tags read back as set in `traffic`, and `traffic_statuses` is Knative's status, each tag's `uri` the URL Knative publishes for it; 40 requests to the service URL reached **both** revisions, and each tag URL answered with its own revision. A service that set no traffic reports 100% to `LATEST`. Refused with **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`** before anything is applied: a percent outside 0 to 100, percents that do not sum to 100 (`TestRunUpdateService`), a `REVISION` target with no revision or a `LATEST` one naming one, a bad or repeated tag, a 0% target with no tag, and a revision the service does not have (unit `TestTraffic*` in `internal/adapter/run`; codes not measured against Google). A tagged revision counts as serving even at 0%, so `DeleteRevision` refuses it. The console's **Manage traffic** sets it (`TestCloudRunManageTrafficThroughTheBrowser`). |
| `GetRevision`, `ListRevisions`, `DeleteRevision` | **Verified** | `TestRunRevisions` (#299), official `run.RevisionsClient` against Knative in CI. Knative Revisions are mapped onto `run.v2.Revision`: the name under the caller's service, the service, the generation (Knative's `configurationGeneration`: 1 for the first deploy), create time, uid, containers (image, env, ports), concurrency and every condition. A new service has exactly one revision; an unknown one is NOT_FOUND. **Deleting a revision that serves traffic is refused** with FAILED_PRECONDITION, as Cloud Run refuses it; a retired revision is deleted. Revision fields Knative has no counterpart for (scaling, VPC access, encryption, execution environment) are absent rather than invented. |
| Operations (`google.longrunning`) | **Verified** | `GetOperation` backs the SDK's `op.Wait`. Pending, succeeded and failed are all reachable; a failed revision reports Knative's own message. **`ListOperations` and `WaitOperation`** (#1229): `TestRunOperationsListAndWait`, through Google's longrunning `OperationsClient` on the Cloud Run port, lists a location's operations in name order and in pages, and applies a `filter` before paging (#1263): AIP-160 comparisons on `done`, `name` (`=`, `!=`, `:`) and `error.code`, joined by `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` and parentheses; any other field is INVALID_ARGUMENT naming it (UNVERIFIED), never ignored. It waits: a done operation returns at once, a pending one returns as it is when the request's `timeout` passes (or the call's deadline, with none), as AIP-151 describes, and otherwise when it finishes; an unknown one is NOT_FOUND. Operations are kept in memory, so a restart forgets them. `CancelOperation` stays UNIMPLEMENTED. |
| `Builds.SubmitBuild` | **Verified** | `TestRunSubmitBuildDockerDeploys` (#1268), with the official `run.BuildsClient`, in the run shard: a gzipped tarball (a Dockerfile and a static server built from `testdata/sourcebuild`) is uploaded to the instance's Cloud Storage, `SubmitBuild` with `storage_source` and `docker_build` returns at once with `build_operation`, polled through the Builds client's `GetOperation` until done, and a following `CreateService` naming the same `image_uri` deploys it and answers through the ingress. **The build is local, not Cloud Build**: the archive is read through the instance's Cloud Storage JSON API (`generation` honoured), unpacked (entries escaping the directory refused), built with the host's Docker for the cluster nodes' platform (`docker_build`, the `Dockerfile` at the archive's root) or with pack and the pinned Google builder (`buildpack_build`, `function_target` and `environment_variables` mapped; amd64 images only), and loaded into the kind cluster as `dev.local/<image_uri>` (`:latest` when untagged). Since #1383 the image is also pushed to the `image_uri`'s Artifact Registry repository when this instance holds it (otherwise it is only loaded, and `image_uri` is a name only); on this instance `CreateService`, `UpdateService` and jobs naming it run the loaded image, reading back as the `image_uri`. Since #1347 the operation is Cloud Build's, as Google's is: `projects/*/locations/*/operations/{build id}`, with `BuildOperationMetadata` (the `Build`) while it runs, answering the `Build` on success (see the Cloud Build row) and failing with the build's own output; `base_image_uri` is not set. A missing object is **`NOT_FOUND`** at the call; an instance without Cloud Storage is **`FAILED_PRECONDITION`**. **`UNIMPLEMENTED`**, naming the field, as they need Cloud Build: `service_account`, `worker_pool`, `machine_type`, and `buildpack_build.runtime`, `cache_image_uri`, `base_image`, `enable_automatic_updates`, `project_descriptor`. `tags`, `release_track` and `client` are accepted and ignored. The buildpacks path is `TestFunctionsSubmitBuildBuildpacks`, gated with the Functions tests (`CLOUDBURROW_TEST_FUNCTIONS`, pack, amd64 nodes; `functions.yml`) and **not yet run**. `gcloud run deploy --source` is verified below (#1347). The archive may also be a zip, which gcloud uploads. Unit: `TestSubmitBuild*`, `TestUntarGz*`. |
| JSON API (REST) | **Verified** | **One port serves gRPC and JSON** (#591), as `run.googleapis.com` does: the shared `Transcoder` in `internal/transport/rest` serves Google's own `google.api.http` bindings of every `google.cloud.run.v2` service, plus the four Operations bindings of `run_v2.yaml` (`GetOperation`, `DeleteOperation`, `ListOperations`, `:wait`), and calls the same registered servers gRPC does. Services, Revisions, Jobs, Executions, Tasks (#1223), WorkerPools (#1300), Instances (#1299) and Operations are transcoded; `ListOperations` and `WaitOperation` are served since #1229 (unit `TestRESTUnservedPaths`); Builds is transcoded since #1268 (`POST /v2/{parent}/builds:submit`); a path Google does not bind answers 404. The query-parameter policy is KMS's: request fields the path and body do not bind (`serviceId`, `jobId`, `validateOnly`, `allowMissing`, `etag`, `pageSize`, ...) are query parameters, and an unknown one is INVALID_ARGUMENT. `TestTerraformRun` drives it with Terraform's provider (below); unit `TestRESTJobLifecycle` and `TestRESTUnservedPaths` pin the wire. JSON requests appear in `/admin/events` with their project; fault injection and the gRPC request log are not interposed on them. |
| Terraform `google_cloud_run_v2_service`, `google_cloud_run_v2_job` | **Verified** | `TestTerraformRun` (#591): both apply through `cloudburrow terraform` with `hashicorp/google` 8.4.0 and egress blocked, plan clean, take a label and an environment-variable change as a `PATCH` each, plan clean again, and destroy; each step is read back through the official gRPC clients, and the event log shows the creates, operation polls and deletes arrived as JSON. The wrapper sets `cloud_run_v2_custom_endpoint`. Only what the adapter maps is accepted: JSON reaches the same server methods as gRPC, so a refused field (a service account, VPC access, volumes) is UNIMPLEMENTED naming it; no module setting one has been applied. |
| `gcloud run services list` / `describe`, `gcloud run revisions list` | **Verified** | `TestGcloudRunServicesList` (#1293), the pinned gcloud 586.0.0 through `gcloud-setup`'s configuration alone: `services list` with no `--region` is the global `projects.locations.services.list` (`locations/-`), and `describe` and `revisions list` with `--region` call the namespaced v1 path at `{region}-{host}`, which gcloud derives from the override. `gcloud-setup` therefore writes `run = http://run.localhost:<port>/` on a loopback bind: `us-central1-run.localhost` is still loopback (RFC 6761; resolved by macOS and by systemd-resolved or nss-myhostname on Linux), where `us-central1-127.0.0.1` does not resolve. In the console's terminal pod the override is the in-cluster host, so there only the region-less `services list` works. `gcloud run deploy --image` is verified separately below (#1297). |
| `gcloud run deploy --image`, `gcloud run services describe`, `gcloud run services delete` | **Verified** | `TestGcloudRunDeployImage` (#1297), gcloud 587.0.0 through `gcloud-setup`'s configuration alone: it deploys an image with a variable and `--no-allow-unauthenticated`, becomes ready, deploys again with a changed variable (a GET and a `replaceService`, cutting revision 2), `describe` shows the URL, the ready revision and the new value, and `services delete` removes it. Three things refused it before: gcloud asks Service Usage (`serviceusage.googleapis.com`, not served then; served since #1352) whether the API is enabled, which `gcloud-setup` now turns off with `core/should_prompt_to_enable_api = false`; it annotates the service and revision with `run.googleapis.com/client-name`, `client-version` and `startup-cpu-boost`, now mapped (see the v1 row); and it sends an empty `spec.template.spec.sandboxes`, now dropped. gcloud 586 and 587 send no `startupProbe` of their own unless `--startup-probe` is given (both releases' `command_lib/run/flags.py`, checked for #1349); one in Cloud Run's default shape (`tcpSocket` on 8080, `timeoutSeconds` and `periodSeconds` 240, `failureThreshold` 1), as a client that read it back from Google would send, is mapped (unit `TestV1RoundTripAndRefusals`). A 240-second period is slow locally: a kind kubelet started less than one period ago delays the first probe by a random part of it. `--source` is verified in the next row (#1347). |

| Cloud Build default logs bucket, `{project number}.cloudbuild-logs.googleusercontent.com` | **Verified** | `TestCloudBuildDefaultLogsBucket` (#1430) with the official `cloudbuild` client on the Run port, on an instance started with `--cloudbuild-host-steps`: a build with no `logsBucket` reports `gs://NUMBER.cloudbuild-logs.googleusercontent.com`, and the official Cloud Storage client reads and lists its `log-{id}.txt` there; an upload to that bucket is **403**, as the bucket is Google's, and the project's `buckets.list` leaves it out. `TestGcloudBuildsSubmitDefaultLogsBucket`: `gcloud builds submit --async --config` of a cloudbuild.yaml naming no `logsBucket`, egress blocked; `gcloud builds describe` gives the default bucket and `gcloud storage cat` prints the log. Unit-tested: Cloud Build makes the bucket on the first log through the storage server's own path, past the bucket-name check a user's create still fails (`google` in the name, **400**); uploads, deletes, patches and copies into it through the JSON and XML APIs are **403** (gRPC, served by the same handlers in process, is refused the same way), a copy out of it is served; a log that cannot be written is recorded for the build (the instance log and the console's build page) instead of dropped. `gcloud builds submit` without `--async` and `gcloud builds log` read the log from `storage.googleapis.com` themselves, which no endpoint override changes, nor `--suppress-logs` (see [functions-and-builds.md](functions-and-builds.md)). |
| Cloud Build triggers: `CloudBuild.CreateBuildTrigger`, `GetBuildTrigger`, `ListBuildTriggers`, `UpdateBuildTrigger`, `DeleteBuildTrigger`, `RunBuildTrigger`, `ReceiveTriggerWebhook` | **Verified**, *manual and webhook triggers with an inline build* | `TestCloudBuildTriggersAndWorkerPools` (#1422) with the official `cloudbuild` client over gRPC on the Run port, on one instance with `--services run,storage,secretmanager,pubsub` and `--cloudbuild-host-steps`: a trigger, global or regional, is stored with an `id` and `resourceName` and read by ID or by name (as `trigger_id` accepts either), listed with paging, and updated with or without an `update_mask`. `RunBuildTrigger` runs its inline `build` as `CreateBuild` does, with the trigger's `substitutions` and the request's `source.substitutions` over them, the built-in `$TRIGGER_NAME` and `$TRIGGER_BUILD_CONFIG_PATH` (empty: the config is inline), and `buildTriggerId` set (ListBuilds' `trigger_id` filter finds it); a `disabled` trigger is `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. A **webhook** trigger (`webhookConfig.secret`, a Secret Manager version) runs on `POST …/triggers/{id or name}:webhook?key=…&secret=…`, JSON or gRPC: the `secret` must equal the version's payload, read from this instance's Secret Manager, else **403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`** (Google's message is UNVERIFIED); `$(body.a.b)` bindings in its substitutions take the payload's values; the API key is not checked. **Refused `UNIMPLEMENTED` with the reason:** GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Cloud Source Repositories events (`github`, `triggerTemplate`, `repositoryEventConfig`), which need a hosted git service; a build read from a repository (`filename`, `gitFileSource`, `sourceToBuild`, `autodetect`), which Google clones from a hosted service and cannot read from a local path or `file://` URL, so it is not faithful here; `pubsubConfig`, whose messages Google pushes through a subscription it owns (a Pub/Sub push subscription to the webhook URL does the same job); a CEL `filter`, `serviceAccount`, `includedFiles`/`ignoredFiles`, a `RunBuildTrigger` source naming a branch, tag or commit, and `approvalConfig.approvalRequired`. Triggers are kept in memory. `TestGcloudBuildsTriggersAndWorkerPools`, gcloud through the harness: `gcloud builds triggers create manual --inline-config --substitutions`, `describe`, `run` (the build is SUCCESS with `$TRIGGER_NAME` substituted, on the pool), `create webhook --secret` (its URL runs a build), `delete`. Console: Cloud Build's Triggers page (create, Run, delete). |
| Cloud Build private worker pools: `CloudBuild.CreateWorkerPool`, `GetWorkerPool`, `ListWorkerPools`, `UpdateWorkerPool`, `DeleteWorkerPool`, and a build's `options.pool.name` | **Verified**, *stored; builds run locally* | `TestCloudBuildTriggersAndWorkerPools` (#1422): a pool (regional; `global` is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`) is created behind a long-running operation (`CreateWorkerPoolOperationMetadata`, the pool as its response) `RUNNING` with a `uid` and `etag`, read, listed, updated with an `update_mask` (`UpdateWorkerPoolOperationMetadata`; a stale `etag` is `ABORTED`) and deleted (`allow_missing`, `validate_only`); its `privatePoolV1Config` reads back as set. A build naming it in `options.pool.name` (or the deprecated `options.workerPool`) runs on the host's Docker like any build, with the pool recorded on the build; a pool that does not exist is `NOT_FOUND`, one in another region than a regional build `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Not acted on: the machine type, disk size and network config (no VPC exists locally); `privateServiceConnect` is 501. `gcloud builds worker-pools create`, `describe` and `delete` in `TestGcloudBuildsTriggersAndWorkerPools`. Console: Cloud Build's Worker pools page (create, delete). |
| `gcloud builds submit` | **Verified** (Dockerfile sources and docker steps, with `--async`) | `TestGcloudBuildsSubmit` (#1347), the pinned gcloud through `gcloud-setup`'s configuration alone, egress to Google blocked: `--tag` of a Dockerfile source (the global `projects.locations.builds.create` at `locations/global`, one `gcr.io/cloud-builders/gcb-internal` step running `docker build`, the image pushed through `images`), and `--config` of a cloudbuild.yaml of a `docker build` and a `docker push` step with `--region` and `--substitutions`, each staged in the `{project}_cloudbuild` bucket; `gcloud builds describe` polls each to `SUCCESS` with its steps `SUCCESS` and its image. **Without `--async`**, gcloud 587 tails the log from `https://storage.googleapis.com/{logsBucket}/log-{id}.txt` itself, ignoring the `storage` endpoint override, even with `--suppress-logs`: with egress blocked it fails, and with egress open it would read Google. The log is written to the instance's Cloud Storage, where `gsutil cat` or the console reads it. `--pack` goes through the pack gate and is **not yet run** through gcloud. |
| `gcloud builds submit` of steps of any image, `gcloud builds list --filter` | **Verified** | `TestGcloudBuildsStepsAndList` (#1382), the pinned gcloud through `gcloud-setup`'s configuration alone, egress to Google blocked, on an instance started with `--cloudbuild-host-steps`: `--config` of a cloudbuild.yaml whose first step is a shell image (`entrypoint: sh`) writing `gen.txt`, then a `docker build` copying it and a `docker push`, with `tags` and `--substitutions`; `gcloud builds describe` polls it to `SUCCESS` with each step `SUCCESS` and its image. `gcloud builds list --filter='tags=… AND status=SUCCESS'` lists exactly that build, and `status=FAILURE` lists none. |
| `Services.GetIamPolicy`, `Services.SetIamPolicy`, `Services.TestIamPermissions` | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | `TestRunServiceIamPolicyIsStoredNotEnforced` (#1216, [ADR-0006](adr/0006-iam-policy-surface.md) as amended by #1216), official `run.ServicesClient`: bindings set read back with a new etag, a stale etag is **ABORTED**, a condition is **UNIMPLEMENTED** naming the field, and a version 3 policy without conditions is accepted (read back as version 1). **Nothing consults a stored policy**: a `roles/run.invoker` binding neither admits nor refuses a request to the service's URL, which is open to every caller. `TestIamPermissions` returns **every** requested permission on a service that exists and an empty set on a missing one, as `iam_policy.proto` documents (not measured on Cloud Run). The policy is kept in a ConfigMap of its own, owned by the Knative Service, so a policy change leaves the service's `etag` alone, the policy goes with `DeleteService`, and a service created again under the same name starts with none (asserted). Like the service itself it is not cleared by `/admin/reset` nor captured by `state save`. From the console's Permissions tab: `TestConsolePermissionsOnARunServiceAndJob`. |

### Data plane

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pull image and start container | **Verified** | Prebuilt images only. Local images are rewritten to `dev.local/` with `imagePullPolicy: Never`; untagged references are refused. An image under a `DOCKER` repository this instance's Artifact Registry holds, and not built here, is pulled from that registry by digest (#1383, `TestArtifactRegistryDockerRegistry`): its tag is resolved there, the revision names `image@digest` (so Knative resolves nothing), and each kind node's containerd reaches the registry through `/etc/containerd/certs.d/{region}-docker.pkg.dev/hosts.toml`, written at `up` for every region, whose server and mirror are the Run port at the address pods reach the host at, so a pull never falls back to Google. The service reads back the reference deployed. |
| Readiness detection | **Verified** | Reported from Knative's `Ready` condition, including the failure message. A service still reconciling is pending, not failed. |
| Request routing to container | **Verified** | The acceptance workflow delivers a Pub/Sub push to a deployed Cloud Run service, which reads and writes Cloud Storage. |
| Injected environment (endpoints, `PORT`) | **Verified** | `TestCloudRunRevisionReachesStorageAndPubSubWithNoClientOptions` (#576): a service deployed with no `env` calls `storage.NewClient(ctx)` and `pubsub.NewClient(ctx, project)` with no options, lists a bucket and publishes to a topic, and the host pulls the message. `TestCloudRunRevisionUsesInjectedMetadataADCAndServedEndpoints` (#681): a service deployed with no `env` gets credentials from `google.FindDefaultCredentials`, which finds no file and asks the metadata server at the injected `GCE_METADATA_HOST`; an official Storage client sends that local token on a bucket listing. The same revision calls KMS `Encrypt`, Scheduler `ListJobs` and Logging `WriteLogEntries` at the injected `CLOUDBURROW_KMS_ENDPOINT`, `CLOUDBURROW_SCHEDULER_ENDPOINT` and `CLOUDBURROW_LOGGING_ENDPOINT`, and the host decrypts the ciphertext, finds its job in the listing and lists the entry. Every revision and job task is given the in-cluster `*_EMULATOR_HOST` of each enabled emulator, `CLOUDBURROW_*_ENDPOINT` and `GCE_METADATA_HOST` at `cloudburrow-host` (with Cloud Run, [networking.md](networking.md#reaching-your-machine-from-a-pod)), and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` (the service's project). **Exercised from a pod, through the injected value:** `STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST`, `PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GCE_METADATA_HOST`, `CLOUDBURROW_KMS_ENDPOINT`, `CLOUDBURROW_SCHEDULER_ENDPOINT`, `CLOUDBURROW_LOGGING_ENDPOINT` and `CLOUDBURROW_BIGQUERY_ENDPOINT`. `TestCloudRunRevisionGetsBigQueryRefusalsThroughTheFront` (#874, #902) calls BigQuery at the injected `CLOUDBURROW_BIGQUERY_ENDPOINT`, the emulator's Service, whose REST port is the validating front in the emulator's pod. **Injected but not exercised from a pod:** `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST`, `DATASTORE_EMULATOR_HOST`, `BIGTABLE_EMULATOR_HOST`, `SPANNER_EMULATOR_HOST` (the Spanner pod test sets its own), `CLOUDBURROW_BIGQUERY_STORAGE_ENDPOINT`, and `CLOUDBURROW_TASKS_ENDPOINT`, `CLOUDBURROW_SECRETMANAGER_ENDPOINT` and `CLOUDBURROW_RESOURCEMANAGER_ENDPOINT` (the host probe is given its addresses); no CI shard enables Cloud Run with the opt-in emulators other than BigQuery (the run shard, #874). **A variable the caller sets wins.** In the pod the injected ones follow the caller's, each in name order. The Cloud Run API (`GetService`, `ListServices`, `GetRevision`, jobs and executions) shows **only the caller's** env, as Cloud Run keeps `K_SERVICE` and `PORT` out of the resource, so a Terraform plan sees no drift; `kubectl get ksvc -o yaml` shows the injected ones. No credential is injected. `PORT` is Knative's. The caller's `env` is still mapped and ordered deterministically. |
| Logs in Cloud Logging | **Verified** (stderr severity and `instanceId` value UNVERIFIED) | `TestCloudRunLogsInCloudLogging` (#1298), in CI's run shard (Logging as `RUN_LOGGING`), read back with the official `logadmin` client: while Cloud Run and Cloud Logging are both served, each line a revision's or a job task's container writes is an entry in log `run.googleapis.com/stdout` or `run.googleapis.com/stderr` (by the stream the container runtime recorded, read from the pod's log file on the kind node), with resource `cloud_run_revision` (`project_id`, `service_name`, `revision_name`, `location`, `configuration_name`) or `cloud_run_job` (`project_id`, `job_name`, `location`), the label `instanceId` (the pod's UID) and, for a task, `run.googleapis.com/execution_name`, `task_index` and `task_attempt`. A line that is a JSON object is a `jsonPayload`, its `severity`, `logging.googleapis.com/labels`, `trace`, `spanId`, `trace_sampled`, `insertId` and an RFC 3339 `time` or `timestamp` read out of it as Google's structured logging documents, `message` kept; any other line is a `textPayload` with severity DEFAULT, stderr included. The entries go through WriteLogEntries, so exclusions apply, and are read by ListLogEntries, `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloud_run_revision"'` (run by hand through `gcloud-setup`) and the console's Logs Explorer. Not the queue-proxy sidecar's lines; lines a pod wrote before `up` started are not written again. Units `TestRunLogTargets`, `TestRunLogEntry`, `TestRunLogFeederReadsCRIStreams`. Since #1333 `TestGcloudRunLogsRead`, through the compat harness with egress to Google blocked: the real `gcloud run services logs read` and `gcloud run jobs logs read` print the lines the service's and the job's containers wrote, and not another service's; `--log-filter=severity>=WARNING` leaves out the DEFAULT lines. Their filters (`resource.type`, `resource.labels.service_name` or `job_name`, `resource.labels.location`, `severity >= DEFAULT`) are in the grammar below. In CI's run shard where gcloud is installed, through gcloud-setup's `run` and `logging` overrides of that instance. |
| Stop and cleanup | **Verified** | Deletion refuses any Knative Service lacking `cloudburrow.dev/owned=true`. |
| Scale to keep an instance warm (`minInstanceCount`) | **Verified** | `TestMinScaleKeepsAnInstanceWarm`: a pod stays running with no traffic. |
| Requests per instance (`maxInstanceRequestConcurrency`) | Partial | Mapped to Knative's `containerConcurrency` and readable on the console's Configuration tab. **Not tested under load** — proving a concurrency limit needs sustained traffic. |
| Request timeout (`template.timeout`) | Partial | Mapped to Knative's `timeoutSeconds` and asserted by `TestTimeoutReachesKnative`. It was previously **dropped in silence**, so a service deployed with a ten-minute timeout got Knative's default and failed at five with nothing to explain it. The mapping is asserted; the resulting behaviour under a long request is not. |
| Resource limits (`container.resources.limits`) | Partial | CPU and memory limits reach the manifest. Whether the kubelet enforces them identically to Cloud Run is not claimed. |
| Scale to zero | **Verified** | `TestScaleToZeroHappensWithoutTraffic`, observed on Knative's own schedule. Cloud Run also scales to zero but on a different schedule; the timing is **not** claimed to match. |
| Max instances (`maxInstanceCount`) | Partial | `TestMaxScaleIsRecordedOnTheRevision` proves the annotation reaches the revision. **The cap is not tested under load** — proving a ceiling needs sustained concurrency that would make the suite slow and flaky. |
| Traffic to the latest revision | **Verified** | `TestSingleRevisionTakesAllTraffic`: 100% to the latest revision. |
| Traffic splitting across revisions | **Verified** | `TestRunTrafficSplitAndTags`: a 50/50 split over 40 requests reached both revisions (see Traffic above). The split is Knative's; the distribution is not claimed to match Cloud Run's request for request. |
| Service name validated before apply | **Verified** | An invalid name previously reached the cluster and came back as `Internal` — which says the fault is ours when it is the caller's, and buries the rule. Now `InvalidArgument` naming the rule. A cluster rejection is also classified as `InvalidArgument` rather than `Internal`, and carries the cluster's own message. |
| Jobs / Executions | **Verified** | Served on Kubernetes `batch/v1` Jobs (#582); see [Jobs and executions](#cloud-run-jobs-and-executions) below. |
| **Service URL reachable from a browser** | **Verified** | `cloudburrow up` publishes the Knative gateway on a host port (default `9080`) and names services `<service>.<namespace>.cloudburrow.localhost`. Verified with headless Chrome and `test/k8s/ingress_test.go`. **Loopback only**, HTTP only. The mapping is fixed at cluster creation, and `up` reports when a cluster predates it rather than leaving a port that silently refuses. |
| Service URL DNS resolution | Partial | `*.cloudburrow.localhost` resolves on the macOS system resolver and musl, **not** on bare glibc or **Go's pure resolver** (`CGO_ENABLED=0`), which forwards the query to the configured nameserver. The `Host`-header path needs no resolver and always works. Measured matrix in [networking.md](networking.md). |
| HTTPS to a service | **Not supported** | No certificate is issued. Publishing a port answering with a self-signed certificate would look like support for something that does not work. |

### Cloud Run: Worker pools and instances

`google.cloud.run.v2.WorkerPools` (#1300) and `google.cloud.run.v2.Instances` (#1299) are served on
the Cloud Run port, over gRPC and JSON. Both are containers that run with no request routed to them,
at a fixed count, which is an `apps/v1` Deployment with no Knative Service, route or autoscaler. The
resource is kept as protojson in a ConfigMap the adapter owns (`run-worker-pool-<scope>-<id>`,
`run-instance-<scope>-<id>`, where `<scope>` is a hash of `projects/{p}/locations/{l}`, also the
`cloudburrow.dev/run-scope` label on every object and in every selector, so two projects' or regions'
resources of one ID are two, #1399; one an older version created as `run-worker-pool-<id>` still
reads back, updates and deletes under that name), so its `etag` is the ConfigMap's `resourceVersion` and does not move when the
Deployment's status does. The pods are rendered by **the same container mapping as a revision and a
task**: image localisation, `command`, `args`, `env`, `secretKeyRef`, `resources.limits`, probes,
secret and in-memory volumes. A create, update, stop or start operation completes **once the
instances are ready** (#1348), as a service's completes once its revision is: while they come up,
a read reports `reconciling` with a `Ready` terminal condition of `CONDITION_RECONCILING`, then
`CONDITION_SUCCEEDED` once every wanted pod is available (and, for an instance, its route is
programmed). The operation fails, FAILED_PRECONDITION with the reason, when the Deployment's rollout
stalls (`CONDITION_FAILED` with the controller's message), when a pod cannot start (`ErrImagePull`,
`ImagePullBackOff`, `InvalidImageName`, `CreateContainerConfigError`, `CreateContainerError`), or
when the instances are not ready within the adapter's ready timeout (five minutes by default).

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `WorkerPools.CreateWorkerPool`, `WorkerPools.GetWorkerPool`, `WorkerPools.ListWorkerPools`, `WorkerPools.UpdateWorkerPool`, `WorkerPools.DeleteWorkerPool` | **Verified** | `TestRunWorkerPoolLifecycle`, official `run.WorkerPoolsClient`: a pool of two instances becomes ready, is read and listed (newest first). `scaling.manualInstanceCount` is the Deployment's `replicas`; unset, a pool gets **one** instance. Changing only the count keeps the revision; a changed template is a new revision named `{pool}-{generation}-{suffix}` (or `template.revision` when set), and the old one is retired. `UpdateWorkerPool` with no `update_mask` replaces the whole pool; **with one** (#1387) only the fields it names change, merged onto the stored pool as `UpdateService` merges (#1260, AIP-134): `TestRunWorkerPoolUpdateMaskAndInstanceSplits` rescales with `scaling.manual_instance_count` alone (the description and the revision are kept) and changes `template` alone (a new revision at the same count); a path names a field anywhere in the tree and replaces it whole, `*` replaces every settable field, and an output-only or unknown path is INVALID_ARGUMENT. `allow_missing` creates; a stale `etag` is ABORTED. **`instanceSplits` across revisions** (#1387), as Google documents for worker pools: each split gives the latest revision (`INSTANCE_SPLIT_ALLOCATION_TYPE_LATEST`) or a named one a percentage of `scaling.manualInstanceCount`, and they add up to 100 (otherwise INVALID_ARGUMENT, as is a split naming no revision, the same revision twice, or a revision the pool does not have). The pool's Deployment runs the latest revision's share; each other revision with a share runs as a Deployment of its own, rendered from the template its ReplicaSet recorded. A share is its percentage of the instances rounded by largest remainder, so the shares add up to the instance count, ties to the split listed first (Google does not document its rounding; UNVERIFIED). The test splits four instances 50/50 between two revisions and finds two running pods of each, both revisions `Active`, `instanceSplitStatuses` as set, and the split revision's `DeleteRevision` FAILED_PRECONDITION; 100% to the latest again retires the old revision and its pods stop. The pool is ready once every revision's instances are. Unit `TestInstanceSplitsAreChecked`, `TestSplitSharesAddUpToTheInstanceCount`, `TestSplitRevisionRendersItsOwnDeployment`, `TestMergeWorkerPoolMask`. `DeleteWorkerPool` removes the Deployment, every revision and every pod. Refused as UNIMPLEMENTED with the reason: `container.ports` (a worker pool has no ingress), `customAudiences`, `binaryAuthorization`, `template.serviceMesh`, and the pod fields a service refuses (VPC access, CMEK, node selector, GCS and NFS volumes). |
| Worker pool revisions: `Revisions.GetRevision`, `ListRevisions`, `DeleteRevision` under `workerPools/{pool}` | **Verified** | `TestRunWorkerPoolLifecycle`, official `run.RevisionsClient`. Each revision is the ReplicaSet the Deployment created for its template, which records the template; a retired revision is a ReplicaSet scaled to zero, with `Active` `CONDITION_FAILED` reason `RETIRED`; a revision with a share of `instanceSplits` is `Active` (#1387). Listed newest first. Deleting the revision the pool runs, or one with a split share, is FAILED_PRECONDITION; a retired one is deleted. `service` is left empty. |
| `CreateInstance`, `GetInstance`, `ListInstances`, `StopInstance`, `StartInstance`, `DeleteInstance` | **Verified** | `TestRunInstanceLifecycle`, official `run.InstancesClient`: a standalone instance is a Deployment of one replica, becomes ready, is listed, is stopped (scaled to zero; the terminal condition says "the instance is stopped") and started again, and is deleted. Whether it is stopped is kept on the stored instance. `CreateInstance`'s operation completes once the instance is ready and its route is programmed (#1348). **An instance has a URL** (`urls`, which the proto documents as "All URLs serving traffic for this Instance"): `http://<id>.instance.<namespace>.cloudburrow.localhost`, served through the Knative gateway as a service is, by a Knative networking Ingress over a ClusterIP Service on the serving port; `TestRunInstanceLifecycle` reads the container's reply through it. The serving container is the one that declares a port, or the only one, on its port or 8080, and is given `PORT` unless it sets it, as Cloud Run's container contract does; an instance of several containers none of which declares a port has no URL. Google's URL form for an instance is not documented; the local host is CloudBurrow's (UNVERIFIED). `ingress` `INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL` (the value read back when unset) is mapped; any other value is UNIMPLEMENTED, as for a service; `invokerIamDisabled` is stored and returned, and no invoker IAM is enforced either way; `iapEnabled` is UNIMPLEMENTED. `showDeleted` is UNIMPLEMENTED, since a deleted instance is not kept. `etag` is checked on stop, start and delete. |
| Two projects' resources of one ID | **Verified** for worker pools, jobs, instances and services | `TestRunNamesPerProject` (#1399, #1400), official `run.WorkerPoolsClient`, `run.JobsClient`, `run.ExecutionsClient`, `run.InstancesClient`, `run.ServicesClient` and `run.RevisionsClient`: two projects each create a worker pool, a job, an instance and a service of one ID; each reads back under its own full name with its own labels, lists only in its own project, runs its own pods (each instance and each service answers at its own URL with its own greeting), and counts only its own executions; a second create of the service in one project is ALREADY_EXISTS; deleting one project's leaves the other's ready and serving. Their Kubernetes objects are named `run-<kind>-<scope>-<id>` (bounded to 63 characters with a hash where a DNS label needs it) and selected by the `cloudburrow.dev/run-scope` label; the full resource name is the `cloudburrow.dev/cloud-run-name` annotation, which is what reads back. An execution keeps its generated ID as its batch Job's name, drawn again on a collision. **A service** (#1400) is the Knative Service `<id>-<scope>` (an ID too long for that keeps its first 48 characters and a hash of the full name, so its revisions' names fit in 63), so its URL is `http://<id>-<scope>.default.cloudburrow.localhost` and a tag's `http://<tag>-<id>-<scope>.default.cloudburrow.localhost`; Google's `https://<id>-<hash>-<region>.a.run.app` does not resolve locally. Its revisions read back as Cloud Run names them, `<id>-<generation>-<suffix>` (`x-00001-k4q`; the three-character suffix is a hash of the Knative revision's name, so it is the same on every read), in `latestReadyRevision`, `latestCreatedRevision`, `traffic`, `trafficStatuses`, `Revisions.*`, the v1 API, the console and the logs' `revision_name`, and a revision named so is found again for `GetRevision`, `DeleteRevision`, traffic and tags; Knative's own form (`x-<scope>-00001`) is not a revision ID. A service an older version created is a Knative Service named by its ID: it keeps that name, its URL and its revisions' names (`x-00001`), and is still read, updated, deleted and given IAM under them. **Gap:** a revision's container sees `K_SERVICE`, `K_CONFIGURATION` and `K_REVISION` as Knative sets them, the scoped Knative names, where Cloud Run sets the service ID and the revision ID; Knative reserves the three, so they cannot be set to Cloud Run's values. The console lists the selected project's services (and any older one that recorded no project). |

### Cloud Run: Jobs and executions

`google.cloud.run.v2.Jobs`, `google.cloud.run.v2.Executions` and `google.cloud.run.v2.Tasks` (#1223) are served on the Cloud Run port
over gRPC (#582). A job is configuration, stored as a ConfigMap the adapter owns
(`run-job-<scope>-<id>`, scoped by project and location as a worker pool is, #1399, labelled
`cloudburrow.dev/owned=true`, the job kept as protojson; one an older version created as
`run-job-<id>` still reads back, updates and deletes); each
`RunJob` creates one `batch/v1` Job, which is the execution. Its containers are rendered by
**the same code as a service's revision**: image localisation and pull policy, untagged images
refused, `command`, `args`, `workingDir`, `env`, `secretKeyRef` resolved to the Secret Manager
store's Kubernetes Secret, and `resources.limits`. They are served over JSON too, on the same port (#591): Terraform's
`google_cloud_run_v2_job` applies, updates and destroys (`TestTerraformRun`). `gcloud run jobs`
uses Cloud Run's v1 API: `create`, `list`, `describe` and `delete` are served (#1349), and `update`, `execute` and `executions` (#1379). Worker pools and standalone instances are served
on `apps/v1` Deployments (below); Builds is (#1268, above).

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateJob`, `GetJob`, `ListJobs`, `UpdateJob`, `DeleteJob` | **Verified** | `TestRunJobLifecycle`, with the official `run.JobsClient`. Each returns a long-running operation that is done at once: the job is ready when it is written. Unset task fields read back with Cloud Run's documented defaults (1 task, 3 retries, a 10-minute timeout; asserted in unit `TestJobRunsAsABatchJob`). `etag` is the ConfigMap's `resourceVersion`, and a stale one on update, delete or run is **`ABORTED`**, as for services (not measured against Google). `UpdateJob` replaces the whole job and bumps `generation`; `allow_missing` creates; `validate_only` writes nothing (unit, on create). `DeleteJob` deletes every execution of the job too. A job under another project or location is NOT_FOUND. `executionCount` counts the executions that **still exist**; Cloud Run may keep counting deleted ones. |
| `RunJob` | **Verified** | `TestRunJobLifecycle`: a two-task job runs as one batch Job with `completions: 2` and `completionMode: Indexed` (asserted on the cluster), each task printing its own `CLOUD_RUN_TASK_INDEX`. `task_count` is `completions`, `parallelism` is `parallelism` (0 runs every task at once), `max_retries` is `backoffLimitPerIndex` (retries per task, as Cloud Run counts them), and the task `timeout` is each pod's `activeDeadlineSeconds` (per attempt). `CLOUD_RUN_JOB`, `CLOUD_RUN_EXECUTION`, `CLOUD_RUN_TASK_INDEX` and `CLOUD_RUN_TASK_COUNT` are set; **`CLOUD_RUN_TASK_ATTEMPT` is not**, since no pod field counts its retries. The operation's metadata is the execution from the start, and it completes when the execution does: with the execution on success, and on failure with an error carrying the failing task's message (code FAILED_PRECONDITION, not measured against Google). Overrides of `args`, `env`, `task_count` and `timeout` apply to that execution only (`TestRunJobFailureAndCancel`; unit `TestRunJobOverridesAndEtags`). `secretKeyRef` is verified by `TestRunJobReadsASecretManagerSecret`, which also asserts the batch Job carries the reference, not the payload. |
| `GetExecution`, `ListExecutions` | **Verified** | `TestRunJobLifecycle`. Read from the batch Job's status: `runningCount` is `active`, `succeededCount` is `succeeded`, `failedCount` the tasks in `failedIndexes`, `retriedCount` the other failed pods. Conditions are `Completed` and `Started`; `reconciling` is true until the execution ends. Listed newest first; a missing job is NOT_FOUND. The execution's `template` is the one it ran with, recorded on the batch Job. |
| A failed task | **Verified** | `TestRunJobFailureAndCancel`: a container that exits 3 yields `Completed` = `CONDITION_FAILED`, `executionReason` `NON_ZERO_EXIT_CODE`, and a message naming the task, the container, the exit code and **the container's own output** (the container's termination message is `FallbackToLogsOnError`, so the tail of its log is kept). A task timeout reports the pod's `DeadlineExceeded` the same way (unit `TestExecutionHelpers` only). |
| `CancelExecution` | **Verified** | `TestRunJobFailureAndCancel`: a running execution is cancelled by suspending its batch Job, which stops its pods; the operation completes when none is running, with the unfinished tasks in `cancelledCount` and `executionReason` `CANCELLED` (`CANCELLING` while pods stop). Cancelling an execution that has ended is FAILED_PRECONDITION (unit only; not measured against Google). |
| `DeleteExecution` | **Verified** | `TestRunJobLifecycle`: the batch Job and its pods are deleted, running or not. |
| `ListTasks`, `GetTask` | **Verified** | `TestRunTasksAreAnExecutionsPods` (#1223), with the official `run.TasksClient`: an execution of two tasks lists one task per index, named `{execution}-task{index}`, in index order. A task is the pods the batch controller made for its completion index, one per attempt: `retried` is the attempts after the first, `start_time` the newest attempt's container start, `completion_time` its container's finish, `scheduled_time` its pod's creation, and `last_attempt_result` the newest finished attempt's exit code, signal and status (OK, or UNKNOWN with the failing container's message, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED for a task timeout). Conditions are `Completed` and `Started`: a failed attempt with retries left keeps `Completed` pending, the last one fails it with `NON_ZERO_EXIT_CODE`, and a task the execution ended before (cancelled, or stopped by another task's failure) is `CANCELLED`. `containers`, `max_retries`, `timeout`, labels and annotations are the execution's. `log_uri` is Google's Logs Explorer link for the task's entries (Logs, `logUri`, below; #1379); the console's task page shows its pods' logs. A task beyond the count, or under another execution, is NOT_FOUND; paging is unit-tested (`TestTasksAreReadFromTheExecutionsPods`). |
| Refused fields | **Verified** | The task template's Cloud Storage and NFS `volumes` and `nodeSelector`, a container's `dependsOn`, `readinessProbe`, `baseImageUri` and `sourceCode`, are refused by **the same check as a service's template**, in the same words, prefixed `template.template.`; so are `startExecutionToken`/`runExecutionToken`, `gpuZonalRedundancyDisabled`, and a job container's `ports`, `startupProbe` and `livenessProbe`, which a task has no use for. All UNIMPLEMENTED naming the field (`TestRunJobFailureAndCancel` for `nodeSelector` through the SDK, `TestRunJobSubPathAndStoredSettings` for `gcs` and `nfs`; unit `TestJobRefusesWhatItDoesNotMap` for the rest). `vpcAccess`, `encryptionKey`, `executionEnvironment`, `binaryAuthorization` and a mount's `subPath` are stored, and `subPath` mapped (#1346; "Stored settings" above); a Cloud SQL volume is served (#1346; "Cloud SQL volumes" above). |
| `Jobs.GetIamPolicy`, `Jobs.SetIamPolicy`, `Jobs.TestIamPermissions` | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | `TestRunJobIamPolicyIsStoredNotEnforced` (#1216), official `run.JobsClient`, with the same semantics as a service's (above): a policy round-trips with its etag, a stale etag is ABORTED, conditions are UNIMPLEMENTED, and the job's own `etag` is unchanged. `RunJob` does not read it: the test runs the job under a policy that grants `run.jobs.run` to no one. Kept in its own ConfigMap owned by the job's, so it goes with `DeleteJob`. Unit `TestJobIamPolicyIsStoredNotEnforced`. From the console's Permissions tab: `TestConsolePermissionsOnARunServiceAndJob`. |
| `WorkerPools.GetIamPolicy`, `WorkerPools.SetIamPolicy`, `WorkerPools.TestIamPermissions` | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | `TestRunWorkerPoolLifecycle` (#1300), official `run.WorkerPoolsClient`, with a service's and a job's semantics under ADR-0006: a policy round-trips with its etag, a stale etag is ABORTED, conditions are UNIMPLEMENTED, an empty set on a missing pool. Kept in its own ConfigMap owned by the pool's. |
| Logs, `logUri` | **Verified**, *Google's form* | `TestRunV1JobExecutionsAndTasks` (#1379), v1 `status.logUri` and v2 `log_uri`, which are the same: an execution's is Google's Cloud Logging console link, `https://console.cloud.google.com/logs/viewer?project={project}&advancedFilter=…` with the filter `resource.type="cloud_run_job"`, `resource.labels.job_name`, `resource.labels.location` and `labels."run.googleapis.com/execution_name"`, and a task's adds `labels."run.googleapis.com/task_index"`. It is not the CloudBurrow console's Logs Explorer, which takes no Cloud Logging filter; the same filter given to `gcloud logging read` reads the entries locally, which the run log feeder writes under that resource and those labels (#1298). |
| Console screen | **Verified** | `TestConsoleRunJobsCreateExecuteAndCancel` (#785): the console's Jobs page at `/run/jobs`, through this API. See the Console table. |
