## Optional services

Opt-in, and **never started by default** — a developer should not pay memory for databases
they did not ask for. Enable with `--services firestore,datastore,bigtable,spanner`.

These four each wrap a **Google-published emulator**: Firestore, Datastore and Bigtable run the
emulators of the Google Cloud CLI image (`gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/google-cloud-cli`,
digest-pinned), and Spanner Google's own `gcr.io/cloud-spanner-emulator/emulator` (measured
2026-10-16 for the first three, from their pods' images; Spanner's is the digest in
`internal/components/optional.go`). The database is not reimplemented, but some of what each pod
serves is CloudBurrow's own: the call front in each pod (#1288), Firestore's Admin API and
Bigtable's instance admin API (#1331), and the fifteen Bigtable RPCs the front answers itself
(#1206). The other opt-in services are **not** Google emulators: BigQuery runs a community
emulator, built from source with CloudBurrow's patches ([below](#bigquery-is-a-community-emulator);
measured: `goccy/bigquery-emulator v0.8.1-cloudburrow.2`), Cloud SQL runs PostgreSQL or MySQL
([below](#cloud-sql-is-not-an-emulator)) and Memorystore Valkey
([below](#memorystore-is-not-an-emulator)). Each of the four has an official emulator environment
variable, so an application needs no code change to use it.

| Service | Backing component | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Firestore ([every RPC](coverage/firestore.md); Admin API, [every RPC](coverage/firestoreadmin.md)) | Cloud SDK `cloud-firestore-emulator`; the Admin API is CloudBurrow's own, in the pod's call front (#1331) | **Verified** | `TestFirestoreDocumentCRUD`: document CRUD, a `>` query, and a transaction. `TestFirestoreAdminDatabases`, `TestFirestoreAdminIndexes`, `TestFirestoreAdminFields`: databases, indexes and field overrides through the official Admin client (the `FirestoreAdmin` rows below) |
| Datastore ([every RPC](coverage/datastore.md)) | Cloud SDK `cloud-datastore-emulator`, as Firestore in Datastore mode | **Verified** | `TestDatastoreEntityCRUD`: entity CRUD, a filtered query, and a transaction. `TestDatastoreQueriesSeeAFreshWrite`: 50 queries in a row, each made right after its write, all see it. The emulator runs in Firestore-in-Datastore mode, which is strongly consistent like a Datastore database in Google Cloud today. It does not reproduce legacy Datastore's eventually consistent non-ancestor queries. Left at its default (`--consistency=0.9`), about one query in ten missed a fresh write (#371). |
| Bigtable ([every RPC](coverage/bigtable.md)) | Cloud SDK `bigtable` (`cbtemulator`); the instance admin API is CloudBurrow's own, in the pod's front (#1331) | **Verified** | `TestBigtableTableAndRows`: table and column family creation, row write, read, and a filtered scan. `TestBigtableInstancesAndClusters`, `TestBigtableAppProfilesAndInstanceIAM`: instances, clusters, app profiles and instance IAM through the official `InstanceAdminClient` (the `BigtableInstanceAdmin` rows below) |
| Spanner ([every RPC](coverage/spanner.md)) | `cloud-spanner-emulator` 1.5.58 (own image, digest-pinned) | **Verified, host and pod** | `TestSpannerSchemaAndQuery`: instance, database, DDL, write, read, SQL query. `TestSpannerReadWriteTransactionIsAtomic`: a read-modify-write transfer, and an aborted transaction leaving nothing behind. `TestSpannerDatabasesAreIsolated`. `TestSpannerFromInsideAPod`: the same client from a Job, over cluster DNS. Every RPC is classified (#1199): 33 verified through the official clients, 32 refused by the emulator with `UNIMPLEMENTED` (backups, backup schedules, IAM, instance configurations, instance and partition updates, `FetchCacheUpdate`). |

A **Verified** row above is for the RPCs a test exercises, not for the whole service. Each
service's generated page lists every RPC of its protos: an RPC an official-client test issues is
Verified and links that test, and every other RPC is **Unknown**, so nothing is claimed for it.
The RPCs are the ones each client method issues, read from the pinned client libraries: Firestore's
`DocumentRef.Get` is `BatchGetDocuments` and `Set` and `Delete` are `Commit`; Datastore's `Get` is
`Lookup` and `Put` and `Delete` are non-transactional `Commit`s; Bigtable's `ReadRow` is `ReadRows`
and an unconditional `Apply` is `MutateRow`; Spanner's `NewClient` creates a multiplexed session
with `CreateSession`, and a mutation-only `Apply` is `BeginTransaction` then `Commit`. A result a
test ignores (a cleanup's `DeleteTable` or `DeleteInstance`) claims nothing. Bigtable's instance
admin service is listed on its page since #1331, and waiting on an admin operation polls `google.longrunning.Operations`,
which no page lists.

| RPCs a test exercises | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|

The emulator does not serve PartitionQuery (it answered `UNIMPLEMENTED`); the call front in the Firestore pod answers it (`internal/queryfront`), over gRPC and REST, from the emulator's `RunQuery` over the collection group selecting `__name__` alone (at `read_time` when given): at most `partition_count` cursors, each a document reference, evenly spaced in name order, none when there are too few documents to split, paged by `page_size` and `page_token`. A query Google does not partition (not a collection group, a filter, limit, offset, cursor, or an order other than `__name__` ascending) is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. **Difference:** Google may return fewer cursors than asked, choosing its split points from its storage; this returns as many as asked whenever the group has more documents than that, so its partitions can be smaller than Google's |

The Firestore Admin API is not the emulator's, which serves the documents API alone and answered every admin call 404: the call front in the Firestore pod serves it itself (`internal/firestoreadmin`), over gRPC and over REST on the same port, keeping its state in memory as the emulator keeps its documents, and passes every other call to the emulator. `(default)` is described for every project (`FIRESTORE_NATIVE`, location `nam5`, `PESSIMISTIC` concurrency, Standard edition, point-in-time recovery and delete protection off, a one-hour version retention) until it is deleted. CreateDatabase makes a named Native mode database: the emulator serves any database ID it is sent, each with its own documents (measured), so the created database is the emulator's database of that ID, and the official client writes and reads a document in it. A taken ID is `ALREADY_EXISTS`, an ID outside Google's rule (4 to 63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens) and a missing location `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; Datastore mode, the Enterprise edition and CMEK answer `UNIMPLEMENTED`, naming why. UpdateDatabase changes concurrency mode, point-in-time recovery (enabled, the version retention is seven days), App Engine integration and delete protection; DeleteDatabase is `FAILED_PRECONDITION` while delete protection is on, and otherwise deletes the database's documents through the emulator's reset endpoint, after which the client's read is `NOT_FOUND`. Every create, update and delete returns a done long-running operation with Google's metadata type, which `google.longrunning.Operations` (Get, List, Delete, Cancel) serves. **Differences:** a project's documents can be written to a database ID that was never created, which Google would refuse; the location is stored, not served from. |

A managed export would have to be written to the instance's Cloud Storage in Firestore's own export format, which is not documented well enough to write faithfully; the emulator's own export (`--export-on-exit`) is not that format either. The emulator keeps no backups or versions to restore or clone from, and user credentials are for Firestore with MongoDB compatibility. |
| `Datastore.Commit`, `Datastore.Lookup`, `Datastore.RunQuery`, `Datastore.BeginTransaction` | **Verified** | `TestDatastoreEntityCRUD`; `Commit` and `RunQuery` also `TestDatastoreQueriesSeeAFreshWrite` |
| `Datastore.AllocateIds`, `Datastore.ReserveIds` | **Verified** | `TestDatastoreAllocateAndReserveIDs` (#1197): two distinct allocated IDs and a reserved one, each written and read back |
| `Datastore.Rollback` | **Verified** | `TestDatastoreRollback` (#1197): a rolled-back transaction's `Put` is absent and the transaction can no longer commit |

**Fifteen Bigtable RPCs would crash the emulator**, so CloudBurrow answers them itself (#1206):
the backup methods, the schema bundle methods, `UndeleteTable` and the change stream reads.
`bttest` embeds a nil server for them, so a call panicked it: measured before #1206, the client saw
`UNAVAILABLE` "error reading from server: EOF", the pod restarted, and every table was lost. The
Bigtable pod now runs `cloudburrow-storage bigtable-front` (`internal/bigtablefront`) before the
emulator, which listens on the pod's loopback alone: it answers those fifteen `UNIMPLEMENTED` and
passes every other call through, each message undecoded.

**Firestore, Bigtable and Spanner are in-memory; Datastore keeps its data in persistent mode.**
CloudBurrow provisions no volume for the three, and `status` lists them as never surviving a
restart, whatever `--mode` says. Datastore has a volume in persistent mode, and `status` says it
survives a restart then (how, below). Measured 2026-10-16 across a whole-instance
restart: on `up --mode persistent --services datastore,firestore,bigtable`, an entity, a Firestore
document and a Bigtable table were written with the official Go clients; after `cloudburrow stop`
and the same `up`, the entity read back, the document was `NOT_FOUND` and the table list was empty.

For Spanner this is now **measured rather than quoted**: `TestSpannerStateDoesNotSurviveARestart`
writes a row, restarts the pod, waits for the endpoint to come back, and reads —

```
after the restart the data is gone: spanner: code = "NotFound",
desc = "Instance not found: projects/.../instances/cb-durab"
```

The test fails rather than passes if the endpoint does not return, because an unreachable
address is not evidence about durability. It is on CI's [retry-once list](#retried-once), so this
evidence tolerates one retry.

**Datastore keeps its data in persistent mode, measured (#307).** In persistent mode the
emulator's on-disk store is on a PersistentVolumeClaim, and the emulator's JVM is the container's
main process. The Cloud SDK emulator writes its store only when it shuts down cleanly, and both
`gcloud beta emulators datastore start` and the `cloud_datastore_emulator` script run the JVM as
a child that never receives the pod's SIGTERM, so under the wrapper an entity written before a
pod restart was lost. In ephemeral mode it runs through the wrapper with `--no-store-on-disk`,
as it always did. The emulator loads its store when it starts, and a deleted pod's replacement,
which the ReplicaSet starts at once on the same volume, could load it before the old JVM had
even been signalled to save: with the call front in the pod (#1288) the entity written last was
lost in three runs of three (#1307). So the running JVM holds an exclusive `flock` on
`/data/datastore.lock` on the volume, and the next pod's emulator waits for it (its log says
`waiting for the previous emulator to save /data/datastore`) until the old one has saved and
exited; measured, five of nine pod restarts waited, and every one kept its data.
`TestDatastoreSurvivesAPodRestart` writes an entity with the Go client,
deletes the pod, and reads every entity written so far back from the new one, three times over.
A pod that is killed rather than stopped (OOM, node loss) still loses what was written since it
started. CI's restart probe reads a probe entity after `stop` and `up` in persistent mode, and
finds none after `up --mode ephemeral` (`TestDatastoreAcrossRestart`). Both tests are on CI's
[retry-once list](#retried-once), so this evidence tolerates one retry. `status` reports `volume` for Datastore, and for every
other service, only in persistent mode. That Firestore and Bigtable lose their data is measured
above (2026-10-16), not in CI.

[Cloud Logging](coverage/logging.md), [Vertex AI PredictionService](coverage/vertexai.md), [Pub/Sub](coverage/pubsub.md), the
[Storage JSON API](coverage/storage.md), the [Storage gRPC API](coverage/storagegrpc.md) (#1321) and the opt-in [Firestore](coverage/firestore.md),

[Spanner](coverage/spanner.md) emulators with its status, and every REST method of

[Cloud SQL Admin API](coverage/sqladmin.md) (#1301) and of the [Service Usage API](coverage/serviceusage.md) (#1352), and every RPC of the [Firestore Admin API](coverage/firestoreadmin.md) the Firestore call front serves (#1331), and links each Verified one to the compat
test that proves it. CI fails when it is stale. `TestCoverageMatchesCompatibility`
(`tools/coverage`) fails when a row of this document that names one of those methods gives it a
status the generated page does not, when a method the page calls Verified or Implemented is named
in no row of its section, or when a page is not linked here, and
`TestCompatibilityCitesOnlyDefinedTests` fails when a row cites a `Test*` or `test_*` name no test
in the repository defines. The statuses correspond as that test documents: **Verified** is
Verified; **Partial** is Verified or Implemented; **Implemented** is Implemented;
**Unimplemented**, **Refused**, **Not supported** and **Verified unsupported** are Unimplemented or
Refused; Planned is Unimplemented, Refused or Not served; **Not served** is Not served.

### BigQuery is a community emulator

`--services bigquery` runs [`goccy/bigquery-emulator`](https://github.com/goccy/bigquery-emulator)
0.8.1 (MIT), **built by CloudBurrow from its source with patches to the SQL engine it links**
(#1061): the CLI embeds linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 builds made from Go modules pinned and
checked by checksum, and `up` builds its image locally; nothing is pulled but the digest-pinned
base. The patches fix table functions (#1043, #1047), `DROP TABLE FUNCTION` (#976), a RECORD
inside a REPEATED RECORD (#900, upstream's open goccy/googlesqlite#76), a FLOAT64 NaN (#1066)
and an infinity inside an ARRAY or STRUCT (#1077), BYTES that are not UTF-8 text (#1075), the
`-` operator on a column, the engine's memory past 2 GiB (#989), its growth through DDL
(#1057, upstream's open goccy/googlesqlite#80), functions of another dataset (#1107, #1123) and by
one quoted path (#1122), INTERVAL signs and comparison (#1126, #1120), NULL arguments (#1109,
#1121), GEOGRAPHY text (#1119) and REPEATED fields a row leaves out (#1124); [third_party/bigquery-emulator/PROVENANCE.md](../third_party/bigquery-emulator/PROVENANCE.md)
lists each. Where a row below says "the pinned emulator" or "measured first", it was measured
against the unpatched v0.8.1. **Google publishes no BigQuery
emulator**, so this is the one opt-in backend that is neither Google's nor the real engine. It runs
ZetaSQL, so it accepts GoogleSQL, but the only fidelity claimed is what is listed below.

Rows are read when `ReadRows` asks, not as a snapshot at the session's creation; each `ReadRows` is one query, whose result the emulator keeps with its job (in memory) until it restarts. Units `TestStorageReadRowsAreWrittenByTheFront`, `TestStorageReadRowsInBatches`, `TestStorageReadRefusesWhatWouldCrashTheEmulator`, `TestArrowIsFramedAsBigQueryFramesIt`. |

In BigQuery a read session names its table by project, dataset and table ([ReadSession](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/storage/rpc/google.cloud.bigquery.storage.v1#readsession)). The emulator names the schema's record by the namespace `<project>.<dataset>` and the table (`TableToAVRO`, `types/avro.go`), and an Avro name may hold only letters, digits and `_` ([names](https://avro.apache.org/docs/1.11.1/specification/#names)); a RECORD's record is named after its column, so two RECORD columns of one name at different depths were two records of one name, which Avro refuses too. Now the session's schema is the emulator's with every name made valid (a character a name may not have becomes `_`, a leading digit gets a `_` before it, a record whose name another has gets `_2`, `_3`…; field names, types and order unchanged), and the front writes the rows in it, in Avro's binary encoding, as it does Arrow's (row *Storage Read API, Arrow*). The emulator writes the session's Arrow schema and each batch as whole IPC streams (schema, batch, end-of-stream), where BigQuery sends the schema's message and each batch's ([ArrowRecordBatch](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/storage/rpc/google.cloud.bigquery.storage.v1#arrowrecordbatch)), and the Go client reads a batch after the schema, so it read the schema's empty batch and stopped. The Storage Read front now sends them framed as BigQuery's, for every session (`TestBigQueryStorageReadAPIStreamsArrowRows` still streams its four rows); since #1095 it writes the batches itself (row *Storage Read API, Arrow*). The Go client reads the Storage Read API in Arrow only. |
| Storage Write API (`cloud.google.com/go/bigquery/storage/managedwriter`): the default stream and `COMMITTED`, `PENDING` and `BUFFERED` streams; `CreateWriteStream`, `AppendRows`, `GetWriteStream`, `FinalizeWriteStream`, `BatchCommitWriteStreams`, `FlushRows` | **Verified**, every column type below, `RANGE` (#1391; next row), `REPEATED` columns and RECORDs; **Not implemented** (501) where the row after next says | `TestBigQueryStorageWriteDefaultStreamOfEveryType`, `TestBigQueryStorageWriteCommittedStreamsKeepTheirTables`, `TestBigQueryStorageWritePendingStreamCommitsOnce` and `TestBigQueryStorageWriteBufferedStreamFlushesOnce` (#1102), official managed writer, each stream's rows read back with the official Go client's `Table.Read`. A row of `INT64`, `FLOAT64`, `NUMERIC` and `BIGNUMERIC` (BigDecimalByteStringEncoder's bytes), `BOOL`, `STRING`, `BYTES`, `DATE` (days), `DATETIME` and `TIME` (CivilTimeEncoder's packed `int64`), `TIMESTAMP` (microseconds), `JSON`, `GEOGRAPHY`, a RECORD holding a `TIMESTAMP` and a `REPEATED STRING`, `REPEATED INT64`, `REPEATED TIMESTAMP` and a `REPEATED RECORD`, and a row of `NULL`s and empty arrays, read back as written; the conversions are BigQuery's table of protocol buffer types ([supported data types](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/supported-data-types)). A default stream's results carry no offset; a stream's result offset is the append's first row, an offset already written is `ALREADY_EXISTS` and one past the end `OUT_OF_RANGE`; two `COMMITTED` streams of two tables appended in turn, and two default streams on one multiplexed connection, each write to their own table; `Finalize` counts the rows and an append after it fails; a `PENDING` stream's rows are in the table only after `BatchCommitWriteStreams`, a stream not finalized is a stream error and nothing is committed, a second commit is `STREAM_ALREADY_COMMITTED`; a `BUFFERED` stream's rows are in the table up to each `FlushRows` offset, once each. **Measured first against the pinned emulator, to which the front passed the Write API: the rows after an `AppendRows` connection's first request, which the managed writer sends without `write_stream`, landed in another table; a `NUMERIC` was stored as 0, a packed `DATETIME` as `6483-06-17T05:36:51.664`; each result had the wrong offset, an offset already written was accepted again, and `FlushRows` past the rows crashed the emulator.** So the front serves the Write API itself and never calls the emulator's: it keeps each stream and writes its rows through its own `tabledata.insertAll`, whose checks every row has. **A restart of the front's container keeps every stream**, its offset, and the rows a `PENDING` stream holds until its commit and a `BUFFERED` one until its flush (#1115): the front keeps them in files on an emptyDir of the BigQuery pod, as the Pub/Sub front keeps its state (#898). `TestBigQueryStorageWriteStreamsOutliveAFrontRestart`, official managed writer: rows appended to a `PENDING`, a `BUFFERED` and a `COMMITTED` stream, the front's container stopped alone, then each stream found by `GetWriteStream`, reopened by name, appended to at its next offset, committed and flushed, every row in its table once (unit `TestStorageWriteStreamsOutliveAFrontRestart`, which also shows an append torn between its rows and its state is ignored). **A restart of the pod loses them**, with the emulator's tables: a stream made before is then `NOT_FOUND` (the default stream is always there). A `FlushRows` or commit whose rows reached the table just before the front's process ended, and whose state had not been written, writes them again when the client retries it. |

The front sends each variable a script declares under a name of its own for that request (`renameVariables`), renaming exactly the words the engine would replace, so the script reads its variables as before (`DECLARE`, `DEFAULT` from an earlier variable, `SET`: 10 and 9 read back) and a later query gets "Unrecognized name: zz", and an alias `w` is an alias. Measured against the pinned emulator: **through `jobs.query`** it runs a script in one transaction and rolls all of it back (`CREATE TABLE ds.e1 AS SELECT 1 AS a; SELECT * FROM nope.nope; CREATE TABLE ds.e2 …` failed 400 and `ds.e1` did not exist; the same for `INSERT`, and for a runtime error, `ERROR('boom')`); **as a query job** it commits what the statements before the failing one did, as it records the failed job in the script's transaction (after `INSERT INTO ds.t VALUES (9); SELECT * FROM nope.nope`, `ds.t` had the row; through `jobs.query`, it did not), and the job fails with the statement's error. So a script whose statements before its last include a query (`SELECT`, `WITH`, a parenthesized query) is carried out by the front as a script with control flow is (`internal/bigqueryfront/scriptflow.go`, `earlierQuery`): each statement is a request of its own, and the script fails at the first that fails, with that statement's error (read back: the row of the `INSERT` before it kept, the one after it not run). A `TEMP` table or function lasts only for the request that made it, so such a script cannot be split: 501. (`ASSERT`: row below, #1253.) Since #1201 a transaction the front carries out has each statement probed, so its queries' errors are seen (row `Multi-statement transactions`). Measured first against the pinned emulator, through the front: `ASSERT FALSE` answered done with no rows and `ASSERT FALSE; SELECT 1` the row `1`; the emulator does not check an `ASSERT` at all. BigQuery fails the query when the expression is `FALSE` or `NULL`, with the description in the error message ([debugging statements](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/debugging-statements#assert)). So a script with an `ASSERT`, or a lone one, is carried out by the front, as a script with a query before its last is (row above; `scriptflow.go`, `assert`): it runs `SELECT (expression)` as a query of its own; `TRUE` goes on, `FALSE` or `NULL` fails the query 400 `invalidQuery` with `Assertion failed: ` and the description, or the expression's text without one (the reference says only that the description appears in the message, and its examples show the description alone after `Error:`; the `Assertion failed: ` prefix is not quoted there, so a test reading the message should match the description). Read back: a runtime error in the expression fails it with that error, the `INSERT` before a failed `ASSERT` is kept and the one after it never runs, an `ASSERT` inside `IF` is checked, a `BEGIN … EXCEPTION` handler catches it with that `@@error.message`, and `ASSERT TRUE; SELECT 2` answers `2`. An expression that is not a `BOOL`, or a description that is not a `STRING` literal, is refused 400. A `TEMP` table or function lasts only for one request, so such a script is 501. | The tables after a failed script | **Verified** for the tables and views a script's `CREATE` and `DROP` statements name, and its `TEMP` tables; functions and `DROP SCHEMA` are the next row | `TestBigQueryFailedScriptLeavesTheCatalogInStep` (#955), official Go client, through `jobs.query` and `jobs.insert`. Measured against the pinned emulator, a failed script left, for every later query, its SQL engine's catalog (goccy/googlesqlite v0.3.1) or its list of tables (`tables.get`, `tables.list`) out of step with its tables. The engine changes its in-memory catalog as each statement runs and reloads it only from catalog rows updated since it last did (`Catalog.Sync`: `WHERE updatedAt >= lastSyncedAt`), so a rollback puts the rows back and not the catalog; the emulator updates its list of tables from a query only when the query succeeded. Through `jobs.query` (rolled back): after `DROP TABLE ds.keep; SELECT * FROM nope.nope`, `ds.keep` was listed and `SELECT a FROM ds.keep` failed "Table not found"; after `CREATE TABLE ds.c1 AS SELECT 1 AS a; …`, `SELECT * FROM ds.c1` failed "sqlite3: SQL logic error: no such table"; after `DROP TABLE ds.keep2; CREATE TABLE ds.keep2 (z STRING); …`, `SELECT a FROM ds.keep2` failed "Unrecognized name: a"; after `CREATE TEMP TABLE ghost AS SELECT 1 AS a; …`, the next `CREATE TEMP TABLE ghost AS SELECT 2 AS b; SELECT b FROM ghost` failed "Unrecognized name: b". As a query job (committed): a dropped table was still listed and not found by a query, and a table made was read by a query and not listed. After a failure the front puts them back with statements of its own (`resyncCatalog`; each measured): rolled back, the catalog is made to match the list (a listed table is taken out of the catalog by a script that drops it and fails, which `jobs.query` rolls back, and added again by `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` from its schema, which leaves the table and its rows; one not listed is dropped `IF EXISTS`); committed, the list is made to match the catalog (a table the engine reads and the list lacks is added again from the engine's columns, which lists it; a listed one the engine lacks is created and dropped, which unlists it; one listed with other columns is patched). Read back through `jobs.query`: `ds.keep` with a STRUCT and an ARRAY, `ds.keep2` and a view as before the scripts, `ds.c1` "not found" and then made again, and a new `ghost` with its own columns; as a query job: `ds.keep` and the view gone, `ds.keep2` listed and read with the new column `z`, `ds.c1` listed and read. The engine's copy of a table put back is made from its schema (names, types, modes, defaults), without its options; the front's statements are recorded by the emulator as jobs, as its other checks are. No upstream issue found (goccy/bigquery-emulator, goccy/googlesqlite, as of 2026-09-28). Unit `TestFailedScriptResyncsTheCatalog`. |
