So, for a script of several statements given to `jobs.query`: each function a `CREATE [OR REPLACE] FUNCTION` makes is looked up before the script runs (calling it with no arguments: "Function not found" or "No matching signature", measured), and when the script fails, each that did not exist is taken out of the catalog again by a script that drops it and fails, which `jobs.query` rolls back: `f(1)` is then "not found", and the same `CREATE FUNCTION` run later makes it with its new body (`f(1)` read 3). A function that existed before is left as it was (`g(1)` still 10). A table function is taken out the same way, with `DROP TABLE FUNCTION`, which the engine CloudBurrow builds carries out (#1061): after `CREATE TABLE FUNCTION ds.tf …; SELECT * FROM nope.nope` (501), `ds.tf(1)` is "not found", and made again it reads its new body; the pinned emulator refused `DROP TABLE FUNCTION` (400 "Statement not supported: DropTableFunctionStatement", and `DROP FUNCTION` of one left it callable, measured), so this was 501 before anything ran. **501**, nothing run: a `DROP [TABLE] FUNCTION` in such a script (the emulator has no `routines.get`, so the function cannot be read to be made again). A query job is sent as it is (`k(1)` read 6 after its failed job). `DROP SCHEMA` the emulator refuses alone and in a script, through both (measured: 400 "currently unsupported DROP SCHEMA statement", and the dataset and its tables were kept), so a failed script never ran one; since #990 the front carries it out through `datasets.delete` after the query succeeds, and keeps the dataset when the script fails (row `DROP SCHEMA` below; this test's 501 for it is gone). `CREATE FUNCTION` of a function that exists, and `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` of one, are the row after it (#986). Units `TestFailedScriptFunctions`, `TestDropSchema`. |
| `DROP SCHEMA` | **Verified** alone and in a script whose other statements do not name the dataset, `CASCADE` and `RESTRICT`, `IF EXISTS`; **Not implemented** (501) where the other statements of a script could see the dataset | `TestBigQueryDropSchema` (#990) and `TestBigQueryDropSchemaCascadeDropsTableFunctions` (#1061), official Go client, through `jobs.query` and `jobs.insert`. BigQuery deletes the dataset, with `CASCADE` its tables, views and functions, and with `RESTRICT` (the default) "only if it's empty. Otherwise, returns an error" ([DDL](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language#drop_schema_statement)). Measured first against the pinned emulator: every `DROP SCHEMA`, `IF EXISTS` of a dataset that does not exist too, was 400 "currently unsupported DROP SCHEMA statement" (501 in the front since #976). Its `datasets.delete` does delete a dataset: without `deleteContents` it refuses one with a table, 400 `resourceInUse` "Dataset project:ds is still in use", and with it the tables go too; it does not count a dataset's functions, and leaves them callable after the dataset is gone (`ds.f(1)` still read 2) until a `DROP FUNCTION`; its engine has no `routines.list` (500 "unsupported") nor `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.ROUTINES`. So the front sends the statement as one that does nothing and, when the query succeeds, deletes the dataset through `datasets.delete` (with `deleteContents` for `CASCADE`) and drops each function it knows in the dataset: one it saw a `CREATE FUNCTION` statement or `routines.insert` make, and, since #1001, one a `CREATE FUNCTION` of the emulator's jobs from before the front started made (the emulator keeps every job and its query in memory while it runs, so a front whose container restarted reads them there: `jobs.list`, then `jobs.get` of each job older than the front, once per project). **Since #1115 a restart of the front's container does not scan again**: what the front knows of the functions, and that it has scanned, is kept in a file on the pod's emptyDir beside the Storage Write streams (unit `TestKnownFunctionsOutliveAFrontRestart`). Measured before: on an instance with 587 jobs, the first `DROP SCHEMA` after a restart of the front's container took 97 seconds, past the Go client's deadline in `TestBigQueryDropSchemaCascadeDropsTableFunctions`. A front that starts without the file (a new pod, whose emulator has no jobs, or an unreadable file) still scans (#1135). Measured for #1001: the engine has no other list of its functions (`routines.get` is 404 even for a function `routines.insert` made, and a GoogleSQL query cannot read the engine's catalog table, "Table not found"), and `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` makes none, since the emulator runs no `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` at all (#1011). **Not found**, and so left callable after `CASCADE` and not counted for `RESTRICT`: a function made through `routines.insert` before the front's container last restarted. Read back: an empty dataset is dropped by `DROP SCHEMA`; one with a table and a function by `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS … CASCADE`, after which the function is "not found" and the dataset made again has no table `t`; `DROP SCHEMA` of one with a table fails `resourceInUse` (400 through `jobs.query`, a failed query job) and the table keeps its row; of one that does not exist, `notFound` (404), or with `IF EXISTS` nothing; `SELECT 1; DROP SCHEMA d CASCADE; SELECT 2` drops it. A dataset whose only content is a function the front saw made fails `DROP SCHEMA` (`RESTRICT`) `resourceInUse` too, and so does one whose only content is a function `Routine.Create` (`routines.insert`) made, which `CASCADE` then drops with it (`TestBigQueryDropSchemaDropsRoutinesInsertFunctions`, #1001; the function called before, "Function not found" after). When the script fails the dataset is kept: `DROP SCHEMA d CASCADE; SELECT * FROM nope.nope` is 501 through `jobs.query` (the emulator rolls the whole script back, #935) and a failed query job answered 501 naming the `DROP SCHEMA`, and `d` is still there. **501**, nothing run: a script whose other statements name the dataset (or whose default dataset it is), a `DROP SCHEMA` in an `EXCEPTION` handler or after a `RETURN`, one that would fail (not found, not empty) after other statements, and anything after the dataset's name other than `CASCADE` or `RESTRICT`. A table function the front knows in the dataset is dropped with `DROP TABLE FUNCTION` since #1061 (501 before: the pinned engine refused it): `RESTRICT` of a dataset holding one fails `resourceInUse`, `CASCADE` drops it, a call is then "not found", and the dataset made again has none (`TestBigQueryDropSchemaCascadeDropsTableFunctions`). Unit `TestDropSchema`, and `TestDropSchemaFindsEveryFunction` (#1001: a function `routines.insert` made, and ones in jobs from before the front started, one named through the job's default dataset; a job after its start is not read). |
| Copy jobs (`Table.CopierFrom`) | **Verified** within the instance's project, one or several sources, every `writeDisposition` and `createDisposition`; `operationType` `CLONE` into a new table, and `SNAPSHOT` and `RESTORE` (#1002, below; the same through DDL, `CREATE TABLE … CLONE` row); Copy table on the console offers each `operationType` (#1002); **Not implemented** (501) where noted | `TestBigQueryCopyJobs` (#987), official Go client. Measured first: the emulator answered a copy job **400** "unspecified job configuration query", `jobInternalError`, and copied nothing (it runs only query, load and extract jobs). The front now carries it out as a job of its own (answered by the front, as the extracts it writes are), with `statistics.copy.copiedRows`: a new destination is made through `tables.insert` with the first source's schema (a DDL `CREATE TABLE` would not keep `REQUIRED`: measured, `NOT NULL` read back `NULLABLE`), made as every `tables.insert` is since #1000, a `FLOAT` column as `FLOAT64` (next row); the rows are written by one `INSERT … SELECT … UNION ALL SELECT …` of the sources. Read back: two sources with a `REQUIRED` column, a `RECORD` with a `REPEATED` field, `FLOAT64`, `TIMESTAMP` with microseconds and `NUMERIC` copied into a new table hold the same rows (`TO_JSON_STRING` of each) and its schema reads back as the sources' (names, types, modes, a description), and takes a `FLOAT64` insert; `jobs.get` and `jobs.list` read the job back. `WRITE_EMPTY` (the default) into a table with rows fails `duplicate` and leaves it; `WRITE_APPEND` adds; `WRITE_TRUNCATE` replaces rows and schema (written to a scratch table first, so a failure keeps the destination; the destination is then deleted and made again from the source's schema); `CREATE_NEVER` of a missing table and a missing source fail `notFound`, and nothing is made; a view as a source fails `invalid`. `operationType` `CLONE` of one table into one that does not exist (#1002): the rows are copied and the destination made with a `cloneDefinition` (the source, and the job's start as `cloneTime`), which the emulator keeps (measured) and `tables.get` reads back; the clone is a writable `TABLE`, and an `INSERT` into it leaves its base as it was (`TestBigQueryCopyJobs`); a later schema change that remakes the table (#1036) does not keep it. **501**, nothing copied: a `SNAPSHOT`, `RESTORE` or `CLONE` of several tables, a `CLONE` into a table that exists (not given by the documentation), `destinationEncryptionConfiguration`, `destinationExpirationTime` into a table that exists (whether it changes that table's expiration is not documented), a table of another project, a `WRITE_APPEND` (or `WRITE_EMPTY` into an empty table) whose destination's schema differs from the source's (BigQuery's rules for which differences it accepts are not in its documentation), a view as the destination, and a dry run (#1002). **`destinationExpirationTime`** (#1002, an RFC 3339 time or milliseconds) is given to a new destination as its `expirationTime`, which `tables.get` reads back: `bq cp --snapshot --expiration=3600` makes a snapshot that expires in an hour (`TestBqCopySnapshotCloneAndRestore`, the real `bq` CLI through the harness, read back by the official Go client, which also reads back `bq cp --clone` and `bq cp --restore`); as for any table's `expirationTime`, the emulator does not delete the table when it passes; a value that is not a time fails `invalid`. Several sources whose schemas are not identical fail the job, `invalid` (BigQuery's documentation: all source tables must have identical schemas; its message is UNVERIFIED), and nothing is copied (#1002). **Why the destination is deleted even when its schema is the source's (#1092, closed):** the front could empty it with `DELETE … WHERE true` and insert the rows, which spares the engine's catalog rebuild of a `DROP TABLE` (*The SQL engine failing* row), only if that gave what BigQuery gives, and BigQuery's documentation does not say what a copy with `WRITE_TRUNCATE` does to the destination's description, labels, expiration or creation time: the copy configuration says only "If the table already exists, BigQuery overwrites the table data and uses the schema and table constraints from the source table" ([JobConfigurationTableCopy.writeDisposition](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationTableCopy)), and Copy tables says "If the copy operation overwrites an existing table, then the table-level access for the existing table is maintained. Tags from the source table aren't copied to the overwritten table, while tags on the existing table are retained" ([managing-tables](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-tables#copy-table)), which the emulator has neither of; row access policies are overwritten and policy tags removed ([row-level-security-intro](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/row-level-security-intro), [column-level-security-intro](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/column-level-security-intro)), which the emulator has neither of either. Whether the destination keeps its own description, labels and expiration or takes none cannot be read, and CloudBurrow does not measure against BigQuery, so the front does not change what it does on a guess. Unit `TestCopyJobs`. |
| Table snapshots: copy jobs with `operationType` `SNAPSHOT` and `RESTORE` | **Verified** (#1002) | `TestBigQuerySnapshotAndRestore`, official Go client. Measured first: the emulator has no snapshots (`CREATE SNAPSHOT TABLE` is 400 "not supported"), and a table made through `tables.insert` with a `snapshotDefinition` reads back type `TABLE`, writable; it does keep the `snapshotDefinition`, and `tables.get` answers it, so the front takes such a table for a snapshot, with nothing kept of its own (`internal/bigqueryfront/snapshots.go`). **`SNAPSHOT`** makes the destination with the source's schema and rows and a `snapshotDefinition` (the source as `baseTableReference`, the job's start as `snapshotTime`); `tables.get` answers it type `SNAPSHOT`, and so does `tables.list` (one `tables.get` per `TABLE` it lists); the source's later writes do not reach it. A `SNAPSHOT` of a snapshot, a view or an external table fails the job `invalid` ("The source table type is TABLE", `OperationType` in the REST reference), and one over a table that exists fails `duplicate` ("You can't overwrite an existing table or table snapshot when you create a table snapshot", [table snapshots](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/table-snapshots-intro)). **Read-only** ("You can only update a table snapshot's metadata"): refused before anything runs are `tabledata.insertAll`, a load, copy or query job into it (`destinationTable`), `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MERGE`, `TRUNCATE TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE` and `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` of it, in a script too (a name without a dataset is read in the default dataset), and a `tables.patch` or `tables.update` that changes its schema; a description update is carried out, and the rows are kept. BigQuery's documentation gives neither the status nor the message of these refusals: the front answers **400** `invalid` (`invalidQuery` for a query, a failed job for a query job), UNVERIFIED. **`RESTORE`** copies a snapshot into a standard, writable table, with any `writeDisposition` (`WRITE_TRUNCATE` over its base takes it back); of a table that is not a snapshot it fails `invalid` ("The source table type is SNAPSHOT"). A `COPY` of a snapshot into a new table makes a snapshot of the same base ("The source and destination table have the same table type"). **The Storage Write API** into a snapshot is refused too, since #1002: `CreateWriteStream` of one (any type), and the first `AppendRows` of a connection to its `_default` stream, are `INVALID_ARGUMENT` before any row is taken, and the snapshot keeps its rows (`TestBigQueryStorageWriteRefusesSnapshots`, official managed writer; code and wording UNVERIFIED). **Left as they are:** `DROP TABLE` of a snapshot is passed to the emulator, which deletes it: BigQuery's DDL reference says `DROP TABLE` "Deletes a table or table clone" and gives `DROP SNAPSHOT TABLE` for snapshots, but does not say a `DROP TABLE` of a snapshot fails (`DROP SNAPSHOT TABLE` deletes a snapshot since #1002, and `CREATE SNAPSHOT TABLE` makes one: the `CREATE TABLE … CLONE` row). **501:** a `CLONE` into a table that exists (the docs say only "If the table clone overwrites an existing table…", with no `writeDisposition` rule), and a `SNAPSHOT`, `CLONE` or `RESTORE` of several sources (the REST reference's `OperationType` speaks of one source). Unit `TestCopyJobs`, `TestStorageWriteRefusesSnapshots`. |
| `CREATE [TABLE] FUNCTION` of a function that exists, and `CREATE OR REPLACE [TABLE] FUNCTION` | **Verified** for a query's first statement and a lone `CREATE OR REPLACE`, for functions and table functions; **Not implemented** (501) after other statements of a script, and for `CREATE OR REPLACE` in a script of several statements | `TestBigQueryCreateFunctionOfAnExistingFunction` (#986), official Go client, through `jobs.query` (`Query.Read`) and `jobs.insert` (`Query.Run`). BigQuery: `CREATE FUNCTION` of a function that exists fails "Already Exists", `OR REPLACE` replaces it and `IF NOT EXISTS` does nothing ([DDL](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language#create_function_statement)). Measured first against the pinned emulator: `CREATE FUNCTION ds.h(x INT64) AS (x + 1)` then `… AS (x + 2)` **succeeded** and `SELECT ds.h(1)` still read 2; `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION ds.h … (x + 3)` succeeded and `h(1)` **still read 2**; so for `CREATE [OR REPLACE] TABLE FUNCTION`; `IF NOT EXISTS` did nothing; `DROP FUNCTION` took one out, and a function whose body does not analyse was not made. The front looks the function up before the query runs (calling it with no arguments: "Function not found", or "No matching signature" or "Table-valued function is not expected here" when it exists, measured). Now: `CREATE FUNCTION` of one that exists as the query's first statement fails **409** `duplicate` through `jobs.query`, and as a query job the job fails `duplicate` (the emulator is sent a statement that does nothing so it records the job; `jobs.get` shows the client's text), and `h(1)` still reads 2; `IF NOT EXISTS` still does nothing; a lone `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` is carried out, through both: the statement is first run under a scratch name in the same dataset, then that and the old function are dropped (`DROP FUNCTION`) and the statement is sent, so `h(1)` read 11, then 12; one whose body does not analyse fails with the engine's error and `h(1)` still read 12. **501**, nothing run: `CREATE FUNCTION` of one that exists (or that the script made) after other statements of a script (BigQuery runs those and fails there; the emulator cannot be stopped in between), `CREATE OR REPLACE [TABLE] FUNCTION` of one that exists in a script of several statements. **Table functions** (#1047, #1061), the same test: `CREATE TABLE FUNCTION ds.tf` of one that exists fails 409 `duplicate`, and as a query job `duplicate`; `IF NOT EXISTS` does nothing (`tf(1)` still 1); a lone `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE FUNCTION` is carried out as a function's is, through both, the old one dropped with `DROP TABLE FUNCTION` (which the engine CloudBurrow builds carries out; the pinned one refused it, so this was 501), `tf(1)` then 11, then 12; one whose body does not analyse fails and keeps it; in a script, 501. A `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` of a table function, or the reverse, drops the old one by its own kind (unit). A TEMP function is not looked up. Unit `TestCreateFunctionOfAnExistingFunction`. |
| `FLOAT` columns (`bigquery.FloatFieldType`) | **Verified** for tables made through `tables.insert`, loads with a schema and CSV loads with autodetect | `TestBigQueryFloatColumnsTakeFloat64` (#1000), official Go client. In BigQuery `FLOAT` and `FLOAT64` are one 64-bit type ([TableFieldSchema.type](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/tables#TableFieldSchema.FIELDS.type)), and the Go client sends `FLOAT` for every float field. Measured first against the pinned emulator: a `FLOAT` column made through `tables.insert` was its engine's 32-bit `FLOAT`, which refused every `FLOAT64` value (400 "Value has type DOUBLE which cannot be inserted into column f, which has type FLOAT": `CAST(0.1 AS FLOAT64)`, a `FLOAT64` query parameter, `INSERT … SELECT` of a `FLOAT64` column, a `STRUCT` with a `FLOAT64` field into a `RECORD` with a `FLOAT` one); so was one a load's schema or a CSV load with autodetect made. An untyped literal and `tabledata.insertAll` were accepted, and read back without losing precision (`0.30000000000000004`, `1.7976931348623157e308` and `123456789.12345679` as sent). `INTEGER`, `BOOLEAN` and `RECORD` are the engine's `INT64`, `BOOL` and `STRUCT` (measured: `CAST(9007199254740993 AS INT64)` and a `BOOL` inserted), and are sent as they are; a field sent by its GoogleSQL name (`FLOAT64` among them) is sent by its legacy name since #1034 (row *GoogleSQL type names in a schema*), so a `FLOAT64` field is made `FLOAT64` in the engine and reads back `FLOAT`. Now the front sends `tables.insert` and a load's schema with each `FLOAT` field (at any depth) as `FLOAT64`, and then sets the schema back to the client's through `tables.patch`, which changes only what `tables.get` reads; a CSV load with autodetect into a new table that detected a `FLOAT` column is made again with it `FLOAT64` and its rows copied in (a scratch table first, as a copy job's `WRITE_TRUNCATE`; if that fails, the load job fails `backendError` naming why). Read back through the Go client: a table with a `FLOAT` column and a `RECORD` with a `FLOAT` field reads back `FLOAT`, and takes `0.1`, `0.30000000000000004`, `1.7976931348623157e308`, `-2.2250738585072014e-308`, `16777217`, `123456789.12345679`, `5e-324` and `-1e300` through `INSERT` with a `FLOAT64` parameter (the column and the struct field), `CAST(0.1 AS FLOAT64)`, `INSERT … SELECT` from a DDL `FLOAT64` table (a query job), `Inserter.Put` and a CSV load appending, and every value reads back exactly (`float64` equality); a table made by a load with that schema, and one by a CSV load with autodetect, read back `f FLOAT` and take a `FLOAT64` `INSERT`. A `FLOAT` column that `tables.update` or `tables.patch` adds is made `FLOAT64` the same way, as the front makes the table again through `tables.insert` to add it (#1010, the schema-update row below). Unit `TestFloatColumnsAreMadeFloat64`. |
| Tables of one ID in two datasets: `tabledata.list`, queries with a `defaultDataset`, DML, loads, extracts | **Verified** | `TestBigQuerySameTableIDInTwoDatasets` and `TestBigQueryExtractReadsItsOwnTable` (#1015), official Go client for both services. In BigQuery a table is named by its project, dataset and table ID, and a query's table name without a dataset is in its default dataset. Measured first against the pinned emulator, with `b1.same (s STRING)` made first and `b2.same (a INT64)` after: `tabledata.list` of `b2.same` answered `b1.same`'s rows (the Go client's `Table.Read` failed "schema length does not match row length"); with `b2` the default dataset, `SELECT * FROM same` read `b1.same`, `INSERT INTO same (a)` failed "Column a is not present in table …_b1_same", and `DELETE FROM same WHERE true` and `TRUNCATE TABLE same` emptied `b1.same`; with no default dataset, `SELECT * FROM same` read `b1.same`. The cause, read in the pinned source: its engine (goccy/googlesqlite v0.3.1) registers each table in its catalog under every suffix of its path, the bare table ID included, only when no table holds that name yet, and resolves a table name only in that catalog, so a bare ID names the first table of that ID made in any dataset; the emulator's `tabledata.list` and extract jobs read `` SELECT * FROM `<tableId>` ``. Now the front sends each table name a query gives without a dataset (after `FROM`, `JOIN`, a comma in a `FROM` clause, `MERGE … USING`, and the tables of `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MERGE`, `TRUNCATE TABLE`, `CREATE TABLE`/`VIEW` and `DROP TABLE`/`VIEW`; not a CTE's or a script's `TEMP` table's, and not one in a `CREATE VIEW`'s query, which is refused (#1049, the row *A view's table names without a dataset*)) as `` `dataset.table` `` of the default dataset, through `jobs.query` and query jobs (`jobs.get` shows the client's text); answers `tabledata.list` itself, paged as BigQuery pages it (`maxResults`, `startIndex`, `pageToken`: `Table.Read` a row a page reads every row; the emulator pages nothing), with the rows of a `SELECT *` of `dataset.table` when another dataset has a table of the ID (it looks through `datasets.list` and `tables.list`, below), else with the emulator's own read, which is then of this table; and writes a CSV extract of such a table itself. Read back through the Go client, each table's rows are its own after `Table.Read`, `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MERGE`, a query job, a CSV load appending, `TRUNCATE TABLE` and an extract. **A table name with no dataset in a query with no default dataset is 400** `invalid` "Table "same" must be qualified with a dataset (e.g. dataset.table)." in the query's first statement (a failed job for `jobs.insert`), BigQuery's message (its wording as the Go client gives it is UNVERIFIED against BigQuery); in a later statement of a script it is sent in a dataset that does not exist, so the statements before it run and it fails ("Table not found: `_cloudburrow_no_default_dataset.same`"). `tabledata.list` with `selectedFields` keeps the cells named itself (the emulator returned every column), top-level and nested (`a.b`, also inside a REPEATED RECORD), in the schema's order, names case-insensitive; a name the schema lacks is 400 `invalid` (#1038, unit `TestSelectedFields`; the order and the 400 are UNVERIFIED against BigQuery). The emulator's Storage Read API reads a table by its bare ID too (read through a view of the front's since #1046), and a view made through `tables.insert` whose query names a table without a dataset read the first table of that ID: both are the rows *Storage Read API of a table whose ID another dataset has* (#1032) and *A view's table names without a dataset* (#1035) below. A function name without a dataset is not changed (#1033). **Cost (#1063):** which table IDs more than one dataset has is read once with `datasets.list` and one `tables.list` a dataset, the front's own datasets (the query results dataset, #1017, and the Storage Read views' dataset) left out, and kept until a request that may make, delete or rename a table (any but a read, or a query of one lone `SELECT` with no destination), or the emulator restarting; a page of such a table is read by `LIMIT` and `OFFSET` of `SELECT *` of `dataset.table`, in the engine's storage order, with the table's `numRows` as `totalRows`, rather than the whole table per page. Before, each request asked `tables.get` of the ID in every other dataset and read the whole table. Measured on my own instance (arm64, `--services storage,bigquery`), each time in a run of the whole BigQuery compat suite and then alone after it on the same instance: before, `TestBigQuerySameTableIDInTwoDatasets` took 78.7 s in the suite (its five checks 8.8–17.8 s each) and 143.7 s after it (18.4–34.8 s each); after, 46.3 s in the suite (3.2–7.6 s each) and 3.3 s after it (0.19–0.36 s each). The before run left 10 datasets on the instance and the after run 1, so the two late runs did not start from the same state. The test still gives each step a context of its own (#1051). Units `TestTableDataListPagesByQueryAndKeepsTheSharedIDs`, `TestTableIDsMayChange`, `TestTableIDsAreNotKeptAcrossAChange`, Units `TestTableNamesAreQualified`, `TestQueriesAreSentQualified`, `TestTableDataListReadsTheWholeName`. |
| Function names without a dataset in a query with a `defaultDataset` | **Verified** for a persistent function the front knows (made by a `CREATE FUNCTION` it sent on, `routines.insert` through it, or the script), and since #1107 for a call of another dataset's function beside the default dataset's, in a query, DML, a script, DDL and beside `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` or `@@dataset_id` (#1123), and since #1122 for a call by one quoted path (`` `project.dataset.fn` ``) | `TestBigQueryFunctionNameInTheDefaultDataset` (#1033), official Go client (`Query.DefaultDatasetID`, `Query.Run`, `Client.JobFromID`). In BigQuery the default dataset is "the default dataset to use for unqualified table names in the query … Setting the system variable `@@dataset_id` achieves the same behavior" ([JobConfigurationQuery.defaultDataset](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationQuery.FIELDS.default_dataset)), `@@dataset_id` "is used when a dataset is not specified for a project in the query" ([system variables](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/system-variables)), and a persistent function must be named with its dataset only "from another persistent UDF or a logical view" ([persistent UDF limitations](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/user-defined-functions)). The emulator's engine registers a function under its bare name only when no function holds it yet, as a table (#1015), and never reads the default dataset for one. Measured first against the pinned emulator, with `one.fn(x) AS (x + 1)` made first and `two.fn(x) AS (x + 2)`: `SELECT fn(0)` with the default dataset `two` failed 400 "failed to query SELECT fn(0): sqlite3: SQL logic error: no such column: <project>"; `SELECT two.fn(0)` read 2. So the front sends a call without a dataset of a function the default dataset has as `dataset.name`, and leaves a built-in's name (the engine takes `SAFE.` only for a built-in, measured), a `TEMP` function's, one after `FROM` or `JOIN`, and those in a `CREATE FUNCTION`, `CREATE PROCEDURE` or `CREATE VIEW` body, as they are. Read back: `SELECT fn(0)` reads 2 with the default dataset `two` and 1 with `one`, `FN(0)` and `` `fn`(1) `` 2 and 3 with `UPPER('a')` `A`, a query job `SELECT fn(10)` reads 12 and `jobs.get` shows the client's text, and a script's `CREATE FUNCTION two.g …; SELECT g(2)` runs and `SELECT g(3)` reads 9. **Not qualified**: a function the front does not know (one `routines.insert` made before the front started), which the engine resolves by its bare name. **A function of another dataset** (#1107): in BigQuery each call of `dataset.name` calls that dataset's function whatever the default dataset. Measured first (every name qualified): `SELECT one.fn(0)` with the default dataset `two`, and `SELECT two.fn(1), one.fn(2)` with the default dataset `one` or `two`, failed "sqlite3: SQL logic error: no such column: <project>". The engine resolves the call, but collects the SQL functions it may inline from the default dataset's name path only (its analyzer's `getFunctions` keeps a function whose path the key `project_dataset` is a substring of), and sends any other as a bare storage name `<project>_one_fn(…)`, which SQLite reads as a subtraction; with no default dataset every function of the project is collected. Fixed in the engine CloudBurrow builds (googlesqlite patch 0007: the analyzer collects every dataset's functions and table functions, keyed by their full storage names), so the front sends such a query as it is, with its default dataset. Read back: `SELECT one.fn(0)` with the default dataset `two` reads 1, `SELECT two.fn(0)` with `one` 2, `SELECT two.fn(1), one.fn(2)` 3 and 3 with no default dataset and with `one`, `SELECT fn(1), one.fn(2), `` `project`.one.fn(3) `` 3, 3 and 4 with `two`; a query job `INSERT INTO t (v) SELECT one.fn(fn(0))` and `SELECT v, one.fn(v) FROM t` with the default dataset `two` write and read 3 and 4, and `jobs.get` shows the client's text and default dataset; with the default dataset `two` (#1123, 501 before), a script `DECLARE x INT64 DEFAULT one.fn(1); SELECT one.fn(x)` reads 3, `SELECT one.fn(1), @@dataset_id IS NULL` 2 and true (`@@dataset_id` reads NULL with a default dataset, #1137), `SELECT one.fn(1), (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM two.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES) > 0` 2 and true, and `CREATE TABLE c AS SELECT one.fn(5) AS v` then `CREATE VIEW vw AS SELECT one.fn(v) AS w FROM c` make a view that reads 7. **A call by one quoted path** (#1122): the [user-defined functions](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/user-defined-functions) guide names a function so (``CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION `project.dataset.masking_routine1`(ssn STRING)``). Measured first: `` `project.dataset.fn`(3) `` and `` `dataset.fn`(1) `` failed "Function not found" with or without a default dataset; the engine registered a table, but not a function, under its whole dotted path. Fixed in the engine (googlesqlite patch 0008, table functions too): `` `project.one.fn`(3) `` reads 4 with the default dataset `two` and with none, `` `one.fn`(1), `two.fn`(1) `` 2 and 3. Units `TestFunctionNamesInTheDefaultDataset`, `TestFunctionOfAnotherDataset`. Since #1137 `@@dataset_id` in a query with a default dataset reads that dataset's ID (the emulator read NULL; the front sends it as a string literal unless the query `SET`s it), unit `TestDatasetIDVariable`, compat `TestBigQueryDatasetIDIsTheDefaultDataset`. |
| `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` | **Verified** (#1037) as a child job: a script with an `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` and no `TEMP` table or function is carried out by the front a statement at a time, as a script with control flow is, so each statement an `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` runs is a `STATEMENT` child job of the script's `SCRIPT` job (also a lone `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`, with one child), whose own query is the statement with its `USING` values bound and whose stack frame is the `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`'s place and text in the script (BigQuery's frame of such a statement UNVERIFIED), and its SQL expression, when not a string literal, and each `USING` value are `EXPRESSION` children; `@@row_count` after DML, run directly or by `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`, read by a query, a `SET`, a condition or another `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`, is the DML statement's `numDmlAffectedRows` (BigQuery: "If used in a multi-statement query and the previous statement is DML, specifies the number of rows modified, inserted, or deleted"), NULL before any DML and after a statement of another kind (UNVERIFIED), and 501 in a script with a `TEMP` table or function, which stays one request, as the emulator does not know it (measured: "Unrecognized name: @@row_count"); `INTO` of a query of more than one row ("an error is thrown if you attempt to return more than one row") and `INTO` a number of variables other than the query's columns (they are "assigned by position") are 400 `invalidQuery` (a failed job for `jobs.insert`), and the statements after do not run; an `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`, `BEGIN … END`, `CASE`, `IF`, `LOOP`, `REPEAT`, `WHILE` or `CALL` inside one is 400 `invalidQuery`, as BigQuery documents each "restricted from being executed dynamically as a nested element" (the wording of these errors UNVERIFIED). In a script with a `TEMP` table or function, the front puts the statement in the script's text, as follows. Formerly **Verified** for a string literal, or a script variable set to one by its `DECLARE`'s `DEFAULT` or a `SET` (a `CONCAT` or `||` of string literals and such variables counts as one, #1037, unit only), with `USING` literals, script variables or query parameters, named or positional, and `INTO` one or several variables of a query (#1037: run as `SET v = IF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (query)) > 1, ERROR(…), (query))`, as the emulator's scalar subquery of two rows gives the first (measured); several variables as one such `SET` per variable, each taking its column of the same row by position, `(SELECT AS STRUCT * FROM (query))[OFFSET(i)]`, since the emulator does not run `SET (a, b) = …` (measured: a parse error); read back: `'SELECT 41 + 1' INTO x` sets 42, a variable's query with `USING` is read, `'SELECT 5, "five"' INTO a, b` sets 5 and `five`, named columns too; a query of two rows fails the script at the statement when a later statement gives the script's answer (a query, DML or DDL: the front puts a `CREATE TEMP TABLE _cloudburrow_into_n AS SELECT IF(…, ERROR(…), 0)` before the `SET`s, which the emulator runs at once, measured, and the statement after is not run); with no such later statement (the guard would become the script's answer), the front counts the query's rows first, with the probe it uses for computed SQL, and when there are several puts `SELECT ERROR(…)` in the statement's place, so the script fails there, after the statements before it; otherwise the statement is run as before and the answer is unchanged (read back: `DECLARE x INT64; SELECT 7 AS v; EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT 1' INTO x` answers 7, and `… INTO x` of two rows with no later statement fails, with and without an earlier query; #1037); when that count cannot be faithful (the probe's rules below) it is 501; no rows set every variable NULL, as BigQuery documents ("If the query returns zero rows, all variables in the `INTO` clause are set to NULL"), read back for one and two variables; a backticked variable that need not be quoted is set as the same name unquoted, read back for `` INTO `a` ``; a number of variables other than the query's columns, when its text gives them, is 400, as the columns are assigned by position, #1037); SQL **computed** by any other expression (`FORMAT`, `CAST`, a variable set by a query, #1037) is evaluated first: the front runs the statements before it and then `SELECT (<expression>)` on the emulator, as a script of its own with its variables renamed (the emulator keeps a script's variables after it, #956), and runs the string it gives; `DECLARE` and `SET` are run again, queries, DML and DDL are left out, and a `BEGIN … END` block is run as its statements (the emulator does not run a block sent as one, measured), so computed SQL also works in a `BEGIN … END` block and after DML and DDL, provided neither the expression nor a `DECLARE` or `SET` after the DML or DDL reads a table (`FROM`); read back: `FORMAT` in a block, after a block, and after `CREATE TEMP TABLE`; read back: `FORMAT('SELECT %d AS v', 1)`, `CONCAT('SELECT ', CAST(4 AS STRING))`, a variable whose `DEFAULT` is `(SELECT 'SELECT 1')`, `FORMAT` of a variable a `SET` changed, with `USING` and with `INTO` of the same variable, and a computed `CREATE TABLE`, which is made; the evaluation is a job of the front's own, which `jobs.list` does not list (checked on a local instance through jobs.query and query jobs: only the client's job is listed); SQL that is NULL or not a STRING, and an expression whose evaluation fails, are 400 `invalidQuery`, BigQuery's wording UNVERIFIED; SQL computed with `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` or `RAND`, or from a table after DML, a `USING` value that is an expression, and a statement that names a script variable BigQuery hides from it, are carried out in their turn, as BigQuery does (#1037, below); **Not implemented** (501) for what BigQuery does not document (`INTO` of a statement other than a query) and the rest | `TestBigQueryExecuteImmediateForms`, `TestBigQueryExecuteImmediateErrors` and `TestBigQueryExecuteImmediateChildJobs` (#1037: a test per form, the documented errors, the child jobs and `@@row_count`), `TestBigQueryExecuteImmediate` (#1011) and `TestBigQueryExecuteImmediateInTurn` (#1037), official Go client, through `jobs.query` and query jobs, on one instance with `--services bigquery,storage`. Measured first against the pinned emulator: every `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` was answered done and ran nothing: `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT 1 AS a'` returned no rows and no schema, `'CREATE TABLE ds.t (x INT64)'` made no table (a query job ended `DONE` with no error), and `'CREATE FUNCTION …'`, alone, in `BEGIN … END` and from a `DECLARE`d variable, made no function. BigQuery runs the statement ([EXECUTE IMMEDIATE](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/procedural-language#execute_immediate)). Now the front replaces each one it can carry out with its statement before the query is sent, each query parameter (`@name`, `?`) with its `USING` value in parentheses, and then checks and runs the query as any other (`jobs.get` shows the client's text). Read back: `SELECT 1 AS a` returns 1, `'SELECT @a + 1' USING 1 AS a` returns 2, `'SELECT ? * 10, ?' USING 4, 'four'` returns 40 and `four`, a variable's statement and a `USING` variable are read; `CREATE TABLE` makes the table, and `CREATE FUNCTION` alone, in `BEGIN … END` and from a variable set by `SET` makes the function, which is then called. **501** `notImplemented`, before anything of the query runs (a `CREATE TABLE` before it is not made): what BigQuery does not document, `INTO` of a statement that is not a query (SELECT or WITH; BigQuery: "If this returns a value, the `INTO` clause must contain values of the same type"), also in a script the front runs in its turn (there after the statements before it ran, which are kept; #1037); `INTO` a backticked name that must be quoted (the emulator does not run a `SET` of one, measured, and the front's own run of a script does not read such a variable); a statement of several statements, which BigQuery's documentation does not give it; and, in a script with a `TEMP` table or function, which lasts only for the request that made it and so keeps the script in one request, what the front carries out in its turn (below). **Carried out in its turn** (#1037): an `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` the front cannot put in the script's text is run, as BigQuery runs it, by the front's own run of the script, a statement at a time, as a script with control flow is (row `DDL in a script's blocks, and control-flow blocks`): its SQL is evaluated when the statements before it have run, its `USING` values each once, and its statement is sent as a request of its own, with only the `USING` values bound. That is: computed SQL that cannot be evaluated first faithfully (in or after a block with an `EXCEPTION` handler, after a `CALL`, `RAISE`, transaction or other `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`, after DML or DDL when the expression or a later `DECLARE` or `SET` reads a table, a probe that fails after DML or DDL it left out, or a function whose value changes from one run to the next, `RAND`, `GENERATE_UUID`, `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` and the other `CURRENT_` functions, `SESSION_USER`, `TABLESAMPLE`, a function of a dataset, or a system variable `@@` in it or before it); a `USING` value that is an expression (`1 + 1`, `n * 2`, `RAND()`), which BigQuery binds as a value ("These identifiers function similarly to query parameters"); and a statement that names one of the script's variables other than as an alias, a field, a parameter or a function: BigQuery hides them from it ("all other local variables and query parameters aren't exposed"), and the statement sent alone does not see them either, so the name reads the statement's own column or alias of that name, or fails (`Unrecognized name`), 400, and the statements after it do not run. Read back in `TestBigQueryExecuteImmediateInTurn`: `FORMAT('SELECT %T', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()) INTO t` after a query sets a timestamp of the statement's time, not after the next statement's; `CREATE TABLE t …; INSERT t VALUES (1), (2); EXECUTE IMMEDIATE (SELECT FORMAT('SELECT %d', COUNT(*)) FROM t)` answers 2; `'SELECT @a, @a * 2' USING 1 + 1 AS a` answers 2 and 4, `USING n * 2` reads the variable, `'SELECT @r = @r, @r < 1' USING RAND() AS r` answers true (one value), `INTO y USING 40 + 1 AS v` sets 42; with `x` declared, `'SELECT x FROM UNNEST([5]) AS x'` answers 5 and `'SELECT x'` fails 400 (a failed job `invalidQuery` for `jobs.insert`) and the `CREATE TABLE` after it is not made. A parameter with no `USING` value, a count of positional values that differs, and named and positional mixed are **400** `invalidQuery` (a failed job for `jobs.insert`), BigQuery's wording UNVERIFIED. The console's Read-write editor runs an `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE FORMAT(…) USING …` that makes a table (`TestBigQueryEditorRunsExecuteImmediate`, browser, #1037). Units `TestExecuteImmediateRunsInTurn`, `TestExecuteImmediateIsExpanded`, `TestExecuteImmediateOfAConstant`, `TestExecuteImmediateHidesVariables`, `TestExecuteImmediateEvaluated`, `TestExecuteImmediateQuotedInto`, `TestExecuteImmediateEvaluatedInBlocks`, `TestExecuteImmediateIntoCountsRows`. |
| Schema updates: `tables.patch` and `tables.update` (`Table.Update`) | **Verified** for new top-level columns at the end (NULLABLE or REPEATED, of any type the emulator makes, `RECORD` included), fields added at the end of a `RECORD` or a `REPEATED RECORD` at any depth (#1036), a schema given in another order (the table keeps its own), a mode relaxed from `REQUIRED` to `NULLABLE`, and descriptions; **400** for what BigQuery refuses, and since #1111 **412** "Precondition Failed" for a new column or field given before one the table has; **Not implemented** (501) for a renamed column and a view's columns | `TestBigQueryTableUpdateAddsColumns` (#1010, #1013, #1036), the official Go client's `Table.Update` (`tables.patch`) and the generated client's `Tables.Update` (`tables.update`, google.golang.org/api/bigquery/v2). Measured first against the pinned emulator: both answered 200 and `tables.get` read the new columns, but the emulator changed only the table's metadata (its `tablesPatchHandler` and `tablesUpdateHandler` call `metadata.Table.Patch`/`Replace`), never its engine's columns: `INSERT INTO ds.t (f, g)` failed 400 "Column g is not present in table", `SELECT h` failed "Unrecognized name: h", and every later `tabledata.insertAll`, with or without the new column, failed **500** "Column … is not present", which the Go client retries until its deadline (#1013). In BigQuery an added column is added to the table, NULL (or empty) in its rows ([Add a column](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas#add_columns)). Now the front, before it sends the request on, makes the table again when its schema adds columns: its rows are copied to a scratch table made with the new schema (in `_cloudburrow_query_results`, deleted later while the instance is idle, #1091), the table is deleted and made again with the new schema and its description, labels, expiration, partitioning and clustering (through `tables.insert`, so a `FLOAT` column is `FLOAT64`, #1000), the rows are copied back, and its creation time is set back; then the request is sent on. Read back through the Go client: a table with a `REQUIRED` `INTEGER` and a `FLOAT` column and two rows, after `Table.Update` adding a `STRING`, a `REPEATED STRING` and a `RECORD` and relaxing the first to `NULLABLE`, reads the new schema, keeps its description, labels and creation time, and its two rows read the new columns NULL (the `REPEATED` one empty); it then takes `Inserter.Put` with all the columns, with the old ones only and with none of the old ones (a NULL `id`), a DML `INSERT` of the new ones (a query job), and a CSV load with the new `STRING` column, and `Table.Read` and a `SELECT` of the new column read every row; `Tables.Update` adding an `INTEGER` then takes an `UPDATE … SET` of it. **400** `invalid`, the table unchanged ("Provided Schema does not match Table p:ds.t. Field id is missing in new schema", "… Field id has changed type from INTEGER to STRING", "… Field id has changed mode from NULLABLE to REQUIRED", "… Cannot add required fields to an existing schema. (field: req)"; BigQuery refuses each, its wording UNVERIFIED). **Fields added to a `RECORD`** (#1036): BigQuery adds a nested field through the same methods, at the end of its `RECORD` ("New columns and nested fields are always added at the end of the table or field", [Add a nested column to a RECORD column](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas#add_a_nested_column_to_a_record_column)). The front makes the table again as above, and copies each row with every `RECORD` rebuilt by name in the new schema's order, the new fields NULL (a `REPEATED` one empty), a NULL `RECORD` NULL and a `REPEATED RECORD`'s elements in their order (`IF(r IS NULL, NULL, STRUCT(r.x AS x, …, CAST(NULL AS T) AS y))`, `ARRAY(SELECT STRUCT(…) FROM UNNEST(rr) … ORDER BY offset)`; measured first: read back every row as it was, the new fields NULL). Read back: after `Table.Update` adding a `RECORD` `n` to the `RECORD` `r` and a new `REPEATED RECORD` `rr`, a DML `INSERT` of both, and a second `Table.Update`, given with its first two columns swapped, adding `r.n.w` (`BYTES`, two levels down), `r.q` (`REPEATED STRING`) and `rr.v` (`NUMERIC`, in the `REPEATED RECORD`), the table reads the new schema in its own order, every earlier row reads as it did (id, f, g, tags, whether `r` is NULL, `r.x`, h), the new fields read NULL or empty and `rr`'s elements in order, and the table takes an `INSERT` of `b'\xff\x00'`, `['q1']` and `NUMERIC '1.25'` into them, which read back so. **A schema in another order** is sent in the table's order, the new columns and fields after its own: "Modifying schema order after table creation doesn't have an effect on column or nested field order" (same page, Add columns). **412**, nothing changed (#1111): a new column or field given before one the table has, at the top level or in a `RECORD` at any depth. BigQuery refuses it: "It isn't possible to add columns in the middle of a table schema … If you attempt to add new columns elsewhere in the array, the following error is returned: BigQuery error in update operation: Precondition Failed" ([Add columns](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas#add_columns)). The bq tool prints the message of BigQuery's REST error there, so the front answers that message, `Precondition Failed`, with the status it names, HTTP 412 (`FAILED_PRECONDITION`), and reason `conditionNotMet`, the reason of BigQuery's other 412s; the status and the reason are UNVERIFIED for this case, as BigQuery documents only the bq text. It is checked after the 400s (a `REQUIRED` column added first is still 400) and before the 501s. Read back through the Go client: `Table.Update` with a new `STRING` column first, one between the table's first and second columns, and a new field before a `RECORD`'s own each fail `googleapi.Error` 412 `conditionNotMet`, and the table reads its schema and rows as before. The console's Edit table adds fields only after the table's own, so it never sends one. **501** `notImplemented`, nothing changed: a column's name in another case, and a view's columns other than descriptions. The emulator's engine keeps no `NOT NULL`, so a mode and a description are metadata alone and are sent as they are. A `tables.update` with no schema is sent as it is. A `tables.patch` that also gives labels or a description is then carried out as the next row says, the table read once for both (#1054). Units `TestSchemaUpdates`, `TestSchemaChange`, `TestAlterTableAdviceIsTrue`, `TestConvertColumns`. |
| Column default values (`defaultValueExpression`, `CREATE TABLE … DEFAULT`, `ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT` / `DROP DEFAULT`) | **Verified** for top-level columns; **Refused** (400, as BigQuery refuses it: "You cannot add a new column with a default value to an existing table") `ADD COLUMN … DEFAULT` and a `tables.patch` that adds a column with a default, wording UNVERIFIED; **Not implemented** (501) a nested field's `ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT`, and a `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` query job whose result lacks a column with a default; **Not supported**: `UPDATE … SET c = DEFAULT`, which the engine refuses ("DEFAULT is supported only in an INSERT's VALUES") | `TestBigQueryColumnDefaults` (#1340), official Go client and Storage Write client, each default read back through `Table.Metadata` and each row through a query, as [default-values](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/default-values) documents them: a default given by `tables.insert`, `CREATE TABLE … DEFAULT` (through `jobs.query` and `jobs.insert`), `tables.patch` (`Table.Update`) and `ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT` reads back as the column's `defaultValueExpression` as written; it is applied by a DML `INSERT` that leaves the column out or gives `DEFAULT`, `VALUES` and `INSERT … SELECT`, by `tabledata.insertAll` for a row without the column, by a JSON load whose records lack it, and by the Storage Write API's default stream when the stream's schema lacks the field; a `NULL` given (DML, `insertAll`, a load's `null`, a Storage Write field in the stream's schema left unset, unless the append's missing-value interpretation is `DEFAULT_VALUE`, #1391) stays `NULL`. `SET DEFAULT` and `tables.patch` change only future inserts, the rows the table has kept as they are; `DROP DEFAULT` and `SET DEFAULT NULL` clear the default. Measured first through the front (2026-10-15): the emulator made the engine's table without a `tables.insert` column's default (an `INSERT` read NULL), applied no default to `insertAll` or a load, and read no `defaultValueExpression` back for a `CREATE TABLE` column; engine patches bigquery-emulator 0014 and googlesqlite 0027 (third_party/bigquery-emulator/PROVENANCE.md) apply them, and since the emulator's `tables.patch` changes only metadata, a change of a default makes the table again with its rows (`internal/bigqueryfront/columndefaults.go`). Units `TestParseAlter`, `TestDefaultChange`. |
| GoogleSQL type names in a schema (`INT64`, `BOOL`, `FLOAT64`, `STRUCT`, `DECIMAL`, `BIGDECIMAL`) | **Verified** for `tables.insert`, a load job's schema and `tables.patch` | `TestBigQueryGoogleSQLTypeNamesReadBack` (#1034), official Go client. BigQuery's reference lists each field type by its legacy name with the GoogleSQL name as an accepted alias: "INTEGER (or INT64)", "FLOAT (or FLOAT64)", "BOOLEAN (or BOOL)", "RECORD (or STRUCT)" ([TableFieldSchema.type](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/tables#TableFieldSchema.FIELDS.type)); the Go client says "The API will accept alias names for the types based on the Standard SQL type names" (its `fieldAliases`, with `DECIMAL` and `BIGDECIMAL` for `NUMERIC` and `BIGNUMERIC`) and reads only the legacy names back (`Table.Read` fails "unrecognized type: INT64" on any other). Measured first against the pinned emulator: `tables.insert` of fields typed `INT64` and `BOOL` read back `INT64` and `BOOL`, and `Table.Read` failed "unrecognized type: INT64"; a table made by `CREATE TABLE … (n INT64, b BOOL, f FLOAT64, r STRUCT<x INT64>)`, and a query's result schema, read back `INTEGER`, `BOOLEAN`, `FLOAT` and `RECORD`. Now the front sends every alias in the schema of `tables.insert`, `tables.update`, `tables.patch` and a load job (at any depth) by its legacy name; the engine's types are the same (a `FLOAT` field is then made `FLOAT64` as in the `FLOAT` row above). Read back through the Go client: a table made with `INT64`, `BOOL`, `FLOAT64`, `DECIMAL` and a `STRUCT` of an `INT64` reads `INTEGER`, `BOOLEAN`, `FLOAT`, `NUMERIC` and `RECORD` of an `INTEGER`, and its row through `Table.Read`; so does a JSON load with that schema, and a column added as `INT64` through `Table.Update` reads `INTEGER`. That BigQuery's own `tables.get` of a field made as `INT64` reads `INTEGER` is **UNVERIFIED** here: it is inferred from the official client, which could not read the table otherwise, and from the emulator's own DDL. Units `TestGoogleSQLTypeNamesAreSentAsLegacyNames`, `TestFloatColumnsAreMadeFloat64`, `TestSchemaUpdates`. |
| A view's table names without a dataset (`tables.insert`, `tables.update`, `tables.patch` of a view) | **Verified**: refused 400 | `TestBigQueryViewsNameTheirTablesWithADataset` (#1035), official Go client. BigQuery: "A reference inside of a view must be qualified with a dataset. The default dataset doesn't affect a view body." ([Views, limitations](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/views)). Measured first against the pinned emulator, with `one.t` made first and `two.t` after: a view `two.v` made through `Table.Create` with `ViewQuery` `SELECT * FROM t` was made and read `one.t`'s rows, through `Table.Read` and a query. Now a view's (or materialized view's) GoogleSQL query that names a table without a dataset, where a query reads or writes one (as in *Tables of one ID in two datasets*: not a CTE's name), is **400** `invalid` "Table \"t\" must be qualified with a dataset (e.g. dataset.table). A view's query is not read in any default dataset, not even the view's own.", and nothing is made (BigQuery's wording for a view is UNVERIFIED); one naming `dataset.t` reads that table. A legacy SQL view is not read. **A `CREATE VIEW` statement's query** (and `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW`'s) is held to the same rule whatever the query's default dataset (#1049, `TestBigQueryCreateViewNamesItsTablesWithADataset`, official Go client, through `jobs.query` and as a query job): since #1015 the front had sent its table names in the default dataset, so `CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT * FROM t` with `two` the default dataset made a view of `two.t`. Now, in the query's first statement, it is **400** `invalid` with the message above (a query job fails so), for `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` too (before its 501), and nothing is made; in a later statement of a script the name is sent in a dataset that does not exist, so the script runs the statements before it and fails there, as for a query with no default dataset. The view's own name is in the default dataset, and `CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT * FROM one.t` with `two` the default makes `two.v` reading `one.t`. What BigQuery answers such a statement was **not measured** (no live GCP); the refusal follows the reference quoted above, and its wording is UNVERIFIED. | Row-level security: `bigquery.rowAccessPolicies.insert`, `bigquery.rowAccessPolicies.list`, `bigquery.rowAccessPolicies.get`, `bigquery.rowAccessPolicies.update`, `bigquery.rowAccessPolicies.delete`, `bigquery.rowAccessPolicies.batchDelete`; `CREATE [OR REPLACE] ROW ACCESS POLICY [IF NOT EXISTS] … ON t [GRANT TO (…)] FILTER USING (…)`, `DROP ROW ACCESS POLICY [IF EXISTS] … ON t`, `DROP ALL ROW ACCESS POLICIES ON t` | **Verified**, filtering for **one fixed caller**; **Not implemented** (501) for every read the front cannot filter | `TestBigQueryRowAccessPolicies` (#1218), the generated client (`RowAccessPolicies.*`) and the official Go client (queries, `Table.ExtractorTo`, `Table.CopierFrom`, `Table.Read` through the Storage Read client). Measured first: the emulator has no row-level security and answered every method 500 (#1200). The front keeps the policies (in its state directory, so a restart of the front does not unfilter a table; an emulator restart drops them) and applies them: each read of a table with policies in a GoogleSQL query's `FROM` clause (`FROM`, `JOIN`, a comma, `MERGE … USING`, in subqueries and CTEs too) is sent as `(SELECT * FROM t WHERE (filter) OR (filter) …)`, with the filters of the policies granted to the caller, or `WHERE FALSE` when none is: a table with policies and none for the caller reads no rows, as [BigQuery documents](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/row-level-security-intro). Read back: someone else's policy alone read no rows; the caller's `region = 'eu'` read the two EU rows; adding an `allUsers` policy `amount > 6` read the union; dropping them read all four. A policy's filter is checked by a query of the table that reads no rows (a filter naming no column is 400). A table's policies go with it: they are dropped when the table is deleted or made again (`CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE`, a changed `creationTime`). **The caller.** CloudBurrow authenticates nobody ([ADR-0004](adr/0004-local-access-and-no-authentication.md)) and cannot tell who sent a query, so **every caller is taken to be the one identity it gives out**: the service account of its credentials and metadata server, `cloudburrow-local@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (`cloudburrow env`'s project). A policy grants the caller when it names `serviceAccount:` that account, `allAuthenticatedUsers` or `allUsers`; `user:`, `group:`, `domain:` and other service accounts never match here, so their rows are not returned to anyone; `SESSION_USER()` in a filter is that account. A test cannot show two callers reading different rows, and none claims to. **501, nothing read:** `tabledata.list`, an extract job, a copy job and a Storage Read session of a table with policies; `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MERGE` and `TRUNCATE TABLE` of one; a time travel (`FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF`) or wildcard read of one; a view (or materialized view) whose query reads one; a table function, and a legacy SQL query, in a project with policies; a row access policy statement in a script with other statements, and a policy on another project's table. `INSERT` into a table with policies is carried out. A scalar SQL function whose body reads a table is not looked into (UNVERIFIED that BigQuery filters it). Unit `TestFilterQuery`, `TestParseRowPolicyDDL`, `TestCallerIdentityIsTheCredentialsAccount`. |

The front reads the table's rows from the emulator (`tabledata.list`, or a `SELECT *` of `dataset.table` when another dataset has a table of the ID, #1015; `TestBigQueryExtractReadsItsOwnTable` extracts a table whose ID another dataset's table, made first, has, and reads back its own rows), writes the file as the [export documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/exporting-data) gives it, and uploads it to **the instance's own Cloud Storage** (`--storage`); the job is the front's, answered by `jobs.get`, `jobs.list`, `jobs.cancel` and `jobs.delete` (the last 1,000, in its memory), with `destinationUriFileCounts` 1 and times in milliseconds; a job ID in use is 409. CSV ("You can control the CSV delimiter"; "GZIP" is listed for CSV and JSON): the bytes are the emulator's comma-separated ones of the row above, measured to be BigQuery's, with the delimiter (a tab read back byte for byte, `x,y` unquoted) or compressed (the `GZIP` object read back decompressed equal to the emulator's `,` file); a wildcard URI is written as its `000000000000` file. An empty table with a header ("header rows are printed to the exported data if the data format supports headers"): its header row, `a,b`. A NULL is left out of a JSON row, and each type is written as the row above gives (#957). **501**, nothing written: a dry run, and a front with no Cloud Storage. AVRO: an Avro object container file, one record field a column in the schema's order, each of the Avro type the [Avro export details](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/exporting-data#avro_export_details) map it to (INT64 `long`, FLOAT64 `double`, BOOL `boolean`, STRING `string`, BYTES `bytes`), a NULLABLE column a union with `null`; the record's name `Root` is UNVERIFIED against BigQuery, and the sync marker and block sizes are the writer's (an Avro reader reads the same rows, not the same bytes). | The SQL engine failing after many queries | **Fixed** for the 2 GiB panic (#1061); the mitigation below is kept for any other failure of the engine | #989. **Since #1061** CloudBurrow builds the emulator with go-googlesql patched to address WebAssembly memory with unsigned offsets (third_party/bigquery-emulator, go-googlesql patch 0001): its test `TestInvokeAboveTwoGiB` fills the engine's heap below 2 GiB and makes a call whose buffers lie above it, which panicked "slice bounds out of range [-2110640288:]" without the patch and passes with it. `scripts/bigquery-engine-soak.sh --jobs 150` on an instance of CloudBurrow's build (with the rest of #1061 and the fronts of main at the time) ran 150 query jobs and 30 `CREATE TABLE`/`DROP TABLE` pairs with no restart, the emulator container at 754 MiB at the end (281 MiB at the start), so the soak no longer reaches 2 GiB and the patched path past it is measured by the patch's test alone. **Growth through DDL** (#1057): every `DROP` of a table, view or function rebuilds every catalog, and each project's and dataset's sub-catalog registered the whole builtin function set again; CloudBurrow's build carries upstream's open goccy/googlesqlite#80 (googlesqlite patch 0006), which builds those sub-catalogs bare. Measured on an instance with 10 datasets of a table each, `bigquery-engine-soak.sh` from PR #1093, 40 operations: `--phase ddl` (CREATE and DROP TABLE) 4342 MiB before the patch, 231 MiB with it (0.50 s and 0.12 s an operation); `--phase orreplace` (CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE … AS SELECT) 11147 MiB and a 500 at the 25th before, 341 MiB and all 40 with it. The BigQuery compat suite (but `TestBigQueryJobsAcrossAnEmulatorRestart`, which restarts the emulator) on one fresh emulator took it from 62 to 2462 MiB before, and from 60 to 1372 MiB with it: less, not gone. What follows is the pinned emulator, as measured before #1061. The pinned emulator's SQL engine, goccy/go-googlesql v0.3.0 (a WebAssembly module translated to Go), lets its memory grow to 4 GiB but addresses it with signed 32-bit offsets (`(*Module).invoke`, `googlesql.go:614`, `624`), so once that memory passes 2 GiB every call panics "slice bounds out of range [-2147…:]": in a request, which the emulator answers 400 or 500 "googlesqlite: panic …" (from then on to every request, `SELECT 1` and `datasets.list` alike), or in a finalizer, which kills the process. The memory grows with each query job that returns rows (the emulator kept each result in a dataset of its own, and the engine builds a catalog of every builtin function for each) and each `DROP TABLE` (which rebuilds every dataset's catalog). The engine's objects are freed by Go finalizers, which run only when the emulator's Go heap is collected, and the engine's memory is one large `[]byte` in that heap, so a collection waits for the heap to double past it: freed engine memory is reused late, and the memory does not shrink. Measured with `scripts/bigquery-engine-soak.sh`: the emulator container went from 455 MiB to 3840 MiB in 40 query jobs and 8 `CREATE TABLE`/`DROP TABLE` pairs, and the 60th job's `DROP TABLE` was answered the panic; one run of the BigQuery compat suite left it at 2692 MiB. go-googlesql v0.4.0 is the same. Upstream: the growth per query is goccy/bigquery-emulator#512 and #313, with a fix in review, goccy/googlesqlite#80; no upstream issue names the signed offsets. **Mitigation:** the front watches the emulator's error answers for that panic (`engineGuard`); at the first it answers that request **501** `notImplemented` naming this, sends the emulator nothing more, and fails the engine's liveness path (`/cloudburrow/bigquery-engine-live` on the front's port), so the emulator is restarted; every request until its port has closed and opened again is answered **503** `backendError` with `Retry-After: 1` (the official clients retry a 503), and then requests pass. Measured before #1091: the soak's panic was answered 501, the container's liveness probe failed, and 14 s later the emulator had restarted (restart count 1) and `SELECT 1` answered 200. **Restarts without Kubernetes' back-off (#1091):** Kubernetes restarted the emulator's container (for the probe, or when the process crashed, #1058), and the kubelet waits longer before each restart of a container that keeps failing (`CrashLoopBackOff`: 10 s, doubled at each restart up to 5 minutes, and reset only after the container has run 10 minutes). On one instance the BigQuery compat suite run four times in a row (#1057, below) reached "back-off 5m0s restarting failed container=bigquery" after the seventh restart, and in two of four series its fourth run failed most tests with 502 "the BigQuery emulator did not answer: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:9051: connect: connection refused" (545 s and 562 s). Now the emulator's container runs `cloudburrow-storage supervise` (`internal/supervisor`), which an init container copies in from the front's image (`install-self`), and which runs the image's entrypoint (`/bin/bigquery-emulator`) as its child: when the child ends, for any reason (the panic in a finalizer, a SIGSEGV, an out-of-memory kill of it), it starts it again within at most 1 s (100 ms, doubled while it keeps ending within 2 s of its start); it gets the front's liveness path every 0.5 s from 1 s after each start and kills the child (SIGKILL) after two 503s in a row, and restarts it the same way; no answer from the front (the front restarting) is not a failure. The container never restarts, so the back-off never applies, and it has no liveness probe. While the emulator's port refuses connections the front answers 503 with `Retry-After` too, not 502. `POST /cloudburrow/bigquery-restart-emulator` on the front's port restarts the emulator as the panic does (answered 202), for tests, soaks, or an instance grown slow (it empties the emulator). Measured on an instance of my own: `scripts/bigquery-engine-soak.sh --phase restart --jobs 10` (a restart, then `datasets.list` until 200) took 1.0–2.6 s each, answering 503 then 200, with the container's restart count 0 and its memory at 78 MiB throughout (the first build, which waited 5 s after a start before checking, took 2.0 s and then 5.9–6.3 s); killing the emulator's process (`kill -9`) three times, it answered 503 and was back in 0.2 s each; the BigQuery compat suite passed, with `TestBigQueryEmulatorRestartsPromptly`'s eight restarts in a row back in 1.0–2.7 s. The suite run four times in a row on that emulator: 305 s, all passed; then 605 s, 610 s and 607 s, each stopped by the 10-minute limit (one test failed "context deadline exceeded" in the third, two in the fourth), with no restart of the emulator, no "connection refused" and no 502 in any of them: nothing failed the engine or crashed the process (table functions, whose SIGSEGV restarted it before, are 501 since #1052), so the emulator was never emptied and the growth through DDL below made it slower with each run (#1103). Units `TestCrashesRestartPromptly` (ten starts of a child that crashes, each within the delay), `TestLivenessFailuresRestartPromptly` (eight restarts in a row through the liveness path, none while it answers 200 or does not answer), `TestRestartEmulatorPath`, `TestProxyAnswersARefusedPort503`; the manifest in `TestBigQueryManifestPutsTheFrontOnTheServicePort`. **Growth per query job, fixed (#1017):** the front names a query job's destination table itself, so the emulator writes every result to one dataset (next row) and a job no longer adds a catalog. Measured with the soak script on one instance, from a fresh emulator: 60 query jobs and 12 `CREATE TABLE`/`DROP TABLE` pairs took the container from 62 MiB to 4301 MiB in 23.7 s before, and from 66 MiB to 701 MiB in 7.8 s after; 400 jobs and 80 pairs held it at 799–802 MiB from the 100th job on (100 s). Tried and measured worse: deleting each job's result dataset right after the job (64 → 1964 MiB in 60 jobs: every deletion is a `DROP TABLE`, which rebuilds the catalogs), and deleting the results of all but the last 20 jobs from the one dataset (3272 MiB at 100 jobs, 300 jobs in 110 s); so the results are kept, as the emulator kept its per-job datasets, until it restarts. Collecting the emulator's heap sooner (`GOGC=10`) held the soak at 200–205 MiB, but the compat suite's `TestBigQueryCreateFunctionOfAnExistingFunction` then failed in each of four runs ("wasm trap: interface conversion: interface {} is nil", "index out of range", a SIGSEGV that killed the process), so it is not set. **Records across a restart, fixed (#1016):** next row but one. **Growth through DDL, loads and scripts, measured (#1057):** it is the catalog rebuild, whatever the statement. Read in the engine (googlesqlite v0.3.1, `internal/catalog.go`, `stmt_action.go`): it builds a catalog with every builtin function (`newSimpleCatalog`) for the root, one for each project, and four for each dataset that holds a table (the dataset under the root and under its project, and each one's `INFORMATION_SCHEMA`: `addTableSpecRecursiveImpl`, `aliasInfoSchemaTable`), and builds them all again at each `DeleteTableSpec`, `DeleteFunctionSpec` and `DeleteTVFSpec` (`resetCatalog`): a `DROP TABLE`, `DROP VIEW` or `DROP FUNCTION` of one that exists, `tables.delete`, each table of a `datasets.delete` with `deleteContents`, and the end of a script that made a TEMP table or function (`Cleanup`); a load, `CREATE TABLE`, the engine's `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` and a `DROP … IF EXISTS` of one that is not there rebuild nothing. So the cost of each rebuild grows with the datasets that hold tables. Measured with `scripts/bigquery-engine-soak.sh --phase <p> --jobs 20 --datasets 10` (each phase from a new emulator, first 10 datasets of one table, about 240 MiB), the container after 20 operations: a `CREATE`/`DROP TABLE` pair 2,247 MiB (10 s); a dataset made and deleted with its table 2,249 MiB; a CSV load with a schema and its `tables.delete` 2,242 MiB; a failed script given to jobs.query 2,248 MiB; `CREATE`/`DROP FUNCTION` 2,197 MiB; `MERGE` from a subquery 2,262 MiB (11 s); a copy job with WRITE_TRUNCATE 4,357 MiB (18 s); `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE … AS SELECT` 4,349 MiB (19 s); `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` of one that exists 4,243 MiB (16 s); a script with a TEMP table 4,218 MiB; a load with autodetect of a FLOAT column (#1000) and its `tables.delete`: the engine failed at the 15th (4,473 MiB); 20 query jobs 902 MiB. **The front's share, cut:** the front's own scratch tables (the copy with WRITE_TRUNCATE, the FLOAT load, `MERGE` from a subquery, `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE`, and since #1091 a Parquet load the front carries out and a schema update that adds columns) and the scratch function of `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` are made in `_cloudburrow_query_results` (next row) rather than the client's dataset, and the front's deletion of each is answered at once and carried out later, with the expired results, while the instance is idle; an error naming one names the client's dataset. Measured the same way after: `MERGE` from a subquery 428 MiB (2 s); `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` 2,249 MiB (10 s); the copy 3,683 MiB (12 s); `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` 3,555 MiB (11 s); the FLOAT load failed at the 20th; a `CREATE`/`DROP TABLE` pair unchanged (2,245 MiB). The Parquet load and the schema update, measured the same way (each phase from an emulator just restarted, twice each), before and after: a Parquet load with `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` of a table that exists (`--phase parquet`) 2,270 MiB (11–19 s) and 447–449 MiB (3–4 s); `tables.patch` adding a column (`--phase schemaupdate`, which also deletes and makes the table again) 4,365 MiB (21–22 s) and 3,528–3,531 MiB (11–12 s). Units `TestScratchTablesInResultsDataset`, `TestScratchFunctionDroppedLater`, `TestUnscratch`; the copy, FLOAT, `MERGE`, `CREATE OR REPLACE` compat tests unchanged. The rest is the clients' own drops (a compat test's cleanup deletes its dataset table by table), which the front cannot leave out without changing their results; it takes an engine whose catalogs do not each hold every builtin (goccy/googlesqlite#80, not released). The BigQuery compat suite run four times on one emulator (`-run BigQuery`, 10-minute limit; each run's time, the container's memory after it and the emulator's restarts so far), in two series on the front before this and two after (two builds that differ only in the cap of the next row, which the suite does not reach): before, 204 s, 1545 MiB, 1; 321 s, 1332 MiB, 2; 381 s, 1480 MiB, 3; 294 s, 2451 MiB, 4; and 214 s, 2476 MiB, 1; 250 s, 2471 MiB, 3; 283 s, 2444 MiB, 5; 545 s, 1311 MiB, 7; after, 169 s, 2453 MiB, 1; 182 s, 2455 MiB, 3; 289 s, 2438 MiB, 5; 562 s, 1604 MiB, 7; and 226 s, 2456 MiB, 1; 271 s, 2447 MiB, 3; 332 s, 2454 MiB, 5; 445 s, 2437 MiB, 6: no change beyond the series' spread, the suite's drops being its tests' own. In two series (one before, one after) the fourth run failed most tests "connection refused": after seven restarts Kubernetes' back-off kept the emulator down for minutes (#1091, fixed above). **What is left:** the restart loses every dataset, table and job, as the crash did (Persistence row); a finalizer can still kill the emulator before any request sees the panic, which the supervisor restarts at once (#1091); a request in flight when the emulator ends is answered 502 (it was sent before the port closed); and the growth through DDL: the BigQuery compat suite is mostly DDL, loads and scripts, and its tests run one at a time from a fresh emulator took the container from 87 MiB to 2427 MiB by its 20th test (the most at `TestBigQueryFailedScriptLeavesTheCatalogInStep`, +840 MiB, and the `CREATE FUNCTION` and `DROP SCHEMA` tests), where it stayed for the other 44. The suite run four times in a row on one emulator (`-run BigQuery`, 10-minute limit; each run's time, the container's memory after it, the emulator's restarts so far, and a `jobs.list` of 200 jobs with `projection=full` after it): before #1017, 218 s, 2872 MiB, 0, 7.4 s; 239 s, 2694 MiB, 1, 5.9 s; 250 s, 2698 MiB, 2, 6.1 s; 270 s, 2721 MiB, 3, 5.8 s; after, 194 s, 2449 MiB, 0, 7.7 s; 606 s (the limit), 4425 MiB, 0, 22.3 s; 275 s, 2830 MiB, 1, 4.9 s; 202 s, 2919 MiB, 2, 5.3 s. Every restart came during `TestBigQueryCreateFunctionOfAnExistingFunction`'s table function, which then failed, before and after alike (after, the emulator's log names a SIGSEGV in the engine, exit code 2); that test passes on a fresh emulator. After a restart, `TestBigQueryDropSchema` failed once (409 for a function it was making), and passed alone. So a long-lived instance that runs much DDL still gets slow and fails; restart it (`cloudburrow stop`, `up`). Follow-ups: the crash #1058; the restart back-off #1091, fixed; the copy with WRITE_TRUNCATE #1092, closed, see *Copy jobs*. Soak: `scripts/bigquery-engine-soak.sh`. Units `TestEngineGuard`, `TestEngineGuardWithoutWatch`, `TestEngineGuardPassesLargeErrors`, `TestBigQueryManifestPutsTheFrontOnTheServicePort`; compat `TestBigQueryEmulatorRestartsPromptly` (#1091), official Go client. |
