| DDL in a script's blocks, and control-flow blocks | **Verified** (#1201) for `IF` / `ELSEIF` / `ELSE`, `LOOP`, `WHILE`, `REPEAT … UNTIL`, `FOR … IN`, simple and searched `CASE`, `BREAK` / `LEAVE`, `CONTINUE` / `ITERATE` with and without labels, `RETURN`, `DECLARE` and `SET` in blocks, with block scope, `SET (a, b) = …` of a STRUCT, `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` (its SQL any STRING expression, evaluated in its turn; `USING` values evaluated once each; `INTO` several variables of a query's one row, NULL with no row, an error with more than one; `INTO` a number of variables other than the query's columns is 400; `INTO` of a statement that is not a query is 501, as BigQuery does not document it, #1037; `@@row_count` after DML, row `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`), and a `FOR` over every page of its query's rows, through `jobs.query` and query jobs; BigQuery's documented limits: the cumulative time limit of a multi-statement query, 24 hours, and 1 MB a variable, 10 MB for all of them; a variable or `FOR` row of type `RANGE<DATE>`, `RANGE<DATETIME>` or `RANGE<TIMESTAMP>` (#1201, `TestBigQueryScriptRangeVariables`); transactions are the row `Multi-statement transactions`; stored procedures are the row `Stored procedures` (#1217) | `TestBigQueryScriptControlFlow` and `TestBigQueryScriptControlFlowMore` (#1201, a subtest per construct) and `TestBigQueryScriptBlocks` (#901), official Go client; `TestBqRunsAScriptWithControlFlow` (#1201), the `bq query` CLI through the harness, a script of `DECLARE`, `WHILE` and `IF` / `ELSE` printing the `IF` branch's row; the console's Read-write editor runs a script with `IF` / `ELSE` and makes only the `IF` branch's table (`TestBigQueryEditorRunsAScriptWithIF`, browser). Measured against the pinned emulator: the statements inside `IF` (either branch), `LOOP`, `WHILE`, `REPEAT`, `FOR` and a script `CASE` were not run, and the script returned success (501 from #901 to #1201). The front now carries such a script out itself ([procedural language](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/procedural-language)): it keeps the variables, each as a literal of its type in the scope of its block, runs each condition, `DECLARE … DEFAULT` and `SET` value and `FOR` query on the emulator with the variables replaced by their literals, and sends each other statement in its turn as a query of its own, through the front's own checks. A statement that fails ends the script with its error (what the statements before it did is kept, as in BigQuery) unless an `EXCEPTION` block catches it. The answer is the last statement's result, as `jobs.getQueryResults` "returns the query results for the last statement to execute" ([multi-statement queries](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/multi-statement-queries)): a final query, or statement that changes data, is held back and sent as the client's own request, so a query job's rows are its rows and its `numDmlAffectedRows` its own (a statement that changes data held back runs before anything that may read it); a final `DECLARE` or `SET` answers with no rows, as it has none (UNVERIFIED against BigQuery beyond that sentence). One in an `EXCEPTION` block runs at once, to see its failure, and a query job ending in such a DML statement is recorded with a statement that does nothing. Every statement is checked before anything runs, whether or not its branch would run, and a name BigQuery refuses is **400** first: `` CREATE TABLE ds.`if!` `` in an `IF`, `` `loop!` `` in a `LOOP`, `` `handler!` `` in an `EXCEPTION` handler, and nothing is made (unit `TestDDLInBlocksAndAlterTable`). A loop that never ends fails after 24 hours, BigQuery's cumulative limit, or stops when the client's request is gone (units `TestScriptTimeLimit`, `TestScriptVariableLimits`, `TestScriptLastStatement`). A `BEGIN … END` block with no handler or control flow is sent to the emulator, which runs it. |
| Stored procedures: `CREATE [OR REPLACE] PROCEDURE [IF NOT EXISTS]`, `CALL`, `DROP PROCEDURE` | **Verified** (#1217) for SQL procedures with `IN`, `OUT` and `INOUT` arguments and `OPTIONS(description)`, through `jobs.query` and query jobs; **Not implemented** (501): a `TEMP` procedure, one in another language (`WITH CONNECTION`, `LANGUAGE`), an `ANY TYPE` argument, a transaction in a procedure, and a procedure statement in a dry run or legacy SQL | `TestBigQueryStoredProcedures`, official Go client. Measured first (#1201): the emulator answered `CREATE PROCEDURE` in a dataset that does not exist done, and a `CALL` of a procedure that inserts a row done with no rows and inserted none; its `routines.get` knows no procedure. So the front keeps procedures itself (`internal/bigqueryfront/procedures.go`), beside the functions in its state file, so they survive a restart of its container (unit `TestProceduresOutliveAFrontRestart`; the emulator's restart empties them, as its datasets go), and runs each script with a procedure statement through its interpreter (row above). `CREATE PROCEDURE` needs the dataset (404 `notFound`) and fails 409 `duplicate` for a routine that exists unless `OR REPLACE` or `IF NOT EXISTS`; `DROP PROCEDURE` of none is 404 unless `IF EXISTS`; `DROP SCHEMA` (`RESTRICT`) of a dataset holding one fails `resourceInUse` and `CASCADE` drops it. `CALL` runs the body with the arguments bound in a scope of its own: an `IN` argument is the caller's expression cast to its type, `OUT` and `INOUT` ones must be the caller's variables and are written back when the procedure ends or `RETURN`s; the procedure sees none of its caller's variables; its last statement's rows are the script's answer when it is last. "The maximum depth of procedure calls is 50 frames" ([procedural language](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/procedural-language)): a deeper `CALL` fails, and a handler catches it. An error in a procedure reaches the caller's `EXCEPTION` handler with `@@error.stack_trace` holding the procedure's frame first (`location` `project.dataset.procedure:line:column`, `filename` NULL) and `@@error.formatted_stack_trace` `At project.dataset.procedure[line:column]` then `At [line:column]`, the reference's forms. Read back: two `CALL`s of a procedure that inserts a row made two rows; `OUT`/`INOUT` values, a `RETURN` part way, a deeper call caught; `routines.list` and `routines.get` show `PROCEDURE`, `SQL`, arguments with mode and type, the description and the `BEGIN … END` body; `routines.delete` and `DROP PROCEDURE` drop it. **Not checked against BigQuery:** the line and column inside a procedure (counted here from its `BEGIN`), and the error messages for an unknown procedure, a wrong argument count, an `OUT` argument that is not a variable and the depth limit. The console's Routines section and routine page show procedures (`TestBigQueryRoutinesSectionAndPage`). Units `TestProcedureParse`, `TestProcedureStackTrace`. |
| Multi-statement transactions: `BEGIN TRANSACTION`, `COMMIT TRANSACTION`, `ROLLBACK TRANSACTION` in a script | **Verified** (#1201) in any script, through `jobs.query` and query jobs, for a transaction whose statements are queries, DML (`SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MERGE`, `TRUNCATE TABLE`), `CREATE TEMP TABLE` and `DROP TABLE` of a `TEMP` table it made, with `DECLARE`, `SET`, control-flow blocks, `BEGIN … EXCEPTION` blocks, `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` and `CALL` of a procedure inside it, its `BEGIN` and its `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK` in any blocks: a statement sees the transaction's earlier writes, `COMMIT` keeps them, `ROLLBACK`, an error with no handler and the end of the query before `COMMIT` discard them, an error goes to an `EXCEPTION` handler with the transaction still open, where `COMMIT` keeps what its statements before the error did and `ROLLBACK` discards it, an error handled inside the transaction leaves it going on, and a nested `BEGIN TRANSACTION` fails the query. BigQuery's own example on the transactions page (a `TEMP` table, `DELETE`, `MERGE` from the `TEMP` table, `DROP TABLE`, `COMMIT`, a handler that rolls back) runs, both ways. **Not implemented** (501): DDL other than the above, a `TEMP` function, and `CREATE` or `DROP PROCEDURE` inside a transaction, and a transaction inside a procedure (nothing run); and, when they run, an expression the script evaluates (a `DECLARE`'s `DEFAULT`, a `SET`, a condition, a `FOR`'s query, `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE … INTO`) that reads a table after the transaction changed data or made a `TEMP` table, a statement after the transaction that names a `TEMP` table it made and did not drop, a statement inside it that names a `TEMP` table it dropped, a `CREATE TEMP TABLE` of a name made before, a transaction statement run by `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`, and a `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK` with no transaction open (undocumented) | `TestBigQueryScriptTransactions` and `TestBigQueryScriptTransactionsMore`, official Go client, through `jobs.query` (`Query.Read`) and `jobs.insert` (`Query.Run`), on one instance with `--services bigquery,storage`. BigQuery: [multi-statement transactions](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/transactions). Measured first against the pinned emulator: it treats `BEGIN TRANSACTION` and `COMMIT TRANSACTION` as statements that do nothing, refuses `ROLLBACK TRANSACTION` ("Statement not supported: RollbackStatement"), and reads the rows of a script's last statement only: `BEGIN TRANSACTION; INSERT …; SELECT 1/0; COMMIT TRANSACTION` succeeded and kept the row. Through `jobs.query` it runs a request in one SQLite transaction, rolled back whole when the request fails (#935); a `TEMP` table lasts for its request, and it cannot drop one inside a script (#936). So the front keeps the transaction itself (`internal/bigqueryfront/transactions.go`), from the `BEGIN TRANSACTION` the script runs to the `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK` it runs, while its interpreter carries out variables and blocks as elsewhere: each statement that changes data, makes a `TEMP` table or reads a table is first run as a probe, a request of the transaction's earlier such statements, the statement (a query as a scalar subquery reading every column of every row) and a statement that fails, so the emulator rolls it all back; a probe that fails with another error is the statement's failure. `DROP TABLE` of its `TEMP` table is kept by the front alone. At `COMMIT` the kept statements are sent as one request, which the emulator applies atomically, all or none; at `ROLLBACK` nothing is sent. The rows of a query inside the transaction that reads a table are not the script's answer. Not as in BigQuery: the DML is applied at `COMMIT` against the tables as they are then, a serial order of the transaction among other requests; BigQuery reads a snapshot from the transaction's first statement and cancels a conflicting transaction. An error's position (`[at line:column]`) in the emulator's message points into the front's request. |
| Loads with `autodetect` and no schema | **Verified** for CSV and for `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` (#1324); **Not implemented** (501) for a JSON column whose values mix types BigQuery does not document detecting, and for `columnNameCharacterMap` `V1` or `V2` when a detected name cannot be renamed by replacing characters (a `V1` name that starts with a digit, a reserved or too long name, two names the same once replaced, a Parquet name with a period); a load of another format under any map is 400 (#1336) | `TestBigQueryAutodetectLoadNames` (#901), `TestBigQueryColumnNameCharacterMap` (#1326), `TestBigQueryColumnNameCharacterMapFormats` (#1336), `TestBigQueryParquetColumnNameCharacterMap` (#1373), official Go client, a load from a local file. The emulator names the columns of a CSV from its first row whatever they hold: a header `a b!,c` made a column `a b!` (measured). BigQuery's rule is the load's `columnNameCharacterMap`: `STRICT`, the default, "reject[s] invalid column names"; `V1` and `V2` normalize them ([JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)). The front does not read the data, so it checks the table the load made, after the emulator ran it: under `STRICT` a name the column rules refuse **fails the job as BigQuery fails it**: the job is `DONE` with an `invalid` `errorResult`, which `Job.Wait`'s status and a later `jobs.get` (`Job.Status`) report, and the table is deleted, as BigQuery creates a load's table only when it succeeds. Under `V1` (the classic rule) or `V2`, whose renaming the emulator ignores (measured: `a!` kept under `V2`), the front **renames the detected columns** (#1326), as BigQuery does: unsupported characters "are replaced with underscores" ([load statements, `column_name_character_map`](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/load-statements)), so each character the map's rule does not take (letters, digits and `_` for `V1`; the flexible rule's for `V2`) becomes `_`, and the table is made again with the new names, its rows copied through a scratch table. Read back through the Go client (`Loader.ColumnNameCharacterMap`, a CSV load from a local file): under `V2` a header `first name,a!,n` gives `first name`, `a_`, `n`, under `V1` `first_name`, `a_`, `n`; the types are kept, `jobs.get` reports the job done, and the rows read back by the new names through a query and `tabledata.list`. A name still refused once replaced (`1a` under `V1`, whose rule for a leading digit BigQuery does not document: "Invalid column names will be normalized"), and two names the same once replaced (`a!`, `a?`), stay **501** and the table is deleted (unit `TestColumnNameCharacterMap`). Since #1336 (`TestBigQueryColumnNameCharacterMapFormats`, official Go client, uploads): the map is refused for a format other than CSV and Parquet, as BigQuery documents ("Character map supported for column names in CSV/Parquet loads ... Using this option with unsupporting load formats will result in an error", [JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)): a `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` load that gives `V1`, `V2` or `STRICT` is 400 `invalid` (wording UNVERIFIED) and nothing is loaded; and a Parquet file's column names are held to it: a name the rules refuse (`!`) is 400 `invalid` under `STRICT` or no map ("Load jobs with unsupported characters in column names fail with an error message"), and under `V1` or `V2` is renamed (`_`); a name the rules take loads under any map (unit `TestCharMapFormat`, `TestParquetCharMapNames`). Since #1373 (`TestBigQueryParquetColumnNameCharacterMap`, official Go client, an upload of a file written by Arrow's Go Parquet writer) a Parquet load under `V1` or `V2` **renames the file's columns** as the documentation says, unsupported characters "(except periods in Parquet file column names) are replaced with underscores", at every depth: the front renames each name as it reads the file's schema and carries the load out itself, each value going to its renamed column. Columns `first name`, `a!` and a RECORD `rec?` with a field `in ner!` read back through `Table.Metadata` as `first_name`, `a_`, `rec_` and `in_ner_` under `V1`, and `first name`, `a_`, `rec_` and `in ner_` under `V2`, the types kept, `jobs.get` reporting the job done, and the rows read back by the new names through a query and `tabledata.list`. As for a CSV, names the same once replaced (`a!`, `a?`) and a name still refused once replaced (`x.y`, its period kept, which no rule takes; `1a` under `V1`) stay **501**, with no table (unit `TestParquetNamesUnderCharMap`). A RECORD's field with a flexible name made no table in the emulator, which wrote it unquoted in its engine's `CREATE TABLE` (measured: "Syntax error: Expected \">\" but got keyword IN"); engine patch bigquery-emulator 0019 quotes it. A header BigQuery takes, `first name,n`, loads its row. A `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` load with `autodetect` into a new table, which the emulator answers 500 "nil pointer dereference" (measured), has its schema **detected by the front** as [schema auto-detection](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/schema-detect) documents it (#1324, `TestBigQueryJSONAutodetectLoad`, official Go client, from a local file and from Cloud Storage, the schema read back with `Table.Metadata` and the rows with a query): from the first 500 records of the first file, a JSON boolean is `BOOLEAN`, an integer `INTEGER`, another number `FLOAT`, and a string `BOOLEAN`, `INTEGER`, `FLOAT`, `DATE`, `TIME` or `TIMESTAMP` when it holds one ("BigQuery converts strings into Boolean, numeric, or date/time types when possible"), `STRING` otherwise; an object a `RECORD`, an array a `REPEATED` column, every other column `NULLABLE`, and a column only ever null `STRING`. `INTEGER` with `FLOAT` is `FLOAT`, and strings of which some hold no other type `STRING`; any other mix, an array of arrays, an object only ever empty, an integer outside INT64 and a date or time in a form other than `YYYY-MM-DD`, `HH:MM:SS[.SSSSSS]` and `YYYY-MM-DD[ T]HH:MM[:SS[.SSSSSS]]` with an optional offset, `Z` or `UTC` are **501**. The detected names are held to `columnNameCharacterMap` as a CSV's are (a refused name under `STRICT` is 400 `invalid`, with no table). The load is then sent with the detected schema; a detected `TIMESTAMP` value is written in RFC 3339 UTC, the one form the emulator reads in every case (measured: it failed `2020-01-02T03:04Z`). A field first seen after the sample is outside the detected schema, which is the load's schema, so its record is bad unless `ignoreUnknownValues` is set, as the JSON loads row below says (#1339, `TestBigQueryLoadFieldsOutsideTheSchema`: a field first seen in record 501 fails the load, and loads under `ignoreUnknownValues` with the schema of the first 500) (unit `TestDetectJSONSchema`). A load into an existing table keeps that table's schema (measured) and is not checked; with no `skipLeadingRows` it is **501** (#945, the CSV loads row below) (unit `TestAutodetectedNamesAreHeldToTheCharacterMap`). The header, a resumable upload, a load from Cloud Storage and `jobs.list` are in the next rows (#919). |
| CSV header detection with `autodetect` | **Verified** where BigQuery and the emulator agree; **Not implemented** (501) where they do not | `TestBigQueryAutodetectHeaderAndResumableLoads` (#919), official Go client. The emulator takes a CSV's first row as the header whatever it holds (measured: `a,b / c,d` gave columns `a` and `b`, `1,2 / 3,4` columns `1` and `2`) and ignores `skipLeadingRows`. BigQuery takes the first row as the header only "if the first line contains only strings, and the other lines contain other data types" ([schema detection](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/schema-detect#csv_header)); otherwise it loads it as data. The front reads both halves of that rule from the table the load made (the first row is the column names; the other rows' types are the columns'), and a load BigQuery would read otherwise is **501**, the table deleted: every column `STRING`, or a name that reads as a number, boolean, date or timestamp. `first name,n / bob,3` loads its row. `skipLeadingRows` other than 1 with `autodetect` into a new table is **501** before it is sent (2 checked; 0, which the Go client cannot send, unit only). Unit `TestCSVHeaderDetection`. |
| Loads with no `sourceFormat` | **Verified** as CSV | Every load in `TestBigQueryAutodetectHeaderAndResumableLoads` sets none, as the Go client sends none for CSV unless told. BigQuery's default is CSV; the emulator has none (measured: 400 "not support sourceFormat: " with a schema, and 500 "nil pointer dereference" with `autodetect`, which the Go client retries until its deadline). The front sets `sourceFormat` `CSV` in the job, in `jobs.insert`'s body or a multipart upload's first part, whose data is sent as it came (unit `TestLoadWithoutSourceFormatIsCSV`). |
| CSV loads with a schema, or into an existing table | **Verified** for a load from the client (multipart and resumable uploads) and from Cloud Storage (#944) | `TestBigQueryCSVLoadWithSchemaLoadsEveryRow` (#931) and `TestBigQueryCSVLoadFromCloudStorage` (#944), official Go client. BigQuery reads every row as data unless told otherwise: `skipLeadingRows` "The default value is 0" ([JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)), and each value goes to the column at its position. The emulator ignores `skipLeadingRows` and always takes the first row as a header (measured, and in its source): a file of three rows with a schema and no header **loaded two, the first lost with no error**, and a file of one row loaded none; `skipLeadingRows` 2 failed the load; and a first row whose values are the columns' names maps the columns by name. The front drops the rows BigQuery skips and puts a header of its own before the rest, the columns' names in order (the load's schema, or the table's when the load gives none), which the emulator takes as the header; the data is streamed, not held in memory. So three rows load three, one loads one, `skipLeadingRows` 1 skips a header `b,a` and still loads by position, `skipLeadingRows` 2 skips a title and a quoted value over two lines, a load into an existing table with no load schema loads every row, and a resumable upload of over 768 KiB loads every row, its first included. **From Cloud Storage (#944):** the emulator reads a `gs://` load's objects itself, so the front reads them instead, from the instance's own Cloud Storage (the in-cluster server the front is started with, `--storage`, never `storage.googleapis.com`), and sends them to the emulator as a multipart upload of the same job without its `sourceUris`, through the same path: each file's leading rows are skipped, the files are loaded as one job in the order of their URIs, and a URI with one `*` wildcard reads every object it matches, in name order, as the emulator's own reader does. So a file of three rows and no header loads three, `skipLeadingRows` 1 skips a header `b,a` and loads by position, `parts/*.csv` with a header in each loads every data row of the two `.csv` objects and not the `.txt`, and two URIs into an existing table load six rows. An object that does not exist, a bucket that does not, or a wildcard that matches nothing is **404 `notFound`** from `jobs.insert` and makes no table (BigQuery fails the job "Not found: URI" instead); so is Cloud Storage that does not answer. With `autodetect` and columns given, `skipLeadingRows` says how many rows are not data (BigQuery: "0 - … no headers", "N > 0 - Autodetect skips N-1 rows and tries to detect headers in row N"); unset, BigQuery decides from the data whether the first row is a header, which the emulator always drops (measured), so that is **501** (the Go client cannot send 0). A load with `autodetect` and no columns, into a new table, keeps its header for the emulator, and a later file's first row is dropped. Unit `TestCSVLoadWithColumnsLoadsEveryRow`, `TestCSVLoadFromCloudStorage`, `TestCSVLoadFromCloudStorageIsRead`, `TestSkipRecords`. |
| CSV loads: `fieldDelimiter`, `quote`, `allowJaggedRows`, `nullMarker` | **Verified** for a one-character ASCII delimiter or quote (or none); **Not implemented** (501) otherwise, and for an empty value with a `nullMarker` in a `STRING` column | `TestBigQueryCSVLoadOptions` (#945), official Go client (`ReaderSource.FieldDelimiter`, `Quote`/`ForceZeroQuote`, `AllowJaggedRows`, `NullMarker`), from the client and from Cloud Storage. Measured first: the emulator reads a load's data with Go's `encoding/csv` defaults: a tab- or pipe-delimited file, a file quoted with `'` and a short row with `allowJaggedRows` failed 400 "wrong number of fields"; with `quote` `""` it loaded `"x"` as `x`; with `nullMarker` `\N` it loaded the text `\N`; it loads every empty value as NULL. The front reads the data by the load's options as it passes and writes it on as the CSV the emulator reads: a tab (`\t` too) or pipe delimiter, `'` quotes with `''` inside, no quoting, short rows filled with NULLs, and `\N` loaded as NULL all read back as BigQuery documents ([JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)); a short row without `allowJaggedRows` still fails. With a `nullMarker`, BigQuery loads an empty value into a `STRING` or `BYTES` column as an empty string, which the emulator cannot load (NULL): **501**, and into another column refuses it: **400 `invalid`**; a quote that is not closed, or data after a closing quote, is 400 `invalid`. These fail the load while its data passes, before the emulator loads anything, and `jobs.get` reports the job failed (unit `TestCSVDialectFailureReadsBackFailed`). A delimiter or quote of more than one character, or outside ASCII, is **501** before anything is sent. **Not covered:** whether BigQuery reads a quoted `"\N"` as the marker (the front does not). The other CSV options are in the next row (#952). Unit `TestCSVDialect`. |
| `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` loads: a field outside the schema, `ignoreUnknownValues`, `maxBadRecords` | **Verified** (#1339); **Not implemented** (501) for a field outside the schema whose value is null, and for a load with `maxBadRecords` that the emulator then fails | `TestBigQueryLoadFieldsOutsideTheSchema`, official Go client, a load from a local file and from Cloud Storage. BigQuery's `ignoreUnknownValues`: "If false, records with extra columns are treated as bad records, and if there are too many bad records, an invalid error is returned in the job result ... JSON: Named values that don't match any column names" ([JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)). The emulator drops such a field and loads the record (measured: `{"i":13,"zz":1}` loaded into a table without `zz`). So the front reads every JSON load whose columns it knows (the table's, the load's schema, which may add to them, or the one it detected) and holds each record to them, names matched without case, at any depth of a `RECORD` and in each element of a `REPEATED` one: a record with a field outside them **fails the load** (400 `invalid`, "No such field: zz" or "No such field: r.y", nothing loaded); with `ignoreUnknownValues` it loads without the field; with `maxBadRecords` 1 it is left out, listed in the job's `status.errors`, and the other records load. A null field outside the schema is **501**, as the reference does not say whether BigQuery counts it as extra. With `maxBadRecords`, a load the emulator fails on a value is **501**, as for CSV: the record may be one BigQuery would leave out. A CSV record with more values than columns follows the same rule (the CSV loads row below, `TestBigQueryLoadFieldsOutsideTheSchema` from a file and from Cloud Storage). A load from Cloud Storage with no Cloud Storage given to the front (`--storage`) is read by the emulator, which drops the field (unit `TestJSONLoadUnknownFields`). |
| CSV loads: `allowQuotedNewlines`, `encoding`, `maxBadRecords`, `ignoreUnknownValues`, `nullMarkers`, `preserveAsciiControlCharacters`, `sourceColumnMatch`, REQUIRED columns; `timeZone` and the date and time formats | **Verified** for each, C-style (`%m/%d/%Y`) formats and `timeZone` or a format with `autodetect` and no schema among them (#1338), but `sourceColumnMatch` `NAME` with a `skipLeadingRows` other than 1, and, with `autodetect` and a format or `timeZone`, a sample BigQuery's detection is not documented for (below), which are **Not implemented** (501) | `TestBigQueryCSVLoadTimeFormatsAndEncodings` (#1325), official Go client (`FileConfig.TimeZone`, `DateFormat`, `DatetimeFormat`, `TimeFormat`, `TimestampFormat`, `Encoding`), from a local file and from Cloud Storage, the rows read back with a query: each format is read with BigQuery's SQL-style [format elements](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/format-elements#format_string_as_datetime) (`MM/DD/YYYY`, `DD.MM.YYYY HH24:MI`, `HH12:MI P.M.`, `YYYY/MM/DD HH24:MI:SS`; "this format is the only compatible DATE format"), by the code the engine's `CAST ... FORMAT` uses, and the value written in the form the emulator reads; a value outside its format makes its record bad (left out under `maxBadRecords`, otherwise **400 `invalid`**), a format the elements cannot parse with and an unknown `timeZone` are **400 `invalid`**. `timeZone` (a tz database name or an offset) is the zone of a TIMESTAMP with none, in a format or in the default forms (`YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY/MM/DD`, `T` or a space, `HH:MM[:SS[.SSSSSS]]`); one with a zone keeps it. UTF-16BE, UTF-16LE, UTF-32BE and UTF-32LE data (`café 😀`, with a byte-order mark) loads as its text: the front decodes it to UTF-8 before it reads the records, a leading byte-order mark dropped and an unpaired surrogate read as U+FFFD (the reference's "decodes the data after the raw, binary data has been split" cannot hold byte for byte where a comma is two or four bytes); an unknown `encoding` is **400 `invalid`**. Measured first, the emulator ignored all of them. A C-style format (#1338, same test: `%m/%d/%Y`, `%d.%m.%Y %H:%M`, `%I:%M %p`, `%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S`, loading the same rows from a file and from Cloud Storage), which the Go client's `FileConfig` says BigQuery "Supports" and the REST reference does not describe, is read with GoogleSQL's [format elements for PARSE_DATE and its kin](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/format-elements#format_elements_date_time), by the engine's own parser (a copy, each literal character held to the value's); an element its type does not take (`%H` in a `dateFormat`) is **400 `invalid`**, and a TIMESTAMP whose format reads no zone (`%z`, `%Z`, `%Ez`, `%s`) is in `timeZone`. With `autodetect`, no schema, a new table and a format or `timeZone` (#1338, same test: `dateFormat` `%m/%d/%Y` and `timeZone` `America/New_York`, the schema read back with `Table.Metadata`), the front detects the schema, as "Schema autodetection will also decide DATE column type based on this format" and "this format is the only compatible DATE format" (loading-data-cloud-storage-csv), from the header and the first 500 records of the first file: a value its type's format parses is of that type, one in that type's default form a `STRING` (`2018-12-03` under `%m/%d/%Y`), any other typed as a JSON string is (the autodetect row above), the types of a column resolved as a JSON field's; the load is then sent with that schema and its values converted. **501**: a first row that is not all strings over a typed column (BigQuery would load it as data and name the columns), columns all `STRING`, a mix of types not documented, records of different widths, and a delimiter of more than one character, a `quote` or an `encoding` of its own (unit `TestDetectCSVSchema`). `TestBigQueryCSVLoadOtherOptions` (#952), official Go client (`ReaderSource.AllowQuotedNewlines`, `Encoding`, `MaxBadRecords`, `IgnoreUnknownValues`, `NullMarkers`, `PreserveASCIIControlCharacters`, `SourceColumnMatch`, `TimeZone`, `DateFormat`, a `Required` field). Measured first, with a header row the emulator takes as one: it loaded a quoted newline whatever `allowQuotedNewlines` said; under `encoding` ISO-8859-1 it stored the byte 0xE9 as U+FFFD; with `maxBadRecords` 1 it failed a load with one bad value (400 "strconv.ParseInt") or one row too wide (400 "wrong number of fields"), and failed the wide row the same way with `ignoreUnknownValues`; it loaded the values of `nullMarkers` as text; it stored `\x00` and `\x01` as they were whatever `preserveAsciiControlCharacters` said; it stored a TIMESTAMP with no zone as UTC whatever `timeZone` said, and failed a DATE in `dateFormat` `MM/DD/YYYY` (#1325 above); it stored NULL in a REQUIRED column given an empty value; it matched a header's names to the columns by name. The front reads each record by BigQuery's rules as the data passes ([JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)): a quoted newline loads with `allowQuotedNewlines` and is **400 `invalid`** without it; ISO-8859-1 data reads back as `café`; a record that is too short (without `allowJaggedRows`), too wide (without `ignoreUnknownValues`, which drops the trailing values) or leaves a REQUIRED column without a value is bad, up to `maxBadRecords` of them are left out and one more is **400 `invalid`**; each value of `nullMarkers` loads as NULL; a control character loads with `preserveAsciiControlCharacters`; with `sourceColumnMatch` `NAME` and `skipLeadingRows` 1, each value goes to the column its header names. **501**, and nothing is loaded: a load with `maxBadRecords` the emulator then fails (on a value its column's type refuses, which BigQuery may count as a bad record); a quoted newline without `allowQuotedNewlines` in a row `skipLeadingRows` skips, or with `maxBadRecords`; a control character other than tab, newline and carriage return without `preserveAsciiControlCharacters`; an empty value that is not one of the `nullMarkers`; an empty quoted value in a REQUIRED `STRING` or `BYTES` column; a `NAME` header that does not name each column once (the reference documents none of these cases). `nullMarker` with `nullMarkers` is **400 `invalid`**. The job reports the records it left out (next row, #960). **Not covered:** a load from Cloud Storage with no Cloud Storage for the front to read passes these checks by (#944). Units `TestCSVLoadOptions`, `TestCSVLoadOptionsRefused`, `TestCSVTimesConvert`, `TestWideReader`, `TestParseDatetime`. |
| CSV loads: the job's `statistics.load` (`badRecords`, `outputRows`, `inputFiles`, `inputFileBytes`) and the bad records left out in `status.errors`, on `jobs.insert`, `jobs.get` and `jobs.list` | **Verified** for a load whose records the front reads; `outputBytes` is **Not covered** | `TestBigQueryCSVLoadReportsBadRecords` (#960), official Go client (`JobStatus.Errors`, `JobStatus.Statistics.Details.(*bigquery.LoadStatistics)` `OutputRows`, `InputFiles`, `InputFileBytes`, from `Loader.Run`, `Job.Wait` and `Client.Jobs`), and, as that client's `LoadStatistics` has no `BadRecords`, the official generated client it is built on, `google.golang.org/api/bigquery/v2` (`JobStatistics3.BadRecords` from `Jobs.Get` and `Jobs.List`). Measured first, on the front of #952: a load with `maxBadRecords` 2 left two bad records out and read back from `jobs.get` with no statistics and no errors (the emulator's upload job is the job as sent, [JobStatistics3](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobStatistics3)). The front counts a load's data as it reads it: the files and their bytes, the rows written on, the bad records left out; the first 100 bad records (CloudBurrow's bound; BigQuery lists "the first errors") are each an `invalid` error in `status.errors`, located at the file's `gs://` URI for a load from Cloud Storage, and the job does not fail. A load with `ignoreUnknownValues` trims its wide records and reports `badRecords` 0. `outputBytes` is not reported (#965, next row). A load whose records the front does not read is counted around it (#966, the row after). Units `TestCSVLoadReportsBadRecords`, `TestCSVLoadReportsNoBadRecords`, `TestCSVLoadBadRecordsListed`, `TestCSVLoadFromCloudStorageReportsBadRecords`, `TestCSVLoadReportForgotten`. |
| A load's `statistics.load.outputBytes` | **Not covered**: left out | BigQuery documents it only as "Output only. Size of the loaded data in bytes. Note that while a load job is in the running state, this value may change." ([JobStatistics3](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobStatistics3); the same words in the official generated Go client, `google.golang.org/api/bigquery/v2` `JobStatistics3.OutputBytes`). That is not the size of the data sent, which is `inputFileBytes`, and neither the reference nor any public source found says how the size is taken (whether it is the table's `numBytes` growth, or the logical sizes of [data size calculation](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/pricing#data_size_calculation), which are documented for query pricing, not for loads). The emulator keeps no stored size to read: its `tables.get` reports `numBytes` 0 after a load (measured, with the official Go client's `TableMetadata.NumBytes`). So the front does not report it, and the official Go client reads `LoadStatistics.OutputBytes` as 0 (`TestBigQueryLoadsReportCounts` checks it is 0, #965; unit `TestCSVLoadReportsBadRecords` that it is left out). |
| Loads whose records the front does not read: the job's `statistics.load` (`outputRows`, `inputFiles`, `inputFileBytes`) and status, on `jobs.insert`, `jobs.get` and `jobs.list` | **Verified** for a `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` or Parquet upload (new table, appended, `WRITE_TRUNCATE`), a CSV upload the front passes on as it is, and a `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` load from Cloud Storage (two URIs, and a wildcard); **Not covered**: `badRecords` for these, and `inputFiles` and `inputFileBytes` of a load from Cloud Storage with no Cloud Storage given to the front | `TestBigQueryLoadsReportCounts` (#966), official Go client (`JobStatus.State`, `JobStatus.Statistics.Details.(*bigquery.LoadStatistics)` `OutputRows`, `InputFiles`, `InputFileBytes`, from `Loader.Run`, `Job.Wait` and `Client.Jobs`), and the official generated client, `google.golang.org/api/bigquery/v2` (`Jobs.Get`). Measured first, on the front of #960: each of these loads read back from `jobs.get` with `DONE` and no `statistics.load`, and from `jobs.insert` and `jobs.list` with no status at all (for an upload) or with no `statistics.load` (from Cloud Storage), so the Go client's `JobStatus.Statistics` was nil or had no load details; an `AVRO` or `ORC` load is 400 "not support sourceFormat" from the emulator, which loads no other format, so it has nothing to report. The front counts such a load around it: **`outputRows`** is the destination table's rows after the load (`tables.get`'s `numRows`, which the emulator counts in the table) less those before it, or all of them after a `WRITE_TRUNCATE`, which the emulator carries out in the same transaction as the load; **`inputFiles`** and **`inputFileBytes`** are the upload's, one file and the bytes of its data as they pass through the front unchanged, or for a load from Cloud Storage the objects the emulator reads (a URI with no wildcard, or every object listed under a wildcard's prefix whose name ends with the text after it, as its source, `importFromGCS`, matches them) and their sizes in the instance's Cloud Storage; a CSV load from Cloud Storage the front reads (#944), and since #1079 every JSON load from Cloud Storage (row "A load of several objects from Cloud Storage"), has the files and bytes it read. The job's status is `DONE`, as the load has run when `jobs.insert` answers. `badRecords` is left out (the Go client reads 0): the emulator fails a load on its first bad record (measured, #952), so a load that succeeded left none out, but the front does not read the records to say what BigQuery would count. **Not covered:** a write to the same table by another request while the load runs is counted in its `outputRows`; a load into another project's table has no `outputRows`; a load from Cloud Storage with no Cloud Storage given to the front (`--storage`) has no `inputFiles` or `inputFileBytes`. A Parquet load with no schema in the job is 500 from the emulator (measured; #970), and a load job's times are not BigQuery's (#971). A failed load reports no counts. Units `TestJSONLoadReportsCounts`, `TestCloudStorageLoadReportsCounts`, `TestCSVLoadReportForgotten`. |
| Parquet loads: the file's columns and types against the table's, nested and repeated columns, converted types and schema changes | **Verified** for flat, nested and repeated columns of the types listed, into a new table, appended to one that exists (by name, in any case), with `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION` and `ALLOW_FIELD_RELAXATION`, and replacing one (`WRITE_TRUNCATE`, `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA`), from an upload and from Cloud Storage; **400** where BigQuery refuses the file's columns; **Not implemented** (501) for the rest listed | `TestBigQueryParquetLoadWithoutSchema` (#970), `TestBigQueryParquetLoadColumns` and `TestBigQueryParquetLoadTypes` (#988), `TestBigQueryParquetConvertedTypes` (#1005), `TestBigQueryParquetNestedColumns` (#1004), `TestBigQueryParquetSchemaChanges` (#1006), `TestBigQueryParquetColumnNameCharacterMap` (#1373: a flexible column name such as `first name` loads under `STRICT`, the default, as it is, carried out by the front; renaming under `columnNameCharacterMap` is in the autodetect loads row above), official Go client (`ReaderSource` and `GCSReference` with `SourceFormat` Parquet, `ParquetOptions`, `DecimalTargetTypes`, `SchemaUpdateOptions`, `WriteDisposition`) and, for `parquetOptions.mapTargetType`, which that client lacks, the generated one; files written by Apache Arrow's Parquet writer (pyarrow 25.0.1, `internal/bigqueryfront/testdata/parquet/gen.py`; the ENUM files by Arrow's Go writer, `genenum.go`, as pyarrow writes no ENUM). BigQuery reads a Parquet file's schema from the file ("the table schema is automatically retrieved from the self-describing source data", [Parquet loads](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data-cloud-storage-parquet)). Measured first: the emulator reads a Parquet file's columns only from the job's schema and each row's values by those names, checking nothing (its source: `uploadContentHandler`, `load.Schema.Fields`): with no schema a load was 500 "nil pointer dereference"; given the table's, into `(a INT64)` a file `(a INT64, b STRING)` dropped `b`, into `(z STRING)` it loaded three rows of NULL, into `(a STRING, b STRING)` it loaded `a` as text, and a file's `A` and `B` loaded NULL into `a` and `b`; it loaded TIME(MILLIS) 01:02:03.004 as 00:12:06.004, TIME(MICROS) 01:02:03.004567 as 01:02:07.567, TIMESTAMP(MILLIS) in 2024 as January 1970, BYTES 0xFF as EF BF BD, and refused INT96 ("failed to convert … to time.Time"); against the image directly, given BigQuery's schema for each shape, a LIST read without list inference failed "failed to convert struct from string", with list inference a NULL list read back NULL and a NULL element was kept, and a MAP left the emulator hung, answering nothing until it was restarted. Its JSON load is no way round it: BYTES given as base64 loaded the base64 text (`/w==` read back `2f773d3d`). So the front reads the file's schema from its footer (`parquetfooter.go`) before anything is sent, and holds it to BigQuery's rules. A load the emulator carries out as BigQuery does (flat columns of BOOLEAN, INT32 with no annotation, INT(8, 16, 32, signed or not), DATE, INT64 with no annotation, TIMESTAMP(MICROS) and BYTE_ARRAY STRING, into a new table, appended by exact names, or replacing a table of the file's schema) is sent to it with the schema to read the file by. Any other is **the front's own job** (`parquetload.go`, as a copy job is): it reads the rows with Apache Arrow's Parquet reader for Go (`github.com/apache/arrow/go/v15/parquet/file`, already in the module graph through the BigQuery client; tested with uncompressed, SNAPPY and ZSTD files, dictionary pages, version 2 data pages and several row groups), puts nested rows back together from their definition and repetition levels, writes each as a GoogleSQL literal of the table's row type, and inserts them with DML into a scratch table and then the table (measured: the emulator stores DML values of every type here exactly, RECORD inside REPEATED RECORD included); the job reports `inputFiles`, `inputFileBytes`, `outputRows` and `badRecords` 0, and `jobs.get` reads it back with the client's configuration (the source format PARQUET). **Types** by the page's "Type conversions" table, each read back as written with a row of NULLs: BOOLEAN; INT32 with no annotation, INT(8, 16, 32, signed or not) and DATE; INT64 with no annotation and TIMESTAMP(MICROS); FLOAT and DOUBLE (FLOAT64, ±Inf); BYTE_ARRAY STRING (`é☃` included); converted by the front: TIME(MILLIS), TIME(MICROS), TIMESTAMP(MILLIS), INT96 (nanoseconds of the day and Julian day), BYTE_ARRAY and FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY BYTES, unsigned INT64 up to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 (above it the job fails `invalid`, as the page says), DECIMAL as INT32, INT64, FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY and 256-bit into NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC by `decimalTargetTypes` ("In the order of NUMERIC, BIGNUMERIC, and STRING, a type is picked if it is in the specified list and if it supports the precision and the scale", default `["NUMERIC"]`; a value beyond the widest type's range fails the job `invalid`), and ENUM as BYTES or, with `enumAsString`, STRING. **Nested and repeated**: "Nested groups are converted into STRUCT types", so a group is a RECORD and, without list inference, a LIST or MAP a RECORD holding a REPEATED RECORD (`l RECORD (list REPEATED RECORD (element))`, `m RECORD (key_value REPEATED RECORD (key, value))`); with `parquetOptions.enableListInference` a LIST in the standard form is `repeated <element-type>`, a NULL list read back empty, and so is one in Parquet's backward-compatible forms (a repeated primitive, a repeated group of several fields or named `array` or `<name>_tuple`, pyarrow's `item`; #1069, unit `TestParquetListElement` only, not yet run against files from those writers); with `mapTargetType` `ARRAY_OF_STRUCT` a MAP is a REPEATED RECORD of key and value. **Into a new table** the table takes the file's schema, a REQUIRED column REQUIRED. **Appending**, columns match by name without regard to case at every depth ("Column names from Parquet files are treated as case-insensitive"), and a table column the file lacks is left NULL (as [LOAD DATA](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/load-statements) documents for a self-describing file; not measured against BigQuery). **Schema changes** ([Modifying table schemas](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas)): `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION` adds the file's new NULLABLE columns at the end, and a field it adds inside a RECORD (REPEATED included) at the end of that RECORD ("New columns and nested fields are always added at the end of the table or field"; #1068, unit `TestParquetAddsNestedFields` only, not yet run against an instance), NULL in the table's rows; the emulator adds no engine column through `tables.patch` (#1010) or `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` (measured: success, then "Column c is not present"), so the table is made again with the new schema, keeping its description, labels, partitioning and clustering (its creation time is new); `ALLOW_FIELD_RELAXATION` sets the column NULLABLE (`tables.patch`: the engine does not hold a REQUIRED column to it, measured); `WRITE_TRUNCATE` with a file whose schema is not the table's makes the table again with the file's schema ("overwrites the data, removes the constraints and uses the schema from the load job"); `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` keeps the table's schema and replaces its rows. The rows go to a scratch table first (in `_cloudburrow_query_results`, deleted later while the instance is idle, #1091, as the front's other scratch tables, #1057), so a load that fails leaves the table as it was, or, if it fails after the table was made again, names the scratch table holding the rows. **400** `invalid`, nothing loaded and the table unchanged: a file column the table lacks ("Cannot add fields", at any depth), a column of another type ("has changed type"), a NULLABLE file column into a REQUIRED one without `ALLOW_FIELD_RELAXATION` ("has changed mode"), a REQUIRED table column the file lacks, data that is not a Parquet file, files of one load from Cloud Storage whose columns differ only in mode, an unknown `writeDisposition` or `mapTargetType`. The messages follow BigQuery's form but were not measured against it. **501** `notImplemented`, nothing loaded: a NaN (the emulator's engine stores it as NULL, measured); an INT96 with a part of a microsecond, and a DECIMAL that NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC would have to round (the page does not say whether BigQuery truncates or rounds); DECIMAL to STRING (the page does not say how it is written); a STRING or ENUM-as-STRING value that is not UTF-8; with list inference a NULL element, a LIST of lists, and a LIST in neither the standard form nor a backward-compatible one; `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION` of a REQUIRED column ("allow adding a nullable field"); a STRING column into GEOGRAPHY; types the table does not list (TIMESTAMP(NANOS), TIME(NANOS), JSON, UUID); `referenceFileSchemaUri`; files of one load whose schemas differ otherwise (BigQuery takes the alphabetically last file's); another project's table; a view; a job schema that is not the file's; a dry run of a load the front carries out. Units `TestParquetFooterSchema`, `TestParquetFooterRefusesOtherData`, `FuzzParquetFooter`, `TestParquetLoadColumns`, `TestParquetUploadIsSentWhole`, `TestParquetLoadFromCloudStorage`, `TestParquetLoadsTheFrontCarriesOut`, `TestParquetLoadValuesRefused`, `TestParquetLoadFailuresLeaveTheTable`, `TestParquetLoadFromCloudStorageTheFrontCarriesOut`, `TestParquetLiterals`. |
| `BYTES` values written by a JSON load, a CSV load and a streamed row (`tabledata.insertAll`) | **Verified**, any bytes, at the top level, in a `RECORD` and in a `REPEATED` column, from an upload and from Cloud Storage | `TestBigQueryBytesValuesAreWrittenAsTheirBytes` (#1065, #1075), official Go client (`ReaderSource`, `GCSReference`, `Inserter.Put` of a `[]byte`). BigQuery reads a JSON, CSV or streamed `BYTES` value as base64. Measured first through the front, on the pinned emulator: `/w==` (0xff) loaded by `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` and by CSV, and `[]byte{0xff}` put with `Inserter.Put`, each read back `TO_HEX` `2f773d3d`, the base64 text, with no error: the emulator bound each value to its engine as the string it read (`AddTableData`), and the engine stores a string as its bytes. #1074 had the front send the decoded bytes as a string, which could carry only UTF-8 text (501 for the rest). The emulator CloudBurrow builds decodes the base64 itself (#1061, bigquery-emulator patch 0001, which also hands a JSON load's nested fields to it), so every value reads back as its bytes: `YQBi`, `4piD`, `YWJj`, `DQo=`, `AA==` and `/w==` read back `610062`, `e29883`, `616263`, `0d0a`, `00` and `ff`, at the top level, in a `RECORD` and in a `REPEATED` column, by a JSON upload and load from Cloud Storage, a CSV upload (a carriage return included) and load from Cloud Storage, and `Inserter.Put` (`a\x00b`, `0xff`). The front still reads the records of a JSON or CSV load into a `BYTES` column, and a streamed row, to refuse a value that is not base64 as BigQuery does and to send one in the URL-safe alphabet, which BigQuery reads too, in the standard one the emulator decodes; a JSON load from Cloud Storage is read by it and sent as one upload when it has Cloud Storage, and sent on as it came when it has none. **400** `invalid`: a JSON value that is not base64 (nothing is loaded), and a line of a JSON load that is not one JSON object; a streamed value that is not base64 makes its row invalid. Units `TestJSONLoadChecksBytes`, `TestJSONLoadRefusesWhatItCannotWrite`, `TestJSONLoadFromCloudStorageIsRead`, `TestCSVLoadChecksBytes`, `TestInsertAllChecksBytes`, and the patch's `TestDecodeBytesValues`. |
| `FLOAT64` NaN, ±Infinity and -0 | **Verified** for NaN, written by every path and computed, and for ±Infinity; **Not supported** for -0 | `TestBigQueryNaNIsWrittenAndReadBack` (#1066), official Go client (`ReaderSource`, `GCSReference`, `Query.Parameters`) and, for `tabledata.insertAll`, the generated client (the Go client cannot marshal a NaN or an infinity). BigQuery's `FLOAT64` "includes NaN". Measured first through the front, on the pinned emulator: its engine keeps `FLOAT64` values as SQLite REALs and SQLite makes a NaN NULL, both when it is bound and when a function returns one, so a NaN from a JSON load, a CSV load, a query parameter and `IEEE_DIVIDE(0, 0)` each read back NULL (`IS_NAN` NULL), even `SELECT IEEE_DIVIDE(0, 0)`, and `CAST('NaN' AS FLOAT64)` was refused, 400 "failed to format query"; #1074 had the front answer 501 for the NaNs it could see. The engine CloudBurrow builds keeps a NaN (#1061, googlesqlite patch 0004, whose `TestNaNIsKept` covers `CAST('NaN' AS FLOAT64)`, a NaN parameter, arithmetic, `SUM` and `COUNTIF(IS_NAN(f))`), and the front sends each write on: a NaN in a `FLOAT64` column (top level, `RECORD`, `REPEATED`) of a JSON load (upload and Cloud Storage) and a CSV load (`NaN`, `nan`; upload and Cloud Storage), a streamed row, a query parameter of an `INSERT`, and `IEEE_DIVIDE(0, 0)` in an `INSERT`, each reads back `IS_NAN` true, and `SELECT @p` of a NaN parameter and `SELECT IEEE_DIVIDE(0, 0)` read NaN. **Not supported**: -0 reads back 0 through each write (its sign is lost, #1076; `CAST(x AS STRING)` of a `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT -0.0` reads `-0`), and is not refused, as BigQuery's handling of it is not documented; an infinity inside a `RECORD` or an `ARRAY`, from a JSON load or computed by a statement (`INSERT … SELECT [CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64)]`), which the pinned engine refused, 400 "json: unsupported value" (#1077), is written and read back since #1061 (`TestBigQueryInfinityInsideCompositeValues`; googlesqlite patch 0004). **±Infinity** from a JSON load (`"Infinity"`, `"-Infinity"`), a CSV load (`inf`, `-inf`), `tabledata.insertAll` and a query parameter reads back `IS_INF` with its sign. | `writeDisposition` `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` of a load, and a query job's `writeDisposition` | **Verified** for JSON and CSV loads, from an upload and from Cloud Storage (Parquet: row above), and for a query job's `WRITE_TRUNCATE`, `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` (with the result's columns in another order, missing a NULLABLE column, into `REQUIRED` columns and fields, #1083), `WRITE_EMPTY` and `WRITE_APPEND`; **Not implemented** (501) for a query job's `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` whose result column has another type or `REPEATED` mode than the table's, that leaves out a column with a default value, or whose `schemaUpdateOptions` would relax a column or add a field inside a RECORD (#1110); `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION` adds the result's new top-level columns at the end of the table, NULLABLE (#1110, unit `TestQueryJobWriteDispositions` only) | `TestBigQueryWriteTruncateDataReplacesTheRows` (#1067, #1080, #1083), official Go client (`Loader.WriteDisposition`, `Query.Dst`, `Query.WriteDisposition`, `Client.JobFromID`). BigQuery: "WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA: If the table already exists, BigQuery overwrites the data, but keeps the constraints and schema of the existing table". Measured first through the front: a JSON and a CSV upload, and a JSON load of two objects from Cloud Storage, each with `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` into a table with rows, kept the rows and added the load's (the emulator knows only `WRITE_TRUNCATE` and `WRITE_EMPTY`), and the job succeeded. The emulator's `WRITE_TRUNCATE` of a table that exists deletes its rows in the same transaction as it inserts the load's, and keeps the table's schema; so the front sends `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` to it as `WRITE_TRUNCATE`, and the job reads back `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` (`jobs.insert`, `jobs.get`) with `outputRows` the rows loaded. Read back: after each of a JSON upload, a CSV upload, a JSON load of two objects and a CSV load from Cloud Storage, the table holds only the load's rows, with its schema and description; into a table that does not exist the load makes it. A query job with a destination table: the emulator appends the result whatever `writeDisposition` says (measured: `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA`, `WRITE_TRUNCATE` and `WRITE_EMPTY` each appended to a table with rows; 501 from #1067), so since #1080 the front carries them out into a table that exists ([JobConfigurationQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationQuery), `querywrite.go`). **`WRITE_EMPTY`** (the default) into a table with rows fails the job, reason `duplicate`, "Already Exists: Table project:dataset.table", and runs nothing ("If the table already exists and contains data, a 'duplicate' error is returned in the job result"); read back: the table unchanged. **`WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA`** and **`WRITE_TRUNCATE`** run the query into a scratch table of the dataset first (so a query that reads the table reads it as it was, and one that fails leaves it: read back after `SELECT ERROR('no')`), then replace the table's rows with the result's in one script, `DELETE` and `INSERT … SELECT`, which the emulator runs in one transaction (measured: a failed script given to `jobs.query` left the rows), when the result's columns are the table's, or the job is `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA`; read back: `SELECT id + 1, … FROM t UNION ALL SELECT 20, 'u'` into `t` replaced its rows with those two, and the table kept its schema and description. **`WRITE_TRUNCATE`** with other columns "uses the schema from the query result": the table is made again with the result's schema, keeping its description, labels, expiration, partitioning and clustering and not its constraints (as a Parquet load's `WRITE_TRUNCATE`), and the result copied in; read back: `SELECT 1.5 AS z, [1, 2] AS arr` made the table `(z FLOAT, arr REPEATED INTEGER)` with its description. Those are two steps (the emulator adds no column through `tables.patch`, #1010): should the copy fail, the job fails `backendError` naming the scratch table that holds the result. `jobs.insert` and `jobs.get` show the client's destination and `writeDisposition`; the job's rows are read through `jobs.getQueryResults`, which the emulator answers from the job (measured: read back after the scratch table was deleted); no scratch table is left. **`WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` keeps the table's schema** (#1083), and the result is written into it as BigQuery writes a query's result into a table it appends to: [`schemaUpdateOptions`](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationQuery.FIELDS.schema_update_options) are "supported … when writeDisposition is WRITE_APPEND; when writeDisposition is WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA", and BigQuery's samples of such an append ([Add columns in a query append job](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas#add_columns_in_a_query_append_job), and relaxing a column in one) write `SELECT "Timmy" as full_name, 85 as age, "Blue" as favorite_color` into a table of `full_name` and `age`, both `REQUIRED`, with `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION`, and `SELECT "Beyonce" as full_name` into it with `ALLOW_FIELD_RELAXATION`, which makes `age` NULLABLE for the row that has none: a result's columns are the table's by name, a result column is written into a `REQUIRED` one, a column the result does not have is NULL only when it is NULLABLE, and a result column the table does not have needs `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION`. So the front writes each of the table's columns from the result's of its name, at any depth, a `RECORD` rebuilt by name in the table's order, and a column the result does not have NULL (a `REPEATED` one empty); the engine has no `NOT NULL`, so the front first counts the result's rows with NULL where the table has a `REQUIRED` column or field. Read back: `SELECT 'r' AS s, 41 AS id` into `(id, s)` wrote `41, r`; `SELECT 'only s' AS s` wrote `NULL, only s`; `SELECT 'a1' AS a, 1 AS b, STRUCT(9 AS y, 'k' AS x) AS r` into `(a REQUIRED, b, r RECORD<x REQUIRED, y>)` wrote `a1, 1, k, 9` and kept the schema. **The job fails**, reason `invalid`, the table unchanged: a result column the table does not have (`SELECT 1.5 AS z`), a NULL for a `REQUIRED` column or field (`CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS a`, `STRUCT(CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS x, …)`), and a `REQUIRED` column the result does not have (`SELECT 3 AS b`); BigQuery's wording of these errors is UNVERIFIED. **501** `notImplemented`, nothing run: a result column of another type (`SELECT 1.5 AS id` into an `INTEGER` column: whether BigQuery coerces is not documented) or `REPEATED` mode, a missing column that has a default value (whether BigQuery writes its default is not documented), and `schemaUpdateOptions` `ALLOW_FIELD_RELAXATION` into a table with a `REQUIRED` column, or `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION` of a field inside a RECORD, which CloudBurrow does not carry out for a query job; `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION` of a top-level column is carried out, the table made again with the column at its end, NULLABLE, keeping its other properties and constraints (the emulator adds no engine column through `tables.patch`, #1010); either destination when it is a view, or when the query is not one `SELECT`. A dry run, `WRITE_APPEND` and a destination that does not exist are sent on. A load of several objects from Cloud Storage is one transaction since #1079 (row "A load of several objects from Cloud Storage"). Units `TestWriteTruncateDataIsSentAsWriteTruncate`, `TestQueryDestinationWriteDispositions`, `TestQueryJobWriteDispositions`, `TestConvertColumns`, `TestNullViolations`. |

| `BYTES` query parameters, `STRUCT` query parameters, and `RANGE` query parameters | **Verified** for a `BYTES` and an `ARRAY<BYTES>` parameter, named or positional, through `jobs.query` and `jobs.insert`, and since #1082 for a `STRUCT` parameter and an `ARRAY` of them, with `BYTES` fields at any depth, and since #1111 for a `RANGE<DATE>`, `RANGE<DATETIME>` or `RANGE<TIMESTAMP>` parameter, named or positional, at the top level, in an `ARRAY` or inside a `STRUCT`, with `UNBOUNDED` bounds (`TestBigQueryRangeParameters`: measured first, the emulator read a top-level `RANGE<DATE>` parameter as a NULL INTEGER; the front sends it built as `RANGE(start, end)` of its bounds, sent as `STRUCT` leaves are, both bounds `UNBOUNDED` as `RANGE<T> '[UNBOUNDED, UNBOUNDED)'` since the emulator refuses `RANGE(NULL, NULL)`, a NULL one a typed NULL; read back as sent, with `RANGE_CONTAINS`, `RANGE_START` and `RANGE_END`), and since #1101 for reading a whole `STRUCT` with a `TIMESTAMP` field | `TestBigQueryBytesParameters` (#1078), official Go client (`Query.Parameters` with a `[]byte` and a `[][]byte`, `Client.JobFromID`). BigQuery takes a `BYTES` parameter's value as base64 and types the parameter `BYTES`. Measured first through the front, on the pinned emulator: `INSERT INTO ds.t (id, b) VALUES (1, @p)` with `@p` the bytes `ff 00 61` failed 400 "Value has type STRING which cannot be inserted into column b, which has type BYTES", `TO_HEX(@p)` failed "No matching signature … STRING", an `ARRAY<BYTES>` read back as its base64 texts, and `@p.x` of a `STRUCT` with a `BYTES` field failed "Cannot access field x on a value with type STRING": the emulator hands its engine the value as a string (its source, `queryParameterValueToGoValue`), which the engine types `STRING`. `FROM_BASE64` of the same text as a `STRING` parameter read back `ff0061` (measured). So the front sends a `BYTES` parameter as a `STRING` of its standard base64 and each reference to it as `FROM_BASE64(@p)`, and an `ARRAY<BYTES>` as an `ARRAY<STRING>` referred to as the array of its elements' bytes in order (NULL when it is NULL); positional parameters are sent as named ones (`@cloudburrow_p1` …), so that one can be referred to twice. The references are found by the front's lexer, so a string literal or comment is not changed. Read back: `SELECT @p` returns the bytes `ff 00 61` exactly, `TO_HEX(@p)` `ff0061`, `'@p'` the text `@p`, a positional `?` and a NULL the same, an `INSERT` of `@p` and of an `ARRAY<BYTES>` stores `ff0061`, `WHERE b = @p` finds it, and `jobs.get` shows the client's text and parameters. Before #1101 it failed in the Go client, as any `TIMESTAMP` inside a `RECORD` read back as the engine's text. The other scalar types at the top level are the emulator's (#1108). **Not covered**: a Go client `[]byte{}` is sent with no value, which the emulator reads as NULL, as the Go client does not send an empty base64 text. Units `TestBytesParameters`, `TestBytesParameterJobShowsTheClients`. |

In BigQuery a parameter has the type its `parameterType` names. Measured first through the front with the Go client, on the pinned emulator: `SELECT @p` read back a `STRING` of the text for `NUMERIC` 123.45, `BIGNUMERIC`, `DATE`, `TIME`, `GEOGRAPHY`, `JSON` and `INTERVAL`, and a `TIMESTAMP` for a `DATETIME`, and a positional `NUMERIC` failed "strconv.ParseInt: parsing … invalid syntax"; `CAST` of the same text as a `STRING` read back each as sent, `ST_GEOGFROMTEXT` a `GEOGRAPHY` and `PARSE_JSON` a `JSON` (a `CAST` to either is refused). So the front sends such a parameter as the `STRING` of its value, each reference to it as its conversion (`CAST(@p AS NUMERIC)` …), as it sends a `BYTES` one (previous row), an `ARRAY` of them as an `ARRAY<STRING>` read back element by element in order, and one with a NULL element (which the emulator reads as `''` in an `ARRAY<STRING>`, measured) as a typed `ARRAY<…>[…]` of its elements; positional parameters as named ones. | `NULL` arguments of `ARRAY_TO_STRING`, `ARRAY_CONCAT`, `ARRAY_REVERSE` and the `NET.` functions; an emulator 500 to a query | **Verified** NULL as in BigQuery, and a prompt 400 for a query the emulator answers 500 | `TestBigQueryNullArgumentsOfArrayFunctions` (#1109), official Go client (`Query.Read`, `Query.Run`, `Job.Read`). In BigQuery "If an operand is NULL, the function result is NULL" unless a function says otherwise ([function call rules](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/functions-reference)), and `ARRAY_CONCAT` "returns NULL if any input argument is NULL" ([array functions](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/array_functions)). Measured first through the front: `SELECT ARRAY_TO_STRING(CAST(NULL AS ARRAY<STRING>), ',')` was answered 500 internalError "runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference", which the Go client retried until its deadline (60 s): the engine (goccy/googlesqlite v0.3.1) passes a NULL to a function as a nil value, which these functions called a method on. Fixed in the engine CloudBurrow builds (googlesqlite patch 0011, next row); the front no longer rewrites these calls (it sent each as `IF(arg IS NULL …, NULL, call)` since #1109). Read back through `jobs.query` and a query job: `ARRAY_TO_STRING` of a NULL array, delimiter or `null_text`, with `SAFE.`, nested in `ARRAY_REVERSE` and of a NULL parameter, reads NULL; `ARRAY_REVERSE` and `ARRAY_CONCAT` of a NULL array and `NET.IPV4_TO_INT64`, `NET.IP_TO_STRING`, `NET.REG_DOMAIN` of a NULL are NULL; `ARRAY_TO_STRING(['a', NULL, 'b'], '-')` reads `a-b`, with `'n'` `a-n-b`, of an `ARRAY_AGG` subquery `a+b`. **An emulator 500 to a query**: the emulator answers 500 only for a panic (a query it cannot run is 400, its source), so the front answers a 500 the emulator gave a query (`jobs.query`, or `jobs.insert` of a query job) **400** `invalidQuery` with the emulator's text, which the client does not retry. A 500 to anything else the front sends first (a `datasets.insert`) is left as it is. Units `TestNoRetry`. |
| `NULL` arguments of the other functions the engine failed on, and `IN` with a NULL | **Verified** for those listed | `TestBigQueryNullArgumentsOfOtherFunctions` (#1121), official Go client, through `jobs.query` and a query job. In BigQuery a NULL operand makes a function's result NULL (function call rules, previous row), `GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY` and `GENERATE_TIMESTAMP_ARRAY` return "a NULL array" if any argument is NULL ([array functions](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/array_functions)), "If json_key is NULL, an error is produced" (`JSON_OBJECT`, [JSON functions](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/json_functions)), and `IN` "Returns FALSE if value_set is empty. Returns TRUE if value_set contains a value equal to search_value. Returns NULL if the equality comparison between search_value and any value in value_set produces NULL. Returns FALSE." ([operators](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/operators)). Found by calling each of the engine's functions with a NULL argument (in its own module, googlesqlite v0.3.1): a panic (the emulator's 500) for the step of `GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY` and `GENERATE_TIMESTAMP_ARRAY`, `MAKE_INTERVAL`, `INTERVAL <NULL> DAY`, `ST_BUFFER`, `ST_BUFFERWITHTOLERANCE`, `ST_INTERSECTSBOX`, `NULLIF(x, NULL)`, `JSON_OBJECT`'s key and `JSON_SET`'s path and value, beside the previous row's; an error for `ST_DISTANCE`, `ST_HAUSDORFFDWITHIN`, `JUSTIFY_DAYS`, `JUSTIFY_HOURS`, `JUSTIFY_INTERVAL` and `JSON_TYPE`; FALSE for `NULL IN UNNEST([1, 2])`, `1 IN UNNEST([2, NULL])` and `1 IN (2, NULL)`. Fixed in the engine (googlesqlite patch 0011: one guard where every scalar function is called returns NULL for a NULL argument of those functions, and returns any function's panic as an error naming it; `JSON_OBJECT`, `JSON_SET`, `NULLIF`, `IN` and `IN UNNEST` fixed where they are). Read back: each of those calls with a NULL reads NULL, promptly; `ARRAY_LENGTH(GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY('2020-01-01', '2020-01-03'))` 3, `MAKE_INTERVAL(hour => 10)` `0-0 0 10:0:0`, `ST_INTERSECTSBOX(p, 0, 0, 10, 10)` true, `NULLIF(1, NULL)` 1, `1 IN UNNEST([NULL, 1])` true, `NULL IN UNNEST([])` false, `JSON_SET(JSON '{"a":1}', '$.a', NULL)` `{"a":null}`; `JSON_OBJECT(CAST(NULL AS STRING), 1)` fails 400 "JSON_OBJECT: a key is NULL". |
| `=`, `<` and the other comparisons of `INTERVAL`s; a negative `INTERVAL` of less than an hour; `INTERVAL n MILLISECOND` and `MICROSECOND` | **Verified** | `TestBigQueryIntervalComparison` (#1120, #1126), official Go client (`Query.Parameters` with a `*bigquery.IntervalValue`). In BigQuery "Values of the same comparable data type can be compared to each other. All data types are supported except for: GEOGRAPHY JSON ARRAY" ([comparable data types](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types#comparable_data_types)); the page does not say how two intervals compare, and GoogleSQL's own implementation compares their length, a month counting 30 days and a day 24 hours ([interval_value.h](https://github.com/google/googlesql/blob/master/googlesql/public/interval_value.h), `GetAsMicros` and the comparison operators). The canonical format is `[sign]Y-M [sign]D [sign]H:M:S[.F]`, and `INTERVAL` takes `MILLISECOND` and `MICROSECOND` ([interval type](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types#interval_type)). Measured first through the front: `SELECT INTERVAL 1 DAY = INTERVAL 1 DAY` failed 400 "unsupported eq operator for interval value", and so did `WHERE v = @p`; read in the engine: `INTERVAL -1 SECOND` was written `0-0 0 0:0:1` (and stored so, positive), and `INTERVAL 1500 MILLISECOND` failed "unexpected interval part". Fixed in the engine (googlesqlite patches 0009 and 0010). Read back: `INTERVAL 1 DAY = INTERVAL 1 DAY`, `INTERVAL 1 MONTH = INTERVAL 30 DAY`, `INTERVAL 1 DAY = INTERVAL 24 HOUR`, `INTERVAL 1 DAY < INTERVAL 25 HOUR`, `INTERVAL -1 SECOND < INTERVAL 0 SECOND` true; `CAST(INTERVAL -1 SECOND AS STRING)` `0-0 0 -0:0:1`, `INTERVAL -1 MONTH` `-0-1 0 0:0:0`, `INTERVAL 1500 MILLISECOND` `0-0 0 0:0:1.5`; a table's `WHERE v = @p` of `@p` 1 day finds `INTERVAL 1 DAY` and `INTERVAL 24 HOUR`, `v > @p` `INTERVAL 2 DAY`, `v < INTERVAL 0 SECOND` the stored `INTERVAL -1 SECOND`. **Not supported**: `ORDER BY`, `MIN` and `MAX` of an `INTERVAL` order its text (#1138). |
| A `REPEATED` column a streamed row or a load's record leaves out | **Verified** for `tabledata.insertAll` and a JSON load | `TestBigQueryRepeatedFieldLeftOutIsAnEmptyArray` (#1124), official Go client (`Inserter.Put` of a `ValuesSaver` without the field, `ReaderSource`, `Table.Read`). In BigQuery a stored array is never NULL: "each array is written as an empty array" ([array type](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types#array_type)). Measured first through the front: a row streamed without `tags` read `tags IS NULL` true, `ARRAY_LENGTH(tags)` NULL and `ARRAY_TO_STRING(tags, ',')` NULL. | `TO_JSON_STRING`, `TO_JSON` and `SAFE_TO_JSON` | **Verified** for every type of GoogleSQL's [JSON encodings](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/json_functions#json_encodings) table but `GEOGRAPHY` and the graph types, of a value read from a table (written by DML, `tabledata.insertAll` or a load) and of a literal; and since #1127 of a value `JSON_OBJECT`, `JSON_ARRAY`, `JSON_SET`, `JSON_ARRAY_APPEND` and `JSON_ARRAY_INSERT` take from a table or a literal; **Not verified** for `GEOGRAPHY`, which the table does not list (written as its WKT text, as before), and for the number of sub-second digits of a `TIME`, `DATETIME` or `TIMESTAMP` beyond the table's six-digit examples | `TestBigQueryToJSONStringOfStoredRows` (#1116), official Go client: rows of `INT64` (one past 2^53), `FLOAT64`, `NUMERIC` (123.56), `BIGNUMERIC`, `STRING`, `BYTES`, `BOOL`, `DATE`, `DATETIME`, `TIME`, `TIMESTAMP`, a `STRUCT` and an `ARRAY<BOOL>`, each written by DML, the `Inserter` and an NDJSON load, give the table's encodings (`true`, a quoted ISO 8601 date and time, a wide `INT64` and a fractional `NUMERIC` as strings), and `TO_JSON` of the row the same with the wide numbers as numbers; an `INTERVAL` is an ISO 8601 duration (`"PT10H20M30.52S"`), +inf `"Infinity"`, a `RANGE` `{"start":…,"end":…}`, `stringify_wide_numbers => TRUE` a string. **Measured first**: a `BOOL` read from a table was `1` and a `DATE`, `DATETIME`, `TIME` or `TIMESTAMP` was written without quotes, not JSON.
