## Vertex AI custom prediction

Google's **serving contract**, on CloudBurrow's **own runtime**. See
[prediction.md](prediction.md) for the decision and its reasoning.

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AIP_HTTP_PORT` / `AIP_HEALTH_ROUTE` / `AIP_PREDICT_ROUTE` honoured | **Verified** | `TestPredictionEndpointServesTheVertexContract` deploys with **non-default** routes and asserts the defaults return 404, so the environment is proven plumbed through rather than coincidentally matching. Names checked against `google.cloud.aiplatform.constants.prediction` 2.1.3. |
| Health route reports readiness | **Verified** | Same test. Any 2xx is healthy, as Vertex defines it; a redirect is not. |
| `{"instances":[...]}` → `{"predictions":[...]}` | **Verified** | Same test, decoded through `internal/prediction` types rather than string matching. |
| One prediction per instance enforced | **Verified** | `prediction.ValidateResponse`; a mismatched count is a 500, not a mis-attributed result. |
| `parameters` passed to the container | **Verified** | `TestPredictionDeadlineBoundsASlowPrediction` drives the fixture's delay through it. |
| Malformed input refused | **Verified** | Empty instances, wrong instance type, unknown field and invalid JSON all return 400. |
| Caller deadline bounds a slow prediction | **Verified** | A 10s prediction fails a 2s caller, and the endpoint remains usable afterwards. |
| Endpoint deletion is complete | **Verified** | `TestPredictionEndpointDeletionIsComplete`; `GetService` then returns `NotFound`. |
| Startup failure reported with the container's output | **Verified** | `TestPredictionStartupFailureIsReported`. The adapter prefers Knative's `ConfigurationsReady` message over the top-level `does not have any ready Revision`. |
| **Startup-failure latency** | **Verified** | Knative declares a revision failed only after its `progress-deadline`, and Cloud Run v2 exposes no field that shortens it; with Knative's default `600s` the failure was reported after **602s, measured** (#568). `up` sets the deadline to `240s`, Cloud Run's default startup-probe budget, on install and on an already-installed cluster (`TestKnativeInstallSetsTheRevisionProgressDeadline`, `TestAnAlreadyInstalledKnativeGetsTheProgressDeadline`). Until then the endpoint reports `PENDING`. |
| `AIP_STORAGE_URI` artifact download | **Not supported** | Recognised as a contract variable; nothing fetches from GCS. The offline path downloads no artifacts and loads no credentials. |
| `LocalModel.deploy_to_local_endpoint` | **Declined by design** | It runs `containers.run(detach=True)` outside the cluster — unowned by readiness, reset or delete. Execution goes through the owned runtime instead. |
| `LocalModel.build_cpr_model` | Available, not invoked | CloudBurrow accepts any image honouring the contract; it does not build one for you. |
| Vertex model registry, `Endpoint` and `DeployedModel` resources | **Not supported** | No Vertex management surface is served, so a client fails to connect rather than receiving a stub. |
| Prediction through `PredictionService` | See [below](#vertex-ai-predictionservice--googlecloudaiplatformv1) | The official `aiplatform` PredictionClient reaches a deployed container as `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/endpoints/{service}` (#1193). |
| Model Garden, tuning, batch prediction | **Not supported** | Out of scope. |
| Console: Online prediction | **Verified** | Vertex AI → Online prediction lists the Cloud Run services that set an `AIP_*` variable, read through `ListServices`, and sends `{"instances","parameters"}` to one's predict route through the cluster ingress; the container's status and body are shown verbatim, its own 400s included, and the console's refusals (not a JSON array, not deployed) are kept apart from them (`TestConsoleOnlinePredictionThroughTheConsoleAPI`, `TestCloudRunPredictorAnswersOnlinePredictionInTheBrowser`). Needs the ingress published on a host port; see [playground.md](playground.md) §8. |
| **GPU / accelerators** | **Not supported** | CPU only, on every platform. NVIDIA is untested and nothing configures it. On Apple Silicon a Linux container has no Metal device, so no configuration achieves it — **NVIDIA container flags do not establish Metal acceleration**. |

The host-advertised URI is the cluster ingress address and the Knative gateway is not
published on a host port, so a host-side caller reaches an endpoint through a port-forward
with the service in the `Host` header. In-cluster callers use the cluster-local name
directly. Both are documented in [prediction.md](prediction.md#reaching-the-endpoint).

## Vertex AI PredictionService — `google.cloud.aiplatform.v1`

The local AI endpoint serves `google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.PredictionService` over **gRPC** on the
same port as its JSON routes, so `cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform`'s `PredictionClient`, which has
no REST transport, reaches it (#1193). Each method converts its request to the JSON its route
reads and calls the same function, so both protocols refuse and answer a request identically.
The endpoint starts whenever Cloud Run is enabled, with or without a local model; its address is
the `local AI:` line `up` prints. Two resource name shapes are served:
`projects/{p}/locations/{l}/endpoints/{service}`, where `{service}` is the Cloud Run service ID of
a deployed [custom prediction container](prediction.md), relayed to its `AIP_PREDICT_ROUTE`
through the cluster ingress; and `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/publishers/google/models/{model}`,
for the [embeddings](embeddings.md) and [generation](generation.md) subsets. The same endpoint
names are served as JSON at `POST /v1/{endpoint}:predict` and `:rawPredict`.

| Method | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Predict` | **Verified** | `TestPredictionClientReachesACustomEndpoint`: the official `aiplatform` v1.127.0 PredictionClient against a deployed container on non-default `AIP_*` routes; one prediction per instance (a different count is `INTERNAL`, never a mis-attributed result), `deployedModelId`, `parameters` passed through, the container's own 400 as `INVALID_ARGUMENT` in its words, an endpoint not deployed `NOT_FOUND`. On a publisher model it is the text-embedding `:predict` subset, with provenance in `modelDisplayName` and the `x-cloudburrow-model-provenance` header: `TestEmbeddingGemmaThroughThePredictionClient` (needs the model, `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_EMBEDDINGS`; not run in CI; passed 2026-10-15 on darwin/arm64 with ONNX Runtime 1.29.0, on the same instance and run as `TestEmbeddingGemmaThroughTheOfficialSDK` and the custom-endpoint test) and unit tests comparing it to the JSON route. |
| `RawPredict` | **Verified** (publisher models measured 2026-10-15) | Custom endpoints: same test; the body is relayed to the container's predict route and its answer returned as `HttpBody`. Publisher models (#1284): the model's native body, answered by the same code as its typed method, so the same subset and refusals: on `embeddinggemma-300m-onnx-community` the text-embedding `:predict` body, answered as `:predict` answers it (provenance in `x-cloudburrow-model-provenance`); on the generation model the `generateContent` body, answered with a `GenerateContentResponse`. A `http_body.content_type` other than `application/json` is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming it; another model is `NOT_FOUND`, never substituted; no embedding runtime is the same 501 as `:predict`, no generation runtime the same `FAILED_PRECONDITION` as `generateContent`. Also served as JSON at `POST /v1` (and `/v1beta1`) `/{model}:rawPredict`. `TestRawPredictOnTheEmbeddingModel` and `TestRawPredictOnTheGenerationModel` (official `aiplatform` PredictionClient, gRPC; need the models, `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_EMBEDDINGS` and `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_LOCALAI`; not run in CI) passed 2026-10-15 on darwin/arm64 against `embeddinggemma-300m-onnx-community` (ONNX Runtime 1.29.0) and `gemma-4-e2b-it-community` in a `make litert-lm` runtime; the REST route is unit-tested (`TestRawPredictREST`). Console: Vertex AI → Embeddings, Method RawPredict. |
| `GenerateContent` | **Verified** | The `generateContent` subset of [generation.md](generation.md), unary, from the same code as the JSON route: the same refusals (every generation option, tools, multi-turn) and no substitution. `TestStreamGenerateContentThroughThePredictionClient` (official `aiplatform` v1.127.0 PredictionClient, gRPC; needs the model, `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_LOCALAI`; not run in CI) passed 2026-10-15 on darwin/arm64 against `gemma-4-e2b-it-community` in a `make litert-lm` runtime: one candidate, `STOP`, `modelVersion` the model that ran; `temperature` `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming it; `gemini-2.0-flash` `NOT_FOUND`. Console: Vertex AI Studio (`/ai/playground`) with **Stream** off (#1257). |
| `StreamGenerateContent` | **Verified** | The same subset, streamed (#1257) from the same code as the JSON `:streamGenerateContent` route: one `GenerateContentResponse` per chunk as the runtime decodes it, each naming the model, `STOP` on a final message of its own and on no other; a refusal before the first chunk is the unary call's status, word for word; a failure after one ends the stream `INTERNAL` naming it. Same test and run: 7 messages over 1.83 s, the first after 1.36 s; the same refusals as `GenerateContent`. Unit tests assert the first message arrives while generation is still running. Console: Vertex AI Studio with **Stream** on, the default. |
| `EmbedContent` | **Verified** (measured 2026-10-15) | On `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/publishers/google/models/embeddinggemma-300m-onnx-community` only, from the same local model as text-embedding `:predict` (#1244); also served as JSON at `POST /v1` (and `/v1beta1`) `/{model}:embedContent`. Honoured: `content` (text parts, joined with newlines), `title`, `task_type` (EmbeddingGemma's prompt prefixes; `UNSPECIFIED` is the model's default), `output_dimensionality` (768/512/256/128, truncated and renormalised) and `auto_truncate`, each at the top level or in `embed_content_config` (both set to different values is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`). Refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the field: another size, an unknown task type, a non-text part (`content.parts[i]`), `document_ocr`, `audio_track_extraction`. Another model is `NOT_FOUND`, never substituted; a build without embeddings answers the same 501 (`UNIMPLEMENTED`) as `:predict`. Response `embedding.values`, `usage_metadata.prompt_token_count`, `truncated`; provenance in the `x-cloudburrow-model-provenance` header. `TestEmbedContentThroughThePredictionClient` (official `aiplatform` v1.127.0 PredictionClient, gRPC; needs the model, `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_EMBEDDINGS`; not run in CI) passed 2026-10-15 on darwin/arm64 with ONNX Runtime 1.29.0, its vector equal to `Predict`'s for the same input (cosine ≥ 0.9999); the REST route is unit-tested (`TestEmbedContentREST`). **Not reachable from `google.golang.org/genai`:** on its Vertex backend, `Models.EmbedContent` sends `:embedContent` only for a model whose name contains `gemini` or `maas`, and `:predict` otherwise. Console: Vertex AI → Embeddings, Method EmbedContent. |
| `StreamRawPredict` | **Verified** (measured 2026-10-15) | RawPredict's native body, streamed (#1285), from the same code: on the generation model one `GenerateContentResponse` per `HttpBody` chunk as the runtime decodes it, `STOP` on a final chunk and no other, as `StreamGenerateContent` frames it; on the embedding model and a custom endpoint (whose contract has no streaming route) one chunk, the whole answer. The same refusals as `RawPredict`, before the first chunk. Also served as JSON at `POST /v1/{model or endpoint}:streamRawPredict`, as server-sent events for a publisher model. Console: Vertex AI Studio, Raw with Stream on. |
| `DirectPredict`, `ServerStreamingPredict`, `StreamingPredict`, `StreamDirectPredict` | **Verified** (measured 2026-10-15) | The tensor methods (#1285). Each input `Tensor` becomes the JSON instance it carries (`struct_val` an object, `list_val` a list, a typed value array a scalar when it has one element and no `shape`, else a list) and each prediction an output (a number list as a `DOUBLE` vector), with `Predict`'s code behind it. Embedding model: the text-embedding instance and parameters, one message per request with the 768-value (or smaller) vector. Generation model: exactly one input, the Model Garden text instance `{"prompt": string_val}`, answered `{"content": string_val}`: one message per decoded chunk on `ServerStreamingPredict` and `StreamingPredict`, the whole text on `DirectPredict` and `StreamDirectPredict`. Custom endpoints: relayed as `Predict`, one message. Bidirectional streams need `endpoint` on the first request; a later one may omit or repeat it, not change it. Refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the field: any other prompt-instance field (`inputs[0].struct_val.max_tokens`, …), any `parameters` on the generation model (the runtime applies no option), `tensor_val`, `bytes_val`, a tensor mixing value types. Another model is `NOT_FOUND`; no runtime is the same 501 or `FAILED_PRECONDITION` as `Predict` and `generateContent`. `TestStreamingPredictOnTheGenerationModel` and `TestStreamingPredictOnTheEmbeddingModel` (official `aiplatform` PredictionClient, gRPC; need the models; not run in CI) passed 2026-10-15 on darwin/arm64 against `gemma-4-e2b-it-community` (`make litert-lm`) and `embeddinggemma-300m-onnx-community` (ONNX Runtime 1.29.0). Console: the Playground and Embeddings screens send the same requests in JSON form. |
| `DirectRawPredict`, `StreamDirectRawPredict`, `StreamingRawPredict` | **Unimplemented** | `UNIMPLEMENTED` naming `method_name`: these call a method on a gRPC model server, and none is served — the local models run in-process and custom containers speak HTTP. |
| `Explain` | **Unimplemented** | `UNIMPLEMENTED`. |

## Credentials, metadata and external tooling

**CloudBurrow authenticates nothing.** These exist so that tools which insist on credentials
can run offline. See [credentials.md](credentials.md).

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| IAM Credentials `generateAccessToken` for impersonation | **Verified** | `TestImpersonatedTokenUsedWithACloudBurrowClient` (#303): a `google.golang.org/api/impersonate` token source, served by the metadata server, drives an official Storage client against CloudBurrow. A transport guard fails any request not bound for loopback. **The token is local and not validated; no permission is checked.** Go's impersonate package takes no endpoint override, so its client needs a transport that routes `iamcredentials.googleapis.com` locally ([credentials.md](credentials.md#service-account-impersonation-iam-credentials)). |
| IAM Credentials `generateIdToken` | **Verified** | Unit-tested through the official `impersonate.IDTokenSource`: a JWT with the requested audience and the impersonated account's email, verified against the local `/certs`. It will **not** verify against Google's certificates. |
| IAM Credentials `signJwt` | **Implemented** | Signs the payload's claims with the instance key. Unit-tested over REST. |
| IAM Credentials `signBlob` | **Unimplemented** | UNIMPLEMENTED, tested: a local signature would make signed URLs that no Google service accepts. |
| `cloudburrow env` shell/JSON/plain export | **Verified** | `TestEnvExportsEveryClientVariable`, `TestEnvPrintsARunningInstancesLivePorts`; an instance that is not running is refused with nothing on stdout, `TestEnvRefusesAnInstanceThatIsNotRunning` (#630). Only the running instance's services are exported, `TestEnvExportsOnlyTheServicesARunningInstanceServes` (#652). Exports the client-library variables *and* the `gcloud` endpoint overrides, because `gcloud` ignores the former. |
| ADC fixture usable by Google's auth library | **Verified** | `TestOfficialAuthLibraryUsesTheLocalFixture`: `google.FindDefaultCredentials` mints a token through the fixture. The test fails if a `ya29.` token appears, which would mean it reached Google with the developer's real credentials. |
| Token exchange stays local | **Verified** | Same test. The fixture's `token_uri`, `auth_uri` and cert URLs all point at the instance. |
| Metadata server contract (`/`, project, zone, email, token, identity, scopes, aliases) | **Verified** | `TestMetadataServerAnswersTheContract` and `internal/metadata`. |
| `Metadata-Flavor: Google` required and echoed | **Verified** | Enforced even though the tokens grant nothing: a local server accepting what a real one rejects teaches code to fail in production. |
| ID token is a valid RS256 JWT | **Verified** | Signed with the instance key and verifiable against `/certs`. |
| **ID token verifies against Google's certificates** | **Not supported** | Google did not issue it. Tokens are structurally valid and self-consistent; signature verification against Google's public certs is **not** claimed. |
| **Token validation of any kind** | **Not supported** | No signature, expiry, audience, scope or assertion is ever checked. The token endpoint checks only that an assertion was *sent*, so a client silently sending none finds out. |
| **IAM, scopes, per-resource permissions** | **Not supported** | Every caller can do everything. |
| `cloudburrow gcloud-setup` / `gcloud-teardown` | **Verified where gcloud is installed** | `TestGcloudSetupConfiguration` (#305): through the configuration alone, `gcloud storage ls` and `gcloud pubsub topics list` reach CloudBurrow. The default configuration is unchanged, and teardown removes the configuration and is safe to repeat. Overrides written: `storage`, `pubsub`, `cloudkms`, `secretmanager`, `cloudtasks`, `cloudscheduler`, `logging`, `cloudresourcemanager`, `run`, `artifactregistry`, `cloudbuild`, `cloudfunctions`, `sql`, `serviceusage` and `redis` (`cloudfunctions` since #1377, at the Run port, for `gcloud functions`; `artifactregistry` and `cloudbuild` since #1347, at the Run port, for `gcloud run deploy --source` and `gcloud builds submit`, driven by `TestGcloudRunDeploySource` and `TestGcloudBuildsSubmit`; `redis`, the Memorystore admin API, since #1302, with `memorystore`; `serviceusage` since #1352, written whatever `--services` selects, driven by `TestGcloudServices`; `cloudscheduler` and `logging` since #591; `cloudresourcemanager` since #682, written whatever `--services` selects, and at `cloudresourcemanager.localhost` on a loopback bind since #1350, so the `{location}-` host of `gcloud resource-manager tags bindings --location` resolves; `run` since #1293, at `run.localhost` on a loopback bind so gcloud's `{region}-` host resolves; `sql` since #1301, with either Cloud SQL service, driven by `TestGcloudSQL`); `gcloud secrets`, `gcloud tasks` (queues and tasks), `gcloud scheduler` and `gcloud logging` are driven by `TestGcloudSecrets`, `TestGcloudTasks`, `TestGcloudScheduler` and `TestGcloudLogging`; `gcloud projects` by `TestGcloudProjectsThroughGcloudSetup`; `gcloud run` by `TestGcloudRunServicesList`. |
| `gcloud storage ls` | **Verified** | With `CLOUDSDK_API_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDES_STORAGE` and a local token. |
| `gcloud pubsub topics create` / `list` | **Verified** | With `CLOUDSDK_API_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDES_PUBSUB`. |
| **`gcloud` honouring `*_EMULATOR_HOST`** | **Not supported (upstream)** | `gcloud` ignores them and goes to the real service, which **leaves the machine**. Inherited limitation, recorded rather than worked around; `cloudburrow env` exports the overrides too. |
| `WorkerPool.scaling.scalingMode` (Terraform's `scaling_mode`, and its `min_instance_count`, `max_instance_count`, `max_surge`, `max_unavailable`) | **Refused**, *as published* | #1354: `WorkerPoolScaling` has only `manual_instance_count` (field 6) in `cloud.google.com/go/run` v1.23.0, in googleapis master's `google/cloud/run/v2/vendor_settings.proto` (checked 2026-10-15) and in the run v2 discovery documents of revisions 20260904 and 20260917. A body carrying the field is INVALID_ARGUMENT ("the request body is not a valid WorkerPool"), measured with hashicorp/google 8.4.0. Whether Google accepts it unpublished is UNVERIFIED; accepting it here would invent its meaning. |
| Terraform `google` provider create / read / destroy | **Verified** | `TestTerraformAppliesAndDestroysThroughTheWrapper`: `google_storage_bucket`, `google_pubsub_topic`, `google_secret_manager_secret`, `google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member` (#365), `google_cloud_tasks_queue` and `google_cloud_tasks_queue_iam_member` (#366; IAM stored, not enforced) applied through `cloudburrow terraform` with `hashicorp/google` 8.4.0 on Terraform 1.16.4 (the exact version the modules require, installed only if it matches the hashes in the committed `test/compat/testdata/terraform/.terraform.lock.hcl`, #694), read back through the official SDKs, destroyed, and confirmed gone. Since #928 the front reads the provider's URL mask (`updateMask=ackDeadlineSeconds,labels,bigqueryConfig`, camelCase), keeps the labels, and sends the emulator the other paths in the body, snake_case, so every other change applies too: `TestTerraformPubSubPushAndExpiration` applies a subscription with `push_config` and `expiration_policy`, plans clean, and changes the ttl and the push endpoint in place (see Pub/Sub, CloudBurrow's front). **OpenTofu 1.12.6 too**, through `cloudburrow terraform --binary tofu` (#719): `TestTofuAppliesAndDestroysThroughTheWrapper` applies the first test's module, reads it back, plans clean and destroys it, and `TestTofuSchedulerAndSubscription` runs the scheduler module, both in CI's storage shard, which installs the release checked against its pinned SHA-256. every `dataset_access` argument replaces it, by the provider's design). `TestTerraformTasksQueueHTTPTarget` applies a `google_cloud_tasks_queue` with an `http_target` (#1282: method, a `uri_override` with scheme, host, port, path, query and `ALWAYS` enforcement, a header override and an `oidc_token`), read back by the official Cloud Tasks client, and changes the method, host, header and audience in place. `TestTerraformSecretRotationAndTopics` applies a `google_secret_manager_secret` with two `google_pubsub_topic`s as event `topics` (#1259), a `rotation` schedule and `version_destroy_ttl` (#1278), read back by the official client, and adds a topic and changes the rotation period in place. `TestTerraformKMSPurposesAndImportJob`, in the served shard, applies `google_kms_crypto_key`s of purpose `ASYMMETRIC_SIGN` (`EC_SIGN_P256_SHA256`), `ASYMMETRIC_DECRYPT` (`RSA_DECRYPT_OAEP_2048_SHA256`) and `MAC` (`HMAC_SHA256`) through `version_template` (#1212), and a `google_kms_key_ring_import_job` (`RSA_OAEP_3072_SHA1_AES_256`, `SOFTWARE`); the official client reads each key's purpose and algorithm, its version 1 ENABLED and no primary, and the job ACTIVE with its public key; labels change in place; destroy leaves the keys, with every version DESTROY_SCHEDULED, and the job, which the provider only drops from state, as on Google. `TestTerraformBigQueryPartitionedTableAndJob`, in the emulators shard, applies a `google_bigquery_table` partitioned by `DAY` on a TIMESTAMP column with `expiration_ms`, clustered, with a column's `defaultValueExpression` in its schema (#1272, #1340), and a `google_bigquery_job` running a query into a destination table; the official client reads back the partitioning, clustering, schema and default, the job DONE and the destination's row; the description, labels and clustering change in one in-place update; the job is only dropped from state on destroy, as on Google. `TestTerraformRunVolumesAndServiceAccount`, in the run shard, applies a `google_cloud_run_v2_service` and a `google_cloud_run_v2_job`, each with a `service_account`, a Secret Manager `secret` volume (from a `google_secret_manager_secret` and version) and an in-memory `empty_dir` volume mounted through `volume_mounts` (#1297); stored, not enforced): `TestTerraformStoredIAM` applies a `google_storage_bucket`, a `google_secret_manager_secret` and a `google_cloud_tasks_queue`, and `TestTerraformKMSStoredIAM` a `google_kms_key_ring` and `google_kms_crypto_key` (in the shard KMS is served in), and on each `*_iam_member` and `*_iam_binding`, then `*_iam_policy`, in `TestTerraformBigQueryIAM`'s phases, each read back through the official Go client (`Bucket.IAM`, and `GetIamPolicy` of the Secret Manager, KMS and Cloud Tasks clients), planned clean and removed with every binding gone and the resource kept. `TestTerraformBigQueryDatasetIAM` does the same with `google_bigquery_dataset_iam_*`, which the provider applies as the dataset's access list: it read a dataset made without one as a nil policy and crashed, because the emulator kept no access list; CloudBurrow's front now gives such a dataset BigQuery's default one (`projectWriters` WRITER, `projectOwners` OWNER, `projectReaders` READER; the creator's OWNER entry is left out, as a local caller has no identity). `TestTerraformStorageACLLists` applies the list-valued `google_storage_bucket_acl`, `google_storage_default_object_acl` and `google_storage_object_acl` on a fine-grained bucket, read back with the generated JSON API client's `list` calls, plans clean, and changes a role and removes an entity in place. `TestTerraformRunWorkerPool` applies a `google_cloud_run_v2_worker_pool` (#1300) with `manual_instance_count`, read back by the official `WorkerPoolsClient`, and changes a label, an environment variable and the instance count (1 to 2) in place. **`scaling_mode` is not verified** (#1354): the provider sends it as `scaling.scalingMode`, which neither `google.cloud.run.v2`'s `WorkerPoolScaling` nor Google's published discovery document has, and the transcoder refuses the body as INVALID_ARGUMENT. The wrapper takes a running instance's services, as `env` does, so `--name x` alone sets the endpoint of an opt-in service it serves. ## Memorystore for Redis — `google.cloud.redis.v1`

**Built, over real servers** (#1302). `--services memorystore` serves the admin API in the CLI
process, on `--port-memorystore-admin` (default `9021`), gRPC and JSON on one port as
`redis.googleapis.com` does, with `google.longrunning.Operations` for its operations. `env`
exports `CLOUDBURROW_MEMORYSTORE_ENDPOINT`; no client library reads it, so pass it to
`option.WithEndpoint`. `gcloud-setup` writes `api_endpoint_overrides/redis` and `cloudburrow
terraform` sets `redis_custom_endpoint`. Per-method status is generated in
[coverage/memorystore.md](coverage/memorystore.md).

Two kinds of instance. The instance `up` runs is
`projects/<default project>/locations/us-central1/instances/memorystore`, described from the
server itself, never invented; it cannot be updated or deleted. Every other instance is one
`CreateInstance` made: a Valkey server of its own, a Deployment and a Service per instance of the
same image and settings (`components.MemorystoreServer`), reached from the host through its own
tunnel on an OS-assigned port, which the instance's `host` and `port` report.

| Claim | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ListInstances`, `GetInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreAdminDescribesTheServer`, with `cloud.google.com/go/redis/apiv1` against an instance started with `--services memorystore,storage`: the instance `up` runs is listed under `locations/-` and its region, and nowhere in another project; `host:port` is the RESP endpoint (`REDIS_HOST:REDIS_PORT`), which a Redis client then reaches; `state` is READY; `redis_version` is `REDIS_7_2`, from the server's `INFO server` (Valkey 8.1 reports Redis 7.2.4); `memory_size_gb` is 1, from `CONFIG GET maxmemory` (`--maxmemory 1gb`, `--maxmemory-policy volatile-lru`, Memorystore's default policy); tier BASIC, DIRECT_PEERING, transit encryption DISABLED, `auth_enabled` false. A server that does not answer is UNAVAILABLE, not a stale READY. An unknown instance is NOT_FOUND. Created instances are listed beside it, in name order and paged. |
| `CreateInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreCreateConnectUpdateDelete`: the operation completes (`op.Wait`) with a READY instance, `OperationMetadata` verb `create` and its target; go-redis at the reported host and port is refused NOAUTH without the AUTH string and works with it; `CONFIG GET` shows `memory_size_gb` as `maxmemory` and `redis_configs` as the server's config; the server `up` runs does not have its keys. `TestGcloudRedis` (gcloud 587.0.0, `redis instances create --tier=basic --size=1 --enable-auth --redis-config --labels`) and `TestTerraformRedisInstance` (hashicorp/google 8.4.0) create one too. A create that fails leaves no instance. **What is accepted:** tier BASIC, or STANDARD_HA (#1385, below), `memory_size_gb` 1 to 300, `redis_version` empty or `REDIS_7_2` (Valkey 8.1, which reports Redis 7.2.4), `REDIS_7_0` (Redis 7.0.15) or `REDIS_6_X` (Redis 6.2.24), each a digest-pinned BSD-3-Clause image (#1386, `TestMemorystoreVersionsAndUpgrade`: INFO reports each); `REDIS_3_2`, `REDIS_4_0` and `REDIS_5_0` are 501 with the reason (#1413): they are end of life and have no maintained image, the Docker official `redis` image having last built 3.2 in October 2018, 4.0 in April 2020 and 5.0 in November 2022, and building only 6.2 and later; `auth_enabled`, `display_name`, `labels`, `location_id` (default `<region>-a`) and `redis_configs` of `maxmemory-policy`, `notify-keyspace-events`, `activedefrag`, `lfu-decay-time`, `lfu-log-factor`, `stream-node-max-bytes`, `stream-node-max-entries` and `maxmemory-gb` (another is INVALID_ARGUMENT). `persistence_config` (#1384) is accepted: see RDB persistence below. **In-transit encryption** (#1413, `TestMemorystoreInTransitEncryption`, official `cloud.google.com/go/redis/apiv1` and go-redis): `transit_encryption_mode: SERVER_AUTHENTICATION` runs the server TLS-only (`--port 0 --tls-port 6378`, as Memorystore's port 6378 in the cluster; `host:port` on the host is its tunnel, as for any created instance), with a server certificate (180 days, issued again at each start) of a CA of the instance's own (ECDSA P-256, ten years, as Memorystore's), which `server_ca_certs` lists (PEM, serial, SHA-1 fingerprint, create and expire times) in `GetInstance`, `ListInstances` and the create operation's response. go-redis over TLS 1.2+ trusting that CA reaches a BASIC and a STANDARD_HA instance with the AUTH string; a plain TCP client is refused and a TLS client without the CA fails verification; a Standard tier instance's nodes replicate over TLS (`WAIT 1`). `TestGcloudRedisInTransitEncryption` (gcloud 587.0.0, `--transit-encryption-mode=server-authentication`; `describe` shows the mode and `serverCaCerts[0].cert`, which a TLS client then trusts) and `TestTerraformRedisInTransitEncryption` (hashicorp/google, `transit_encryption_mode`, the `server_ca_certs` attribute, a clean second plan) create one too. Client certificates are not asked for, as SERVER_AUTHENTICATION has none; the mode cannot be changed after create, and no CA rotation is served. Customer-managed keys are 501. The instance ID is checked with Google's rule (1 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter). Placement is not real: any region is accepted. |
| `UpdateInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreCreateConnectUpdateDelete`: `memory_size_gb`, `display_name`, `labels` and `redis_configs` change; the size and configs are set on the running server with `CONFIG SET`, which keeps its keys, and a config removed from `redis_configs` goes back to its default; `TestGcloudRedis` (`--size --update-labels`, an `updateMask` of snake_case paths, which the JSON API accepts as Google does) and `TestTerraformRedisInstance` (in place) update one too. `persistence_config` changes the server's persistence (#1384, below). A value the server refuses is INVALID_ARGUMENT and changes nothing. `maintenance_policy` is stored and `auth_enabled` turns AUTH off, or on with a fresh AUTH string, on the running server's `requirepass` (#1386, `TestMemorystoreLocationsOperationsMaintenance`; a connection made before keeps its access). `replica_count` and `read_replicas_mode` scale a STANDARD_HA instance (#1385, below); `secondary_ip_range` is accepted and not kept. Another mask path is INVALID_ARGUMENT (not an updatable field). The instance `up` runs is FAILED_PRECONDITION (CloudBurrow's own). Memorystore may flush a BASIC instance it scales; this does not. |
| `DeleteInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreCreateConnectUpdateDelete`, `TestGcloudRedis`, `TestTerraformRedisInstance`: the operation completes, the instance is NOT_FOUND and its server no longer answers; its Deployment, Service and volume are deleted. The instance `up` runs is FAILED_PRECONDITION (*code UNVERIFIED*, CloudBurrow's own): run `up` without `memorystore` to have none. |
| `GetInstanceAuthString` | **Verified**, *code UNVERIFIED* | A created instance's string is returned (`TestMemorystoreCreateConnectUpdateDelete`, `TestGcloudRedis` `get-auth-string`, Terraform's `auth_string`); an instance without AUTH has an empty one. The instance `up` runs has AUTH off and answers FAILED_PRECONDITION; Google's code for that was not observed. |
| Persistence and reset | **Verified, measured** | A created instance follows the CloudBurrow instance's mode, as the server `up` runs does. **Persistent:** the instance's record is kept in `<state-dir>/<name>/memorystore`, its server writes an append-only file on a volume of its own, and after `stop` and `up` it is READY again (REPAIRING while its server starts), with the same AUTH string and its keys: `TestMemorystoreCreatedAcrossRestart`, which CI's restart probe runs with `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_MEMORYSTORE_EXPECT=present` beside `TestMemorystoreAcrossRestart`, and which was run by hand on one instance through persistent, ephemeral and persistent again (the keys came back after the ephemeral run). **Ephemeral:** records are kept in memory only, and `up` removes the servers a previous run left (their volumes are kept, as the server `up` runs keeps its own); `TestMemorystoreCreatedAcrossRestart` with `absent` after `up --mode ephemeral`. `reset` does not touch Memorystore, created instances included, and `state save` does not capture them. |
| `ExportInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreExportImport` (#1384), with `cloud.google.com/go/redis/apiv1` and `cloud.google.com/go/storage` against an instance started with `--services memorystore,storage`: the operation (verb `export`) completes once the server's `BGSAVE` has finished and its RDB file is written to `output_config.gcs_destination.uri` in this instance's Cloud Storage, an object that starts with the RDB header; `TestGcloudRedisExportImport` (`gcloud redis instances export`). The instance stays READY. A URI that is not `gs://{bucket}/{object}` is INVALID_ARGUMENT; without Cloud Storage on the instance, and on the instance `up` runs, FAILED_PRECONDITION (CloudBurrow's own). |
| `ImportInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreExportImport`: the object is read first (a missing one is NOT_FOUND); the instance is IMPORTING until the operation (verb `import`) completes, and then holds exactly the file's keys, as Memorystore documents an import overwrites: a key set since is gone, a changed one is back, and a second instance gets the first's data. The file is copied into the server's container, checked with the server's own `valkey-check-rdb`, and loaded by the server itself: a second server process of the same image serves it on a loopback port and the instance's server replicates it once, which empties its data and loads the RDB (an AOF, when it keeps one, is written again from it), then stops replicating. A file that is not an RDB the server reads, a newer RDB version among them, fails the operation INVALID_ARGUMENT and changes nothing. `TestGcloudRedisExportImport` (`gcloud redis instances import`) imports over later changes. Memorystore restarts the instance to import; this does not, and clients stay connected. |
| RDB persistence (`persistence_config`) | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreRDBPersistence` (#1384): RDB with `rdb_snapshot_period` on create and through `UpdateInstance`'s mask reads back with `rdb_snapshot_start_time` (default: now; kept by an update that leaves it out) and `rdb_next_snapshot_time` aligned to it, as Memorystore documents; the server's `CONFIG GET save` is the period with one change (`21600 1`, `3600 1`) and `appendonly` is `no`, and a snapshot is taken at once (`LASTSAVE`); DISABLED removes the save point (and, in persistent mode, turns the append-only file back on). `TestTerraformRedisInstance` applies `persistence_config` and changes its period in place. The server is started with the same save point (`components.MemorystoreServerOf`), which Valkey also honours when it stops, so in persistent mode the snapshot on the server's volume brings its data back. Valkey counts the period from its last snapshot rather than aligning it to the start time. An unknown period or mode is INVALID_ARGUMENT. |
| Maintenance policy, `RescheduleMaintenance` | **Verified**, *code UNVERIFIED* | `TestMemorystoreLocationsOperationsMaintenance` (#1386): `maintenance_policy` on create and through `UpdateInstance`'s mask is stored and read back as Memorystore documents it, at most one weekly window (a day and a UTC start time) of one hour, with its `create_time` and `update_time`; a second window, no day or a start hour outside 0 to 23 is INVALID_ARGUMENT. CloudBurrow never schedules maintenance, so an instance has no `maintenance_schedule` and `RescheduleMaintenance` is FAILED_PRECONDITION: there is nothing to move. |
| `UpgradeInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreVersionsAndUpgrade` (#1386): a REDIS_6_X instance upgraded to REDIS_7_0 and then REDIS_7_2 runs each version's server (INFO `redis_version` 7.0.x, then 7.2.4) and keeps its keys and AUTH: the data is snapshotted with `BGSAVE`, the server started again on the new image, and the snapshot loaded into it as an import is. The instance is UPDATING until the operation (verb `upgrade`) completes. A version not later than the instance's is INVALID_ARGUMENT (Memorystore does not downgrade); the instance `up` runs is FAILED_PRECONDITION. `TestConsoleMemorystoreUpgrade` upgrades from the console. |
| `FailoverInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreStandardTierFailover` (#1385), official `cloud.google.com/go/redis/apiv1`: on a STANDARD_HA instance with read replicas, `LIMITED_DATA_LOSS` promotes a replica (`REPLICAOF NO ONE`, then `REPLICAOF` it on the other nodes and the instance's Service re-pointed); `host` and `port` are unchanged and a client there reaches the new primary (`role:master`) with the key written before, its writes reach the replicas, and `current_location_id` moves to the new primary's zone. `TestGcloudRedisFailover` (gcloud 587.0.0, `gcloud redis instances failover --data-protection-mode=force-data-loss`) and the console's Failover (`TestConsoleMemorystoreStandardTier`) fail one over too. `LIMITED_DATA_LOSS` aborts the operation FAILED_PRECONDITION when the greatest offset delta between the primary and a replica is 30 MB or more, or a replica is not replicating; `FORCE_DATA_LOSS` does not check (unit `TestLimitedDataLossRefusesALaggingReplica`: the 30 MB bound is Google's documented one, not measured). A BASIC instance is FAILED_PRECONDITION. **Automatic failover** (#1412, `TestMemorystoreAutomaticFailover`, official `cloud.google.com/go/redis/apiv1` and go-redis): after the primary node's pod is deleted (`kubectl delete pod`), the instance fails over on its own, as Memorystore documents ("a healthy replica with the least replication lag"): it is REPAIRING, then READY with `current_location_id` the replica's zone, and a client at the same `host:port` reaches the new primary with the key written before; the old primary's node comes back as its replica. The primary is checked every second (INFO replication through its tunnel) and fails over after three checks in a row in which it does not answer as a primary; Google documents no detection window. No data protection mode applies: writes the replicas had not received are lost, as Google says of asynchronous replication. No operation is recorded, as Google records none for an automated repair; `up.log` has a line. |
| Standard tier: `tier: STANDARD_HA`, `replica_count`, `read_replicas_mode`, `read_endpoint`, `read_endpoint_port`, `alternative_location_id`, `current_location_id`, `nodes` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreStandardTierFailover` (#1385): `READ_REPLICAS_ENABLED` with `replica_count` 2 is three Valkey servers, each a Deployment and Service, replicating asynchronously; `nodes` are `node-0` to `node-2` with zones (`node-0` in `location_id`, `node-1` in `alternative_location_id`); a key SET at `host:port` is read from a replica at `read_endpoint:read_endpoint_port`, which refuses writes (READONLY); `UpdateInstance` of `replica_count` to 3 adds a node that has the data. `TestGcloudRedisFailover` creates one with `--tier=standard` (`replica_count` 1, no read endpoint), `TestTerraformRedisStandardTier` (hashicorp/google 8.4.0) applies `tier = "STANDARD_HA"` with `read_replicas_mode` and `replica_count` 2, plans clean, and changes `replica_count` to 3 in place. Memorystore's rules are kept: `replica_count` 1 without read replicas, 1 to 5 (default 2) with them, read replicas on 5 GB or more and never disabled once enabled, none of these on BASIC (INVALID_ARGUMENT). The read endpoint spreads connections over the replicas in turn; the primary endpoint and the read endpoint are host addresses of their own, not VPC IPs. See [memorystore.md](memorystore.md#5-standard-tier-read-replicas-and-failover-1385). |
| Long-running operations | **Implemented** | `google.longrunning.Operations`: `GetOperation` (polled by the SDK's `op.Wait`, gcloud and Terraform in the tests above), `ListOperations` (paged, with a filter of `done`, `metadata.verb` and `metadata.target` with `=` or `!=` joined by AND; another field is INVALID_ARGUMENT), `WaitOperation`, `DeleteOperation` (the operation is forgotten, its work goes on) and `CancelOperation` (#1386: `TestMemorystoreLocationsOperationsMaintenance` filters, deletes and cancels a done operation, which is left as it is; an import or export in progress is stopped and fails CANCELLED, *not driven by a test*; a create, update or delete in progress is FAILED_PRECONDITION). Operations are kept in memory for the life of the process. |
| Locations (`ListLocations`, `GetLocation`) | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreLocationsOperationsMaintenance` (#1386): every project lists the regions Cloud Scheduler's Locations lists, and any region holding one of its instances, each with `google.cloud.redis.v1.LocationMetadata` naming zones `-a`, `-b` and `-c` (*which zones Google lists per region is UNVERIFIED*); GetLocation of another is NOT_FOUND. |
| Flush | **Console only** | `google.cloud.redis.v1` has no flush method. The console's **Flush** runs FLUSHALL on the server `up` runs (`TestConsoleMemorystoreFlush`). |
| JSON API (REST) | **Verified** | The shared `Transcoder` serves Google's `google.api.http` bindings of `google.cloud.redis.v1`, and the Operations bindings `redis_v1.yaml` adds, with the same servers; gcloud and Terraform drive it in `TestGcloudRedis` and `TestTerraformRedisInstance`. The Locations bindings are served (#1386). |
| `gcloud redis`, Terraform `google_redis_instance` | **Verified** | `TestGcloudRedis`: through the configuration `gcloud-setup` writes and nothing else, with egress to Google refused, gcloud creates, describes, lists, reads the AUTH string of, updates and deletes an instance, and `TestGcloudRedisExportImport` exports and imports one (#1384). `TestTerraformRedisInstance`: through `cloudburrow terraform`, a `google_redis_instance` with AUTH applies, go-redis reaches it with the `auth_string` the provider read, the second plan is empty, size, labels and the RDB `persistence_config`'s period update in place, and destroy removes it. |
| Terraform `google_redis_instance` with a `maintenance_policy` | **Verified** | `TestTerraformRedisMaintenancePolicy` (#1304, #1386), in the emulators shard, with `hashicorp/google` 8.4.0 and egress blocked: an instance with one weekly window applies, the official client reads back its day, UTC start hour, one-hour duration and description, and no `maintenance_schedule` (nothing is scheduled); the plan is clean; a new day and hour change in place (`UpdateInstance`); destroy removes the instance. |

## Cloud Scheduler — `google.cloud.scheduler.v1`

**Built, not reused** (#302). Google publishes no Cloud Scheduler emulator. It runs in the CLI
process, as Cloud Tasks does, and is opt-in: `--services scheduler`, on `--port-scheduler`
(default `9008`). `env` exports `CLOUDBURROW_SCHEDULER_ENDPOINT`. No client library reads it, so
pass it to `option.WithEndpoint`. Per-method status is generated in
[coverage/scheduler.md](coverage/scheduler.md).

| Claim | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateJob`, `GetJob`, `ListJobs`, `PauseJob`, `ResumeJob`, `RunJob`, `DeleteJob` | **Verified** | `TestSchedulerHTTPAndPubSubJobs`, with `cloud.google.com/go/scheduler/apiv1` against the CI instance. |
| `RunJob` delivers at once to an HTTP target | **Verified** | The same test, against an `httptest` server. Deliveries carry `X-CloudScheduler`, `X-CloudScheduler-JobName` and `X-CloudScheduler-ScheduleTime`, and `User-Agent: Google-Cloud-Scheduler`. A 2xx response is success. HTTP targets are called from the host, so they must be reachable from it. |
| Pub/Sub targets | **Verified** | The same test: the job's data and attributes reach a subscription on the local emulator, published through the official client. A job whose topic does not exist fails its attempt, as on the real service. |
| Cron schedules in IANA time zones | **Verified** | Unit-tested through the official client with a fake clock. Unix-cron with five fields, ranges, steps and names. Zones come from Go's embedded tzdata, so they work on hosts with no zoneinfo. Invalid expressions and unknown zones are INVALID_ARGUMENT. |
| Paused jobs do not fire; resumed ones do | **Verified** | Unit-tested through the official client with a fake clock. Resuming restarts from the next slot; runs missed while paused are not made up. |
| Retries | **Verified** | Unit-tested: `retry_count` retries on the Cloud Tasks backoff schedule, fed from `min_backoff_duration`, `max_backoff_duration` and `max_doublings`, and bounded by `max_retry_duration`. The last attempt's outcome is in `status` and `last_attempt_time`. |
| `UpdateJob` | **Verified** | Unit-tested, and applied by Terraform's provider (`TestTerraformSchedulerAndSubscription`) and gcloud (`TestGcloudScheduler`) over JSON. An empty mask replaces every settable field; the mask paths are `description`, `schedule`, `time_zone`, the target, `retry_config` and `attempt_deadline`. Over JSON the mask is lowerCamelCase (`timeZone`), converted by the transcoder. **Refused as the contract refuses** (#795), on `CreateJob` and `UpdateJob`, each `INVALID_ARGUMENT`: a `time_zone` of `Local` (Go's name for the host's zone, not a tz database name), a `schedule` with a `TZ=` or `CRON_TZ=` prefix (the cron parser's extension, not unix-cron, which overrode `time_zone`; one with no space after it panicked in the parser), and an `http_target.body` on a method other than POST, PUT or PATCH ("It is an error to set body on a job with an incompatible HttpMethod"). Before, each was accepted (unit `TestSchedulerRefusesWhatTheContractRefuses`). An invalid cron expression and an unknown time zone were refused already. From the console: `TestConsoleSchedulerEditJob`. |
| `ResumeJob` on an enabled job | **Verified** | Succeeds and changes nothing (#591): the Terraform provider resumes every job it creates unpaused, and `TestTerraformSchedulerAndSubscription` reads such a job back ENABLED after apply. It was FAILED_PRECONDITION here, which failed every such apply. That Google accepts it is inferred from the provider, not measured against Google. |
| `retry_config` of a job given none | **Implemented** | Not returned, though the job retries by the defaults (#591): the provider plans clean against Google for such a job, which it could not if the defaults came back, and here they did, so every plan wanted to remove them. Inferred from the provider, not measured against Google. A job given a `retry_config` returns it, with the defaults filled in. |
| JSON API (REST) | **Verified** | **One port serves gRPC and JSON** (#591), as `cloudscheduler.googleapis.com` does: the shared `Transcoder` serves Google's `google.api.http` bindings of `google.cloud.scheduler.v1`, and the Locations bindings of `cloudscheduler_v1.yaml`, with the same `GRPCServer` gRPC registers. Every CloudScheduler method is transcoded, and the Locations mixin too (#1237); a path Google does not bind 404. The query policy is KMS's: an unknown parameter is INVALID_ARGUMENT. The official client's REST transport drives a job's lifecycle (unit `TestRESTJobLifecycleWithTheOfficialRESTClient`, `TestRESTWire`). Terraform (`TestTerraformSchedulerAndSubscription`) and gcloud (`TestGcloudScheduler`) use it. JSON requests appear in `/admin/events`; fault injection and the gRPC request log are not interposed on them. |
| Terraform `google_cloud_scheduler_job` | **Verified** | `TestTerraformSchedulerAndSubscription`, with egress blocked: a Pub/Sub job applies (a create, then the provider's `:resume`), plans clean, takes a change to its description and schedule (a PATCH) and `paused = true` (a `:pause`), plans clean and is destroyed, each step read back with the official gRPC client. `TestTerraformSchedulerHTTPTarget` (#1304): a paused job with an `http_target` (POST, a header, a body and an `oidc_token`) applies, reads back, plans clean, takes a URI and audience change in place, and is destroyed. The wrapper sets `cloud_scheduler_custom_endpoint`. |
| `gcloud scheduler jobs` | **Verified where gcloud is installed** | `TestGcloudScheduler`, through `gcloud-setup`'s `cloudscheduler` override: `create http`, `create pubsub`, `list`, `describe`, `update http`, `pause`, `resume`, `run` and `delete`, read back with the official gRPC client. **Pass `--location`**: without it gcloud looks for an App Engine app's region, which is not served, and fails. |
| `Locations.ListLocations`, `GetLocation` | **Verified** | `TestSchedulerLocations` (#1237), with the official client's Locations mixin over gRPC; unit `TestLocations` and `TestRESTWire` over JSON. The list is Google's Cloud Scheduler regions plus every location that holds one of the project's jobs (any well-formed location is accepted in a job's name), paged; `GetLocation` of a listed location answers it, any other is NOT_FOUND, a malformed name INVALID_ARGUMENT, and a `filter` UNIMPLEMENTED. Which fields Google sets on each Location (here `name`, `locationId`, `displayName`) is UNVERIFIED. From the console: the Create job form's Region is chosen from the list (`TestSchedulerCreateFormOffersListLocations`). |
| App Engine targets | **Unimplemented** | UNIMPLEMENTED, tested: there is no App Engine locally. |
| OAuth and OIDC tokens on HTTP targets | **Verified**, *locally minted* | `TestSchedulerJobTokens` (#1243), with the official client: `oidc_token` and `oauth_token` are kept and returned by `CreateJob` and `GetJob`, and `RunJob` delivers to a local HTTP target with `Authorization: Bearer` and a locally minted token, the ID token's audience being the URI when none is given and its signature checked against the instance's `/certs`. A token without `service_account_email` is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**. A seed's `httpTarget` takes `oidcToken` and `oauthToken` too. Minted as for Cloud Tasks, with the same differences from Google: see Cloud Tasks, `oidcToken` / `oauthToken`. Before #1243 both were refused `UNIMPLEMENTED`. |
| Durability | **Verified, measured** | Jobs follow `--mode`: a store under the state directory in persistent mode, memory in ephemeral mode. `/admin/reset` clears them. CI's restart probe (#596): `TestSchedulerRestartSetup` runs alone just before `stop` and leaves an enabled and a paused HTTP job, each with its own schedule and time zone. After `stop` and `up` in persistent mode, `TestSchedulerAcrossRestart` reads both back with their schedule, time zone, target and state; brought up again with `--mode ephemeral`, `GetJob` is **NOT_FOUND** for both. |
| `state save` / `state load` | **Verified** | `TestStateRestoresSchedulerJobs`, with the official client against the CI instance (#600). See [state snapshots](#state-snapshots). |
| Seeding | **Verified** | `TestSchedulerSeedIsReadBackByTheOfficialClient`: a `scheduler` section in a seed document creates HTTP and Pub/Sub jobs the official client reads back field for field, and one invalid job refuses the whole document, seeding none (#600). |
## Cloud Logging — `google.logging.v2`

**Built, not reused** (#304). Google publishes no Logging emulator. It runs in the CLI process
and is opt-in: `--services logging`, on `--port-logging` (default `9009`). `env` exports
`CLOUDBURROW_LOGGING_ENDPOINT` for `option.WithEndpoint`. Per-method status is generated in
[coverage/logging.md](coverage/logging.md).

| Claim | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `WriteLogEntries`, `ListLogEntries`, `ListLogs` | **Verified** | `TestLoggingWriteAndRead`, with `cloud.google.com/go/logging` and `logadmin` against the CI instance: structured entries are written, then read back with `logName` and `severity >= WARNING`. |
| API-written entries in the Logs Explorer | **Verified** | The same test finds them in the console's `/api/logs`, under the log's name and the project. Severities are folded onto the console's four levels. |
| Unsupported filters | **Verified** | INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the term, never a silent match: tested with `jsonPayload.event = "boot"`. |
| `DeleteLog` | **Verified** | Removes one log's entries. `TestGcloudLogging`: `gcloud logging logs delete` over JSON (#591). |
| The store | **Implemented** | Bounded at 20,000 entries (the oldest go first), in memory in every mode, cleared by `/admin/reset`. It keeps nothing across a restart. |
| `TailLogEntries`, `ListMonitoredResourceDescriptors` | **Verified** | Since #1215. TailLogEntries is a gRPC stream of entries written after it opens, for parent resource names (`projects/*`, and since #1395 `folders/*`, `organizations/*` and `billingAccounts/*`) and, since #1410, bucket views (`{bucket}/views/{view}`: the bucket's new entries the view's filter matches, `TestLoggingViewFiltersAndRetention`), with the ListLogEntries filter subset and `buffer_window` (default 2s, 0–60s); each response is ordered by timestamp. `suppression_info` is never set, since nothing is dropped. Over JSON (#1410), `POST /v2/entries:tail` takes one `TailLogEntriesRequest` body and streams a JSON array of `TailLogEntriesResponse`, opened at once and one element per send, until the client disconnects (unit `TestTailOverJSON`); the array framing is gRPC transcoding's for a streamed response and is UNVERIFIED, since no official client reads it (Go's apiv2 REST transport says TailLogEntries is not supported for REST). The console's Logs Explorer has its own live stream. ListMonitoredResourceDescriptors returns Google's `global` descriptor, the one resource type CloudBurrow emits, paged (`TestLoggingTailLogEntries`, `TestLoggingListMonitoredResourceDescriptors`). |
| Log-based metrics: `CreateLogMetric`, `GetLogMetric`, `ListLogMetrics`, `UpdateLogMetric`, `DeleteLogMetric` | **Verified** (error codes UNVERIFIED) | Since #1226, `MetricsServiceV2` in full. `TestLoggingLogBasedMetrics`, with the official `apiv2` `MetricsClient`: a counter with the default descriptor (DELTA, INT64, unit `1`, type `logging.googleapis.com/user/{id}`) and a distribution with a label extractor, a `REGEXP_EXTRACT` value extractor and explicit buckets are created, read back (a slash in an ID may be escaped, `nginx%2Frequests`), paged, updated (create_time kept, and UpdateLogMetric of an absent metric creates it, as the proto says), and deleted. As the proto documents: the ID is 1-100 of `A-Za-z0-9_-.,+!*',()%/`, not starting with `/`; `filter` is required (at most 20,000 characters) and `description` at most 8,000; `metric_kind` must be DELTA and `value_type` INT64 or DISTRIBUTION; a DISTRIBUTION needs `value_extractor` and valid `bucket_options` (linear, exponential or explicit) and a counter takes neither; an extractor is `EXTRACT(field)` or `REGEXP_EXTRACT(field, "regex")` with exactly one capture group; every descriptor label needs an extractor and every extractor a label; `bucket_name` must be a bucket of the metric's project; `metric_kind`, `value_type` and existing labels cannot change. Each is INVALID_ARGUMENT, a duplicate ALREADY_EXISTS and a missing metric NOT_FOUND; Google's message texts are not matched. **The filter is compiled with the ListLogEntries subset above**, so a filter outside it (`jsonPayload.x:y`, OR) is INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the term, where Google accepts it. Stored in the instance's state, so they survive a restart in persistent mode, and cleared by `/admin/reset`. |
| Log-based metric values | **Not supported** | Cloud Monitoring is not emulated, so a metric produces **no time series** and nothing can read one; `disabled` is stored and has nothing to stop. The console's metric page counts the stored entries its filter matches over the last hour and day instead, which is a count of entries, not a metric point. |
| Sinks: `CreateSink`, `GetSink`, `ListSinks`, `UpdateSink`, `DeleteSink` | **Verified** (error codes UNVERIFIED) | Since #1226. `TestLoggingSinks`, with the official `ConfigClient`. A project sink stores its destination, filter, description, `disabled`, embedded exclusions and `bigquery_options`. **Every destination is delivered to**: an enabled sink whose destination is `logging.googleapis.com/projects/[P]/locations/[L]/buckets/[B]` routes the entries its filter matches (less its embedded exclusions) there, readable through that bucket's views in ListLogEntries `resource_names` (#1395); a Cloud Storage bucket, Pub/Sub topic, BigQuery dataset or `logging.googleapis.com/projects/[P]` receives them as the next row says (#1404). The destination must have one of the documented forms (`storage.googleapis.com/[BUCKET]`, `bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/[P]/datasets/[D]`, `pubsub.googleapis.com/projects/[P]/topics/[T]`, `logging.googleapis.com/projects/[P]/locations/[L]/buckets/[B]`, `logging.googleapis.com/projects/[P]`), else INVALID_ARGUMENT; the ID is 1-100 letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, starting alphanumeric; the filter is compiled as above. UpdateSink changes only the `update_mask` paths, and an empty mask is `destination,filter,include_children`, as the proto documents; an output-only path is INVALID_ARGUMENT. `writer_identity` is set (#1404) to the parent's Logging service agent, `serviceAccount:service-[PROJECT]@gcp-sa-logging.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (a folder's `fld-[ID]`, an organization's `org-[ID]`, a billing account's `bac-[ID]`), with the project ID where Google has the project number, as `GetSettings` names it (#1292); `logging_config.proto` documents a service agent for `unique_writer_identity` and for every non-project sink, and the identity Google returns for a project sink created without `unique_writer_identity` (an older shared one) is UNVERIFIED: the service agent is returned for it too. Nothing is enforced on it (ADR-0004): a sink delivers whatever IAM grants it has. The built-in `_Default` and `_Required` sinks are not listed. |
| Sink delivery to Cloud Storage, Pub/Sub, BigQuery and another project | **Verified** (error codes UNVERIFIED) | Since #1404, to docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/storage, /export/pubsub, /export/bigquery and /export/troubleshoot. `TestLoggingSinksDeliverToTheirDestinations`: sinks made with the official `ConfigClient` deliver entries written with the official `Client`, read back with the official Pub/Sub, BigQuery and Storage clients. **Pub/Sub** (`pubsub.googleapis.com/projects/[P]/topics/[T]`): each entry is published at once as one message, its data the LogEntry JSON and its attribute `logging.googleapis.com/timestamp` the entry's timestamp; the `compute.googleapis.com/resource_type` and `resource_id` attributes of Google's example are not set (UNVERIFIED which resources Google adds them for). **BigQuery** (`bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/[P]/datasets/[D]`): each entry is streamed (`tabledata.insertAll`, its `insertId` the row's) into a table named for its log, every character but letters, digits and `_` made `_` (`apache-access` is `apache_access`), with `_YYYYMMDD` of its UTC timestamp, or, with `bigquery_options.use_partitioned_tables`, one table partitioned by day on the `timestamp` column; the columns keep the LogEntry field names (`logName`, `resource.type`, `resource.labels.*`, `textPayload`, `jsonPayload.*`, `timestamp`, `receiveTimestamp`, `severity`, `insertId`, `httpRequest.*`, `labels.*`, `operation.*`, `trace`, `spanId`, `traceSampled`, `sourceLocation.*`, `split.*`), the names users choose are lowercased with unsupported characters made `_`, a JSON string is `STRING`, a number `FLOAT`, a bool `BOOLEAN`, an object a `RECORD` and a list `REPEATED`; a top-level `@type` of `type.googleapis.com/abc.Xyz` names the payload column `jsonpayload_abc_xyz`. The first entry makes the schema and later ones add their new fields; an entry that would change a field's type is a schema mismatch. **Not implemented:** Google writes a mismatched entry to an `export_errors` table whose schema it does not document; here it is not written, and the sink records the error; `protoPayload` is not exported; the types of `httpRequest.latency` and of the other unlisted fields are UNVERIFIED and they are left out. **Cloud Storage** (`storage.googleapis.com/[BUCKET]`): entries are batched per hour, as Google writes them, into the objects `CopyLogEntries` writes (`LOG_ID/YYYY/MM/DD/HH:00:00_HH:59:59_S0.json`, LogEntry JSON one per line, `_A0:UNIX` for an entry received in another hour than its timestamp's); an hour's batch is written once the Logging clock passes the hour it was received in, checked every 30 seconds (Google: the first entries can take 2 to 3 hours). The CloudBurrow extension `POST /cloudburrow/logging/v2/clock:advance` with `{"seconds": n}` on the Logging port (n not negative; it answers `{"time": …}`) moves the Logging clock forward, for every entry written after it too, and writes the batches due by then before it answers; the clock does not move back until the instance restarts, and batches not yet written are lost with it. **Another project** (`logging.googleapis.com/projects/[P]`): the entry goes to P's `_Default` bucket, unless one of P's exclusions matches it, read by ListLogEntries of `projects/[P]`, and through P's own sinks, once: a project destination of P's sinks is not followed again (UNVERIFIED: Google documents rerouting, not its depth). **Errors**: a delivery that fails (a missing topic, dataset or bucket, a service the instance does not serve, a schema mismatch) drops the entry, is shown on the sink's console page, and writes, once a day per sink and error code as Google documents, an `ERROR` entry to the sink's parent's `logging.googleapis.com/sink_error` log: resource `logging_sink` (`name`, `destination`, `project_id`), labels `activity_type_name` `LoggingSinkConfigErrorV2`, `destination`, `error_code`, `error_detail` and `sink_id`, and the text `Cloud Logging sink configuration error in [P], sink [S]: [code] ([detail])`. `topic_not_found` is Google's code; `dataset_not_found`, `bucket_not_found`, `schema_mismatch` and `write_failed` are CloudBurrow's (UNVERIFIED). That entry is not routed by sinks. Delivery is in memory, and not across a restart. `TestGcloudLoggingSinksToEachDestination`: `gcloud logging sinks create` for each destination (`--use-partitioned-tables` for BigQuery), `describe` reading `writerIdentity`, and `gcloud logging write` arriving at the topic; `TestTerraformLoggingSinkDestinations`: below. These run in the emulators shard, beside BigQuery, as `SINK_LOGGING`, `SINK_STORAGE` and `SINK_PUBSUB`. Unit `TestSinkDelivery`, `TestTableNames`. |
| Exclusions: `CreateExclusion`, `GetExclusion`, `ListExclusions`, `UpdateExclusion`, `DeleteExclusion` | **Verified** (error codes UNVERIFIED) | Since #1226. `TestLoggingExclusions`, with the official `ConfigClient`. An enabled exclusion is applied as Google applies one to the `_Default` sink: a matching entry written after it is accepted and kept out of its own parent's `_Default` bucket, so ListLogEntries of that parent never returns it; disabled, it drops nothing. Since #1395 an excluded entry still reaches the sinks of the folders and organization above it, as Google documents (exclusions apply to the parent's own `_Default` sink). `filter` is required; `update_mask` is required by UpdateExclusion and may name `description`, `filter` and `disabled`. |
| Buckets and views: `ListBuckets`, `GetBucket`, `CreateBucket`, `UpdateBucket`, `DeleteBucket`, `UndeleteBucket`, `ListViews`, `GetView`, `CreateView`, `UpdateView`, `DeleteView` | **Verified** (refusal codes UNVERIFIED) | Since #1264. `TestLoggingBucketsAndViews`, with the official `ConfigClient`: every project lists `_Default` (30 days) and `_Required` (400 days, locked) in `global`, each with its `_AllLogs` view; `_Default`'s description and retention can be changed (as Terraform's `google_logging_project_bucket_config` does) and it cannot be deleted; `_Required` cannot be changed. A user bucket (an ID not starting with `_`, any location) is created, updated through a required `update_mask` (`description`, `retention_days`, `locked`, `restricted_fields`, `index_configs`, `analytics_enabled`), deleted into `DELETE_REQUESTED` (purged after 7 days, as Google documents) and undeleted. A locked bucket refuses a retention change, unlocking and deletion. Views are created, listed, updated (`description`, `filter`) and deleted. Refusals Google gives no code for are FAILED_PRECONDITION. Stored, durable in persistent mode. Since #1395 sinks route entries into user buckets, and since #1410 reads apply what a bucket and view say (`TestLoggingViewFiltersAndRetention` with the official `apiv2` Client, `TestGcloudLoggingReadView` with `gcloud logging read --bucket --view --location`): a view's `filter` keeps the bucket's entries it matches, with `SOURCE("…")` (the resource and, for a folder or organization, what Resource Manager holds under it), `LOG_ID("…")`, `NOT` on one term and the ListLogEntries grammar; a view filter outside that (`OR`, parentheses, regular expressions, `:`) is **UNIMPLEMENTED** when read, rather than shown unfiltered. A bucket's `retention_days` (`_Default`'s 30, `_Required`'s 400) leaves out entries whose timestamp is older than that before the Logging clock (`clock:advance`, #1404), on read and in a tail. Entries more than 30 days old when written are still dropped at write, whatever a bucket's retention (UNVERIFIED for a longer one). `cmek_settings` is UNIMPLEMENTED. In the console: the Logs Storage screen (#1264). |
| `CreateBucketAsync`, `UpdateBucketAsync` | **Verified** | `TestLoggingLinksSettingsAndAsyncBuckets` (#1292), official `ConfigClient`: each does what `CreateBucket` or `UpdateBucket` does and answers an Operation that is already done, with a `BucketMetadata` (state SUCCEEDED) and the bucket as its response, so the client's `Wait` returns at once. The Operations mixin serves copy operations alone (#1394), so a client that polls one of these by name gets NOT_FOUND. |
| Links (`CreateLink`, `GetLink`, `ListLinks`, `DeleteLink`) | **Verified**, *stored, no dataset made* | `TestLoggingLinksSettingsAndAsyncBuckets` (#1292), official `ConfigClient`; unit `TestSettingsAndLinksOverREST` with its REST transport. A link is stored under a bucket with Log Analytics on (`analytics_enabled`; without it CreateLink is FAILED_PRECONDITION, UNVERIFIED code), is ACTIVE, and names the BigQuery dataset `bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/{p}/datasets/{link_id with - as _}`, which is not made: BigQuery holds no copy of the bucket's entries. CreateLink and DeleteLink answer done Operations with a `LinkMetadata`; a second link of one ID is ALREADY_EXISTS, a missing one NOT_FOUND. From the console: the Linked datasets section, Create link and Delete link on a bucket's page, and Log Analytics in Edit bucket (`TestConsoleLoggingLinks`). |
| Settings and CMEK settings (`GetSettings`, `UpdateSettings`, `GetCmekSettings`, `UpdateCmekSettings`) | **Verified** | `TestLoggingLinksSettingsAndAsyncBuckets` (#1292); unit `TestSettingsAndLinksOverREST`. A project's `storage_location` and `disable_default_sink` are stored and read back (the defaults: none, and the default sink on; they change nothing that is written or read here); an empty update mask names both and `kms_key_name`. A `kms_key_name` is **UNIMPLEMENTED**, as a bucket's `cmek_settings` is. `kms_service_account_id` and the CMEK `service_account_id` are `service-{project}@gcp-sa-logging.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (UNVERIFIED: Google's use the project number). Since #1395 a folder's, organization's and billing account's settings are read, and an organization's stored (the Folder and organization parents row below). The JSON binding `{name=*/*}/settings` carries `projects/{p}` alone, which is accepted. In the console: the Logs Storage settings page, /logs/settings, with Edit settings (`TestConsoleLoggingSettings`, #1311). |
| `CopyLogEntries` | **Verified** | Since #1394. `TestLoggingCopyLogEntries`, with the official `ConfigClient` over gRPC and the official Storage client reading the result; `TestGcloudLoggingCopy` with `gcloud logging copy`, `gcloud logging operations describe` and `list`, for a project and, since #1411, with `--folder` and `--organization`; unit `TestCopyLogEntries` and `TestCopyLogEntriesFromBillingAccount` with the REST transport. The source is any parent's bucket, `{projects|folders|organizations|billingAccounts}/X/locations/L/buckets/B` (#1411, as `gcloud logging copy --folder|--organization|--billing-account` documents). The entries of the source bucket that `filter` matches, stored when the call is made, are written to `storage.googleapis.com/BUCKET` on the instance's Cloud Storage, named as a Cloud Storage sink names its objects: `LOG_ID/YYYY/MM/DD/HH:00:00_HH:59:59_S0.json` for the UTC hour of each entry's timestamp, `_A0:UNIX.json` (UNIX the copy's start) for entries received in another hour, each holding LogEntry JSON one per line in timestamp order. A bucket holds what it is read for: a parent's `_Default` its own entries (those no exclusion kept out) and what sinks routed there, and any other bucket, an aggregated sink's destination among them, what sinks routed to it. The long-running operation `{parent}/locations/L/operations/ID`, under the source's parent (`folders/F/locations/L/operations/ID`), carries a `CopyLogEntriesMetadata` (the request, start and end time, state SCHEDULED, RUNNING, then SUCCEEDED, FAILED or CANCELLED, progress 0-100, `cancellation_requested`, `writer_identity` the parent's Logging service agent, `serviceAccount:service-{project}@gcp-sa-logging.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, or `service-fld-{n}@`, `service-org-{n}@`, `service-bac-{account}@` for the others) and a `CopyLogEntriesResponse` with the copied count. Google's copy takes at least an hour; this one is SCHEDULED for 2 seconds, then writes one object at a time. `google.longrunning.Operations` is served for copy operations (`GetOperation`, `ListOperations` with no filter or `request_type=CopyLogEntries`, `CancelOperation`, over gRPC and at `logging_v2.yaml`'s project, organization, folder and billing-account paths over JSON): a cancel before the copy finishes stops it before its next object and ends it CANCELLED with the error CANCELLED, keeping what was written, as Google documents; cancelling a finished copy is FAILED_PRECONDITION (UNVERIFIED code). A write that fails, a missing destination bucket among them, ends it FAILED with PERMISSION_DENIED "Failed to write export data", the error Google's troubleshooting names. A destination other than a Cloud Storage bucket is INVALID_ARGUMENT, a missing source bucket NOT_FOUND, and an instance without Cloud Storage FAILED_PRECONDITION. Operations are kept in memory, not across a restart. The console's log bucket page offers Copy log entries, lists the bucket's copy operations and cancels one. |
