| Firestore documents that do not exist, and Datastore entity addresses, in the console | **Verified** | #875, in the emulators shard, read back through the official clients. **Firestore** (`TestConsoleFirestoreListsMissingDocumentsWithSubcollections`): a collection's page is read with `ListDocuments` and `show_missing` — the client's `CollectionRef.DocumentRefs` — rather than a query, so a document that does not exist but has a subcollection is listed as `DocumentRefs` lists it, in italics with *no fields — has subcollections*, and paging continues with the API's page token (a page token can be issued for a page that ends the collection, so the next page can be empty). Its page says it does not exist and its Collections tab opens its subcollections; **Add field** on it creates it (`Create`, so one written meanwhile is `ALREADY_EXISTS`), which the client reads back; **Delete document** on it says there is nothing to delete. The documents that exist are then read in one `BatchGetDocuments` for their fields. The query builder still runs a query, which, as in Firestore, does not return a missing document. **Datastore** (`TestConsoleDatastoreOpensARootEntityNamedLikeAKeyPath`, unit `TestDatastoreEntityAddressIsUnambiguous`): an entity's page is addressed by its key encoded as Google's console encodes it — the URL-safe base64 of the key's protocol buffer, the client's `Key.Encode` — so a root entity named `Customer/alice/Order/x` in kind `Order` and the child that path names each open their own page, and Add property on each changes that entity only; so do a root named `id=7` and the numeric id 7. The page is headed by the key as the listing names it, and Delete entity asks for that back. A link in the older form (a name, `id=N` or a key path) still opens what it did. The precedence when a segment is both (#882, unit `TestDatastoreEncodedKeyPrecedence`): it is an encoded key only when it is the canonical encoding — what `Key.Encode` writes, or that with the page's own project named — of a complete key with the page's namespace and kind and the default database; otherwise it is the older form, so another project's, namespace's or kind's key, a non-canonical encoding and an incomplete key are names here. The only older link this changes is a root entity whose name is itself such an encoding, and its row opens it by its own encoded key. The listing named a root entity by its name, so that root and that child shared a Key cell; since #882 a **Parent** column on a kind's entities and the query builder's results — *none (root entity)*, or the parent's key path, as Google's console lists an entity's parent — tells the rows apart (`TestConsoleDatastoreRowsNameTheirParent`, which also opens the child by its key with this project named and reads another project's key as a name no entity has; unit `TestDatastoreEntityRowsTellARootFromTheChild`). Since #885 entities are listed in a **Name/ID** column rendered as Google's console renders it — `name=…` for a name, `id=…` for a numeric ID — so a root named `id=7` (`name=id=7`) and the numeric ID 7 (`id=7`), which both have no parent and read the same before, differ in the list, in the query builder's results and in their pages' headings and breadcrumbs; key paths (the Parent column, Key path, a child's heading) use the same rendering, `Customer/name=alice/Order/id=7`, and Delete entity asks for the heading back. Create entity's Key identifier reads that rendering too, so `name=id=7` makes the name `id=7`. An older `/datastore/Order/id=7` link still opens the numeric ID 7 (`TestConsoleDatastoreNameIDTellsANameFromAnID`, unit `TestDatastoreNameIDTellsANameFromAnID`; in headless Chrome, `TestDatastoreNameIDColumnTellsANameFromAnID`). The Firestore screen's Documents count, and a Collections tab's, count the same `ListDocuments` list as the collection's page, so a document that does not exist but has subcollections is counted, and the lists' notes say so (`TestConsoleFirestoreCountsMissingDocuments`, #882). In headless Chrome (`test/browser`, emulators shard): `TestFirestoreMissingDocumentIsListedInItalics`, `TestDatastoreRootEntityNamedLikeAKeyPathOpens`, `TestFirestoreCollectionCountIncludesMissingDocuments` and `TestDatastoreKindListShowsEachRowsParent`. |
| **Cloud Tasks attempt history on a task's page** | **Not supported** | A task's page shows its attempt and response counts and last response code, not a history of attempts. |
| Deploy a Cloud Run service from the console | **Verified** | Through the **Cloud Run v2 adapter**, not by applying a Knative manifest — applying directly would let the console accept a configuration the API refuses, which is the console inventing support. The deploy **waits for readiness**: a service reported created and never ready is the failure the console exists to make visible. Verified end to end, including invoking the deployed service through the ingress. |
| Delete a Cloud Run service from the console | **Verified** | Through the same adapter, waiting for the operation. |
| Kubernetes pods, services, jobs and events | **Verified** | Scoped, **read-only**, across namespaces, each row showing whether CloudBurrow owns it. Events are what turn "the pod is Pending" into a reason. |
| Ownership shown per object | **Verified** | A developer can tell what CloudBurrow created from what they created. |
| **GKE cluster metadata** | **Not supported** | This is a kind cluster. No node pools, autopilot or release channels are presented, because presenting them would be fabricating exactly what the issue forbids. |
| **Creating Kubernetes workloads from manifests** | **Not supported** | Read-only by design: a console that could apply arbitrary manifests would create workloads CloudBurrow does not track and cannot clean up. |
| Logs Explorer, live | **Verified** | Real pod logs followed from the cluster, streamed over **Server-Sent Events** (#88). Verified in a real browser: 88 live rows, `live` state, pause control, severity filter. |
| Pause / resume with buffering | **Verified** | Resume shows what happened while paused rather than skipping it — the lines you paused to read are usually next to the ones you need. |
| Reconnect and resume | **Verified** | Every event carries an id; a reconnecting client sends `Last-Event-ID` and the **gap** is replayed rather than everything, which would make a reconnect look like a flood of new activity. |
| Filters: severity, source, resource, operation, text | **Verified** | Applied to both the backlog and the live stream. |
| **Credential redaction** | **Verified** | On the way **in**, not on the way out: an entry stored with a token in it has already been written somewhere a later change might expose. Covers `ya29.` and `cbl_` tokens, `Authorization`, api-key/password/secret/token assignments, PEM private keys and JWTs. Operation failure causes are redacted too. |
| Message truncation | **Verified** | 2 KiB, marked. An application logging a whole request body would otherwise push out everything that explains it. |
| Bounded retention | **Verified** | 2000 entries in memory. Nothing is persisted: keeping logs would make CloudBurrow responsible for data it never promised to keep. |
| **System namespaces are not followed** | **By design** | Measured: the control plane, kourier and Knative's own components were **90% of the buffer**, pushing out the lines that explain a developer's failure. Only `default` and the managed namespace are followed; the Events screen and `kubectl logs` still reach the rest. |
| Cloud Tasks attempt history | **Verified** | Each dispatch attempt is logged with its outcome. A queue that says "1 task" tells a developer nothing; the attempt says why it is still there. |
| Activity: operations with states and causes | **Verified** | PENDING / SUCCEEDED / FAILED from the **backend's verdict**, never from the console's optimism. A failed operation links to its own logs. |
| **Severity of container logs is inferred** | Partial | Container logs carry no structured severity, so it is a heuristic over the words applications conventionally use. Used for filtering, never to claim an application said something it did not. |
| **Billing, quota, SLA or cost metrics** | **Not supported** | Nothing of the kind is displayed. There is no billing here to report. |
| **Request-rate, latency and resource metrics** | **Partial** | **Cloud Tasks, Secret Manager, the Cloud Run v2 adapter, Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Logging, Resource Manager, Cloud Storage, Pub/Sub, Bigtable, Spanner, Firestore and Datastore**, the services CloudBurrow serves itself or fronts: every call is counted by service, method and canonical code, with a latency histogram, at `GET /metrics` on the loopback control port in the Prometheus text format (`TestCreateTaskCallsAreCounted`, which parses it with Prometheus's own parser). `/monitoring` charts request rate, error rate and p50/p95 latency per service. A service with no observer (Cloud SQL, Memorystore, BigQuery) is labelled not measured, never charted at zero. That set is derived from the services that registered a call observer, not kept by hand, so a measured service is never also reported unmeasured (`TestMetricsSchedulerAndLoggingAreMeasured`, #600). Cloud Run workloads' own requests need Knative's queue-proxy metrics, which are off (#181). Storage (#513): each request is counted and recorded in `/admin/events` by API method (`storage.objects.insert`, `xml.PUT`), with its bucket, object, status and duration, and never its query string or body, so no upload_id, token, signature or secret (`TestStorageEventsRecorded`, `TestStorageEventsRedactUploadIDs`, `TestMetricsStorageIsMeasured`). The server also keeps its last 1000 calls at `GET /_cloudburrow/events?after=N`, for the CLI to scrape from the in-cluster server (#514). Pub/Sub (#1266): the front before the emulator keeps its last 1000 calls, gRPC and REST, at `GET /_cloudburrow/calls?after=N`, with their method, the topic, subscription, snapshot or project the request names, the gRPC code or HTTP status, start, duration and `traceparent`, and never a payload; the CLI reads it through the tunnel every two seconds into `/metrics` (`GetTopic`, `JSON GET`), `/admin/events` and the console's request log, and with tracing on one span each. Every client is seen, the host's, a pod's and the storage server's notifications alike, since all reach the emulator through the front. `TestPubSubCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`, through the official `cloud.google.com/go/pubsub/v2` client: `CreateTopic`, `Publish` and a `NOT_FOUND` `GetTopic` are counted in `/metrics` and recorded in `/admin/events`, `/api/requests` and `/api/metrics/requests` with their code, resource and duration, no payload, and Pub/Sub is no longer unmeasured. Unit `TestCallLogRecordsGRPCAndREST`, `TestCallLogRecordsStreamingPull`, `TestPubSubCallsAreMeasured` (spans continue the client's trace), `TestPubSubCallsAfterAFrontRestart`. Bigtable (#1267): its front keeps the same call log (`internal/calllog`), so every client's calls are seen, the ones the front refuses `UNIMPLEMENTED` itself among them, which name no resource since they are answered unread (`TestBigtableCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`, unit `TestCallLogRecordsBigtableCalls`). Firestore and Datastore (#1267): the host tunnel's guard, which already reads each request's headers, tells the CLI each call's method, gRPC code (`grpc-status`) or HTTP status, duration, `traceparent` and the database or project its routing headers name (`google-cloud-resource-prefix`, `x-goog-request-params`); a pod's calls reached the Service directly and were not seen (`TestFirestoreCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`, unit `TestGuardObservesEachRequest`). Spanner, Firestore and Datastore (#1288): a call front (`internal/callfront`, `cloudburrow-storage call-front`) now serves each one's Service port in its pod, the emulator on the pod's loopback behind it, and passes every request through unread in the protocol it came in (gRPC over h2c with its streams and trailers, REST over HTTP/1.1), keeping the same call log as the Pub/Sub and Bigtable fronts from the routing headers and the outcome; the host tunnel's guard no longer records, so no call is counted twice. Every client is seen: Spanner's, whose raw tunnel nothing read before, and a pod's. `TestSpannerCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`, through the official `cloud.google.com/go/spanner` client from the host: `CreateDatabase`, `Commit` on its database and a failed `ExecuteStreamingSql` are in `/admin/events` with their code and duration and in `/metrics`, and Spanner is no longer unmeasured; `TestAPodsFirestoreCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`: a one-off pod's `Commit` and `BatchGetDocuments`, with the official Firestore client at `firestore.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:8080`, are recorded with its project's database. The front adds about 0.1 ms to a unary call (median of 300 `GetTopic` calls to an in-memory gRPC server, 138 µs through it against 40 µs direct, `TestGRPCPassesThroughAndAddedLatency`); unit `TestRESTPassesThroughAndIsLogged`, `TestReadinessFollowsTheEmulator`, `TestCallFrontCallsAreMeasured`. `/monitoring` charts each one's request rate, error rate and latency, and each in-cluster emulator pod's container CPU and memory from the kubelet's per-pod readings (`TestFirestoreOnMonitoringChartsItsCallsAndContainer`, `TestSpannerOnMonitoringChartsItsCalls`). |
| **Traffic splitting** | **Verified** | A Cloud Run service's page shows where its traffic goes, with each tag and its URL, and **Manage traffic** sets splits, pinned revisions and tags through `UpdateService` (#1224, `TestCloudRunManageTrafficThroughTheBrowser`). |
| Pagination | **Verified** | Tables page, with rows per page and a range out of the filtered total (`TestTablesPaginate`). Cloud SQL, Firestore, Datastore and Bigtable listings continue past their first page with a cursor, and a cursor the provider did not issue is refused rather than read as the end (`TestEveryPagedListingRefusesACursorItDidNotIssue`). |
| **Bucket listing is not scoped by project** | **Inherited limitation** | The storage backend accepts the project parameter and returns every bucket. The screen **says so** rather than presenting the rows under a project heading. |
| Console walkthrough on a fresh stack | **Verified** | [console-verification.md](console-verification.md): the walkthrough is now `test/browser`, run in headless Chrome against the compat storage shard's instance in CI (#594): landmarks and the LOCAL badge, the theme switch, a bucket created through the form, the error card under an injected fault, a row opened by keyboard, and no request off loopback; since #700 also the four viewport widths, dialog focus and Escape, and the Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler, Subscriptions and Cloud Run edit screens, the KMS and Run tests against the run shard's instance. Focus indicators and colour contrast are no longer walkthrough claims: `TestOutlineSuppressionHasAFocusVisibleRule` and `TestTokensMeetContrast` assert them from the stylesheet. |
| Form validation actually runs in a browser | **Verified** | It did **not** before this walkthrough. An HTML `pattern` is compiled with the RegExp `v` flag, where a literal `-` in a character class must be escaped; an unescaped one makes the pattern invalid and the browser then **silently skips validation**. Every create form had shipped that way. A regression test now compiles each shipped pattern under the `v` rule, and `TestCreateBucketThroughTheForm` (`test/browser`) submits a name the bucket pattern rejects in headless Chrome and asserts nothing is sent before creating a valid bucket through the same form; with the `-` unescaped it fails (#594). The regression test covered only the first four products' forms, so the Cloud KMS key ring and key, Cloud Scheduler job and Secret Manager secret patterns shipped the same way; `TestKMSCreateKeyRingThroughTheForm` found the first in Chrome's error log, and the unit test now reads every product's create form (#700). |
| Subscription creation from the UI | **Verified** | From a topic's page; see the Pub/Sub actions row above (`TestConsolePubSubActions`). |
| Visual regression against reference fixtures | **Not possible today** | No reference screenshots exist, so there is nothing to diff against — a threshold measured against our own output would only prove the console still looks like itself. This is what keeps visual fidelity at `Partial`. |
| Model catalogue screen | **Verified** | Shows the real catalogue with publisher, access, modality, licence, runtime and a **per-model** reason it is unavailable — the reasons differ, and one blanket message would hide that. |
| Generation playground | **Verified** | Offered only when local AI is configured, and relayed to the same API path the SDK calls (`TestPlaygroundGeneratesThroughTheRealAPIPath`); see [Console playground](#console-playground). An embedding playground is **not implemented** ([playground.md](playground.md) §7); custom prediction requests are the Online prediction page ([playground.md](playground.md) §8). |
| Gemma results labelled as Gemini | **Cannot occur** | The playground shows the model and its publisher, and says, where the output appears, that a community conversion's output is not a Gemini result (`TestPlaygroundReportsReadinessFromALiveProbe`). |

**Visual fidelity and API compatibility are separate claims with separate evidence**, and
neither implies the other. A screen that renders correctly proves nothing about the API
behind it, and a verified API proves nothing about the screen.

## Cross-cutting

| Concern | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Google-style error bodies and gRPC status codes | **Verified** | `internal/apierror`: one cause renders a consistent gRPC code and HTTP status, plus the JSON envelope a Google client parses. Used by Cloud Tasks, Secret Manager, Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Logging, Resource Manager, Cloud Storage and the Cloud Run v2 adapter. |
| Pagination with deterministic ordering | **Verified** | `internal/paging`: full-walk coverage proves no duplicates or gaps; invalid and cross-listing tokens are rejected. Used by the list methods of Cloud Tasks, Secret Manager, Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Logging, Resource Manager and the Cloud Run v2 adapter. |
| Long-running operations | **Verified** | `internal/lro`: pending, succeeded and failed are all reachable and terminal states are final. Used by the Cloud Run v2 adapter's operations. |
| Project isolation | **Verified** | `TestPubSubProjectIsolation`; `internal/resource` makes it structural — identical IDs in different projects or locations produce different keys by construction. |
| REST and gRPC transport | **Verified** | `internal/transport`: unknown REST paths return a Google 404 envelope and unknown gRPC methods return `Unimplemented`; request sizes are bounded and unknown JSON fields rejected. Cloud Tasks, Secret Manager, Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Logging, Resource Manager and the Cloud Run v2 adapter are served on it. |
| Background workers registered after startup | **Verified** | A worker registered after `Start` used to sit in the list and never run, because `Start` snapshotted the list once. **Cloud Tasks dispatch was wired into `up` and never dispatched anything.** Found while building the Logs Explorer: a deliberately failing task showed `dispatches=0` after minutes. Now started immediately, sharing the coordinator's lifetime. |
| Scheduling, retry and backoff over an injected clock | **Verified** | `internal/sched`: retry timing is proven by advancing virtual time, never by sleeping. Concurrent duplicate attempts are prevented, and shutdown drains in-flight work. |
| Metadata storage, memory and durable modes | **Verified** | `internal/store`: both modes share one test body; durable state survives restart, a second instance is refused, a failed commit leaves state unchanged, and unsafe keys are rejected. |
| Resource-name parsing and traversal safety | **Verified** | `internal/resource` rejects `..`, encoded separators, NUL and path separators in IDs. |
| Installation and release packaging | Partial | `docs/install.md`, `docs/status.md` and a release workflow that builds and checksums four platforms. v0.1.0 was published by it. The post-publish smoke install (#603) was added after v0.1.0 and has not run on a release yet. |
| Reset / seed / event inspection | Partial | `internal/admin`, served on the loopback-only control port and refused on service ports. **Reset covers Cloud Tasks, Cloud Storage (buckets, objects and notification configurations), Pub/Sub, Secret Manager, Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler (jobs), Cloud Logging (entries, and since #1226 log-based metrics, sinks and exclusions) and Resource Manager's IAM policies (on projects, folders and the organization, #1368; the projects and folders themselves are kept, since the other services' state is scoped by them)**, and Cloud SQL for MySQL's databases when it is enabled, narrowable with `service=` and `project=`. Measured 2026-10-16 on an instance of the default services less Cloud Run, plus Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler and Cloud Logging: `POST /admin/reset` answered `{"reset":["tasks","storage","pubsub","scheduler","logging","kms","secretmanager","resourcemanager"]}`, and afterwards the official clients found the topic, the secret and the Scheduler job `NOT_FOUND`, no entry of the log written, and no binding of the project's IAM policy set through v1 `setIamPolicy`, while a project created through v1 was still there; an unknown `service=` is 400 naming these (MySQL's reset was not measured) (`TestAProjectResetClearsOnlyThatProject`). Storage buckets record their project (#510), so a project-scoped reset clears that project's buckets only (`TestAProjectResetIncludingStorage`). The storage server's reset clears its store directly: live, noncurrent and soft-deleted objects, soft-deleted buckets, upload sessions, rewrite tokens, notification configurations and undelivered events, multipart uploads, IAM policies and HMAC keys, with no API delete and so no soft delete or notification (`TestAStorageResetEmptiesEveryBucketOnBuiltin`, `TestAStorageProjectResetOnBuiltin`). A Pub/Sub reset deletes a project's subscriptions, snapshots, topics and, since #889, schemas (`TestPubSubResetDeletesSchemas`: a schema is `NOT_FOUND` after its project's reset, its ID can be created again, and another project's schema is kept; unit `TestPubSubResetDeletesSchemas`). Pub/Sub state in a project CloudBurrow has never seen survives a full reset. **Seed covers Cloud Tasks, Cloud Storage, Pub/Sub, Secret Manager and Cloud Scheduler** from one document validated whole before anything is created (`TestOneSeedDocumentIsReadBackByTheOfficialSDKs`, `TestAnInvalidSeedDocumentSeedsNothing`, `TestSchedulerSeedIsReadBackByTheOfficialClient`). Pub/Sub fields the emulator is not known to honour are refused by name. Pub/Sub **schemas** (Avro only) and a topic's **`schemaSettings`** are seeded since #890: `TestPubSubSeedSchemaAndBoundTopic` seeds a schema and a topic bound to it, both read back by the official clients, a conforming message is published and a non-conforming one refused `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, a repeat is a 409 and `ifNotExists` skips it, and a `PROTOCOL_BUFFER` schema is refused with 400 before anything is seeded (unit `TestPubSubSeedCreatesSchemasAndBindsTopics`, `TestPubSubSeedValidatesSchemasFirst`). A subscription's **`expirationPolicy`, `messageRetentionDuration` and `retainAckedMessages`** are seeded since #899: `TestPubSubSeedExpirationAndRetention` seeds a 1-day ttl with a 1-hour retention and acknowledged messages kept, and a policy without a ttl, each read back by the official client; the 1-day one is gone 25 hours on by the front's clock and the other kept; a 12-hour ttl, and a 1-day ttl under the default 7-day retention, are refused 400 before anything is seeded, by the front's own check (unit `TestPubSubSeedSetsExpirationAndRetention`). Bucket labels, location and storage class are seeded and kept (`TestStorageSeedAcceptsLabels`, #503). **Events record every API call on the ports CloudBurrow serves itself** — Cloud Tasks (gRPC and JSON, #591), Secret Manager (gRPC and JSON), the Cloud Run v2 adapter (gRPC and JSON, #591), Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler and Cloud Logging (gRPC and JSON, #591), and Cloud Storage, whose calls the CLI scrapes from the in-cluster server (#513, #514) — with method, resource, project, canonical status code and duration, and never a payload or query string (`TestSecretManagerCallsAreRecordedWithoutTheirPayloads`). **Pub/Sub, Bigtable, Spanner, Firestore and Datastore are recorded too**, from the front in each emulator's pod, which every client's call passes through and which the CLI scrapes the same way (Pub/Sub #1266, Bigtable #1267, the others' call fronts #1288): measured 2026-10-16, the official Pub/Sub client's `CreateTopic` and `Publish` were in `/admin/events?service=pubsub` within the scrape's 2 s, with code, duration, project and topic (`TestFaultsPubSubIsRefusedForWhereItRuns`; `TestFirestoreCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`, `TestBigtableCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`, `TestSpannerCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`; Datastore's front is scraped the same way, and no test reads its events). **BigQuery, Cloud SQL and Memorystore are not recorded**: no call observer is registered for them. |
| Go SDK compatibility harness | **Verified** | `test/compat`. Refuses non-loopback endpoints and fails outright if cloud credentials are present in the environment. |
| Local cluster lifecycle (up/status/stop/reset/delete) | **Verified** | `internal/cluster` integration tests. |
| Workstation preflight (`cloudburrow doctor`) | **Verified** | `internal/doctor`: binaries, daemon reachability, memory, CPUs, disk and every port `up` would bind, each with a remedy. Only genuine blockers exit non-zero; an unmeasurable check reports `unknown`, never `ok`. On macOS, and on Linux when the daemon is in a VM (Docker Desktop for Linux), the disk figure is the host volume backing the VM disk, and says so. It names the container engine from `docker info` and warns on rootless and non-Desktop VM engines ([install.md](install.md#container-engines), #712). Windows is not built ([install.md](install.md#prerequisites)). |
| Diagnostics bundle (`cloudburrow diagnose`) | **Verified** | `test/compat/diagnose_test.go` creates a secret with a known payload, runs `diagnose` against the CI instance and searches every file of the bundle for that payload, the ADC fixture's private key and the kubeconfig's client key; none may appear. A stopped instance is covered by a unit test. Redaction is pattern-based (`console.Redact`) plus removal of pod env values; a credential an application logs in a form those patterns do not recognise is not caught, so read a bundle before sharing it. |
| Cluster ownership isolation | **Verified** | Prefix enforced at construction and re-checked on delete; namespace reset requires `cloudburrow.dev/owned=true`. |
| Python SDK compatibility harness | **Verified** | `test/compat-python`: pytest against the official Python clients, pinned by hash in `requirements.lock`, run by `make compat-python` in compat CI. See [Python client libraries](#python-client-libraries). |
| Node.js SDK compatibility harness | **Verified** | `test/compat-node`: `node:test` against the official Node clients, pinned with integrity hashes in `package-lock.json`, run by `make compat-node` in compat CI's `storage` and `emulators` shards, where every test passed with none skipped (#589). See [Node.js client libraries](#nodejs-client-libraries). |
| Java SDK support | Untested, no plan | No Java test exists and none is planned (#718), so CloudBurrow makes no Java claim; [status.md](status.md) lists Java as Untested. The endpoint each Java client needs has not been checked against client source, so none is documented. |
